docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
rgctl is a small Go command-line tool that answers two operator questions repo-guardian itself cannot answer once it is switched off: which pull requests did repo-guardian leave open in this org or repository, and what did its v1 policy file say. It reads a v1 guardian.hcl, lists the orgs, rules, reconcilers and PR templates it declares, scans an org or a repository for open pull requests authored by the App on repo-guardian/* branches, prints them with their links, records them as JSON, and on request closes them with a pointer comment.

It lives outside the engine on purpose, as its own Go module under tools/. Turning v1 off in an org leaves its pull requests open, and v2 does not reap them: the controls model opens one branch per control and ends the frozen-identity adoption that let v1 and v2 recognise each other's PRs (DESIGN-0032 D4, D27). The cutover runbook already needs this tool twice, to record every open repo-guardian PR before anything closes it (step 3) and to close v1's PRs with a pointer comment after the new release is up (step 6). The v1 packages that know how those PRs were made are scheduled for deletion, so the tool depends on none of them: it talks to GitHub through go-github and reads HCL through hclparse, and a lint rule keeps it that way.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Inventory open repo-guardian PRs for one repository, one org, or every org a v1 policy names, with repository, number, branch, title, age, URL and whether a human has pushed to the branch.
  • Record and close. Write the inventory as JSON, and close exactly the recorded PRs with a pointer comment, idempotently, with a dry run as the default.
  • Show what a v1 policy says without the v1 loader: orgs, guardian {} knobs, rules by kind with paths and check mode, reconcilers, PR templates.
  • Outlive v1. Its own Go module under tools/, no requirement on the parent module, no import of internal/, no database. The binary installs from any tag or from main and keeps building after v2 fast-forwards main.
  • Be safe to point at production. Act only on PRs authored by the configured App login, never on a PR a human has pushed to unless asked, never on a branch that is not repo-guardian/*.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Evaluating or remediating anything. rgctl never creates a PR, never commits, never edits policy.
  • Reading or writing repo-guardian's database. The record is a file, not a table.
  • Replacing repo-guardian evaluate or policy validate. config show describes a v1 file; it does not validate it against the v1 schema.
  • Managing GitHub App installations, secrets or webhooks.
  • Closing PRs from other tools. The author and branch rules are deliberately narrow.
  • An interactive terminal UI. A bubbletea front end for interactive searches is attractive, and deferred to v2, where it can run against the API instead of against GitHub directly (D12).

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
How a v1 PR is recognisable. v1 opens PRs from an installation token, so GitHub records the author as the App's bot account, <app slug>[bot]. The head branch is one of three fixed names pinned by TestPRIdentity_IsFrozen: repo-guardian/add-missing-files (the engine, title chore: add missing repo configuration files), repo-guardian/add-catalog-info (chore: add catalog-info.yaml) and repo-guardian/set-custom-properties (chore: set repository custom properties). Titles and bodies are operator-templated since IMPL-0012, so they are not identity. The sticky reconcile-log comment carries the marker <!-- repo-guardian:reconcile-log:v1 --> on its first line, which is a strong confirmation but absent on PRs that never had a second reconcile. The controls model keeps the repo-guardian/ prefix with one branch per control (repo-guardian/<control slug>), so the same two facts, App author plus branch prefix, identify repo-guardian PRs on both lines.

Why v2 will not clean up after v1. On the current v2 line the frozen literals let the two engines adopt each other's PRs. DESIGN-0032 ends that: per-control branches, a tracked-PR model keyed by the Remediation App's own login, a fresh database at cutover with no in-place upgrade path (D27). Its runbook step 3 records every open repo-guardian PR from GitHub so a write whose record was lost is found by exact identity, and step 6 closes v1's PRs with a comment pointing at the per-control PRs, adopting any PR a human has edited instead of closing it. Both steps are this tool.

What GitHub search can do. The issues-and-pull-requests search accepts is:pr is:open org:<org> author:app/<slug> head:<branch>; author:app/ selects an integration account, and head: matches branch names beginning with the given text, so head:repo-guardian/ selects every repo-guardian branch in one query per org. Search is limited to 30 requests per minute, returns at most 1000 results per query in pages of 100, and may return incomplete_results = true on timeout. A search hit is an index entry, not the PR: before anything acts on it the tool reads the PR itself.

Precedent in this repository. cmd/rg-burst is a side binary in cmd/ with its own build tag, inside the product module; there is no nested module yet. .golangci.yml on the v2 line uses depguard three times to keep packages apart (workflow code may not import the engine, the API may not import the GitHub client); main has no depguard configuration yet. cmd/repo-guardian parses flags with the standard library and dispatches subcommands by hand; the maintainer's standard for new tools is cobra. internal/github/client_test.go mocks the GitHub API with httptest.Server.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph tool["tools/rgctl, its own Go module (never requires the parent module)"]
        main["main.go: flags, dispatch, exit codes"]
        cfg["internal/v1config: loose HCL decode"]
        gh["internal/ghapi: App or token auth, search, verify, close"]
        prs["internal/prs: identity rule, classification, record file"]
        main --> cfg
        main --> prs
        prs --> gh
    end
    hcl["guardian.hcl"] --> cfg
    gh --> api["GitHub REST: search, pulls, issues, git refs, apps"]
    prs --> rec["open-prs.json"]
    rec --> prs
    lint["module boundary: tools/rgctl/go.mod has no require on the parent, plus depguard"] -.-> tool

tools/rgctl is a separate Go module (module github.com/donaldgifford/repo-guardian/tools/rgctl) with its own go.mod, so it has its own dependency set and none of them enter the product's go.mod: go-github v68, ghinstallation v2, hcl v2, spf13/cobra (D7) and charmbracelet/log (D15). A directory under the repository's import-path prefix could still import internal/ (Go's internal rule is by path prefix, not by module), which is why the guard is the module boundary: the tool's go.mod never requires github.com/donaldgifford/repo-guardian, so an internal/ import fails to resolve at all, and a depguard rule in the tool's own lint run says why. tools/rgctl/internal/... is importable only from under tools/rgctl, so the tool's packages are private to it.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command What it does rgctl config show <guardian.hcl> prints the orgs in scope, the guardian {} knobs, every rule by kind with its paths, check mode and reconcilers, ignore patterns and defaults.pr; --format json for scripting rgctl prs list finds open repo-guardian PRs in --repo org/name, --org org, or every org of --config guardian.hcl; table by default, --format json writes the record rgctl prs close closes the PRs in --from open-prs.json, or the result of the same selection flags as list; dry run unless --yes; comment, then close, then optionally delete the branch rgctl version build info

Selection flags shared by list and close:

Flag Meaning Default --repo org/name one repository, listed through the Pull Requests API --org org one org, through search then verification --config path every org in the file's scope { orgs }; without a scope block the installations of the App, since legacy mode applies to every installed org --branch name restrict to one head branch, repeatable; default is the prefix repo-guardian/ prefix --exhaustive list every repository and its open PRs instead of searching, for the final cutover pass or when search reports incomplete results off --force also close PRs with commits by someone other than the App; their branch is still never deleted off --format table \| json output table

Auth flags, read from flags or environment, never from positional arguments:

Flag Env Meaning --app-id RGCTL_APP_ID the GitHub App id; with the key, installation tokens are minted per org --private-key-file RGCTL_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE path to the App's PEM; the value is a path, the key is never a flag --token is not a flag GH_TOKEN a personal or fine-grained token for an operator; then --bot-login names the App account to match --bot-login RGCTL_BOT_LOGIN <slug>[bot]; discovered from GET /app under App auth, required under token auth --github-host RGCTL_GITHUB_HOST GitHub Enterprise Server base URL, default github.com

docs.title: Identity rule
docs.text:
A pull request is repo-guardian's when, read from the Pull Requests API, all of these hold:

  1. it is open;
  2. its author login equals the configured bot login (<slug>[bot]), compared case-insensitively;
  3. its head branch starts with repo-guardian/ (or equals one of the --branch names);
  4. its head repository is the repository itself, not a fork.

The reconcile-log marker on a comment is reported when present (reconcile_log: true) but is not required, because a PR that was reconciled once has no comment. Title is never used. A PR is edited when any commit on it has an author or committer login other than the bot, or a commit whose GitHub author is unresolved and whose committer is not the bot. The committer web-flow is never counted: GitHub records every Contents API write with that committer, so it is on the App's own commits, and a human editing in the web UI is still the author (found by the IMPL-0027 homelab smoke, where all 21 PRs read as edited until this was added); the tool lists commits until it finds the first such commit, so the cost is one page for a clean PR.

docs.title: Finding PRs
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    sel["selection: repo, org, or orgs from config"] --> mode{"mode"}
    mode -- "repo" --> pulls["GET pulls state=open per page"]
    mode -- "org, default" --> search["search: is:pr is:open org:X author:app/slug head:repo-guardian/"]
    mode -- "org, exhaustive" --> repos["list repositories: installation repos under App auth, org repos under token auth"]
    repos --> pulls
    search --> incomplete{"incomplete_results or 1000 hits"}
    incomplete -- "yes" --> warn["warn and suggest --exhaustive, continue"]
    incomplete -- "no" --> verify
    warn --> verify["GET pulls/number for every hit"]
    pulls --> rule
    verify --> rule{"identity rule"}
    rule -- "not ours" --> drop["drop, counted in summary"]
    rule -- "ours" --> edited{"commits by anyone but the bot"}
    edited -- "yes" --> e["record as edited"]
    edited -- "no" --> c["record as clean"]
    e --> out["table or JSON record"]
    c --> out

Search is the default for an org because it is one request per page of 100 PRs rather than one per repository, which matters at twenty-plus orgs. Every hit is then read through the Pull Requests API, so the index can only add work, never a wrong action: a stale hit for a PR that has since closed is dropped at verification. The two search limits are surfaced, not hidden: incomplete_results and a 1000th hit both produce a warning naming --exhaustive, and the summary line says how many hits were verified, dropped, clean and edited. The 30-per-minute search budget is respected by pacing search calls, and both auth modes use go-github's rate-limit handling for the core API.

--exhaustive lists repositories, through the installation's repository list under App auth (which is also the set v1 could see) or the org's repository list under token auth, and reads each repository's open PRs. It is the authoritative pass for the cutover and the fallback when search is incomplete.

docs.title: Closing PRs
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Selected
    Selected --> Skipped: not ours, or edited without --force
    Selected --> Planned: ours
    Planned --> Planned: dry run, printed
    Planned --> Commented: --yes, POST comment
    Commented --> Closed: PATCH state=closed
    Closed --> BranchDeleted: --delete-branch
    Closed --> [*]
    BranchDeleted --> [*]
    Planned --> Skipped: already closed when re-read

prs close re-reads every PR immediately before acting, so a record from prs list that has gone stale is handled rather than trusted: a PR closed by a human in the meantime is reported as already closed and skipped. The order is comment, then close, then branch, so a failure leaves a PR that still explains itself. Each step is idempotent on re-run: a comment whose first line is the tool's marker <!-- rgctl:closed-by-migration:v1 --> is not posted twice, a closed PR is not closed again, a missing branch is not an error. The default comment names the tool and the date and says the repository is now managed by the per-control PRs of repo-guardian v2; --comment replaces it. The branch is deleted only with --delete-branch, and never for an edited PR even with --force, because a human's commits are on it.

--from open-prs.json is the cutover shape: the record written by step 3 is the only input to step 6, so the close pass acts on exact identities rather than on a fresh search that might see a different set.

docs.title: Reading a v1 policy
docs.text:
config show decodes the file with hclparse and a body schema that names what it understands, locals, guardian, ignore, scope, defaults and rule <type> <name>, using PartialContent so a block or attribute it does not know is listed under unrecognised rather than failing. Attribute values are rendered as their source text, not evaluated: there is no evaluation context, locals are shown as declared, and a file() or interpolation is shown verbatim. The output is structured as:

Section Content orgs scope.orgs, or "every installed org (legacy mode)" when there is no scope block guardian every attribute of guardian {} as written, so a dry_run = true or auto_close_pr = false is visible rules one row per rule: type, name, enabled, paths, check mode, template, scope, ignore patterns, when gate, reconcilers with their types and watch pr defaults.pr and any per-rule or per-reconciler pr block, title and body as source text, labels ignore global patterns unrecognised anything the schema did not name, with its source location

This is deliberately a reader, not a loader. The v1 loader's strict decode, merge order, env overrides and validation stay in internal/policy and are not reproduced; when they are deleted the reader keeps working because it never depended on them.

docs.title: Logging and output
docs.text: Human-facing output is a log/slog logger backed by charmbracelet/log's handler: levelled, timestamped, coloured when stdout is a terminal, plain when it is not or when NO_COLOR or --no-color is set, --log-level for verbosity (D15). Progress lines ("org acme: 3 pages, 212 hits, 209 verified, 3 dropped") and every planned or performed action are logged, so a dry run reads as a plan and a --yes run reads as a journal. The table and the log both go to stdout. The one exception is the JSON record: when --format json writes to stdout rather than to --out <path>, the log moves to stderr for that run so the record stays parseable with a plain redirect.

docs.title: Output and exit codes
docs.text: The table is for a person; --format json is the record, written to --out <path> or to stdout. Exit codes follow the convention the controls CLI adopts (DESIGN-0033 AR-0033-07): 0 nothing found or every planned action done, 1 open repo-guardian PRs found (list) or PRs skipped as edited (close), 2 usage or configuration error, 3 operational failure (auth, rate limit exhausted, API error). A runbook can therefore gate on rgctl prs list --org X; test $? -eq 0.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
• Nothing is written without --yes, and nothing is ever written by list or config show.
  • No PR is touched whose author is not the configured bot login, whatever its branch.
  • No PR with a human commit is touched without --force, and its branch is never deleted.
  • Every write is preceded by a fresh read of the PR.
  • The tool never holds a database connection, never reads repo-guardian's own config env vars, and imports nothing under internal/.

docs.title: API / Interface Changes
docs.text:
• New binary rgctl from tools/rgctl, with tools/rgctl/internal/{v1config,ghapi,prs} as its private packages.
  • Module. tools/rgctl/go.mod with its own dependencies; the product's go.mod is untouched. The module never requires the parent module, which is asserted by make lint-rgctl (a grep on go.mod for the parent path fails the build) and by a depguard rule in the tool's own .golangci.yml denying github.com/donaldgifford/repo-guardian/internal, probed once with a deliberate bad import.
  • Make. build-rgctl, lint-rgctl and test-rgctl run inside the module directory; make lint, make test and make ci include them, since go test ./... from the root does not descend into a nested module. Renovate picks up the second go.mod on its own.
  • Install. No goreleaser entry on this line: go install github.com/donaldgifford/repo-guardian/tools/rgctl@main (or a tools/rgctl/vX.Y.Z tag if one is ever cut) (D13). When it becomes first-class in v2 it moves into the product module and gets a builds: entry (the package directory, never a file).
  • CI. The go paths filter (**/*.go, go.mod) already matches the module's files; the Make targets above are what put it in the existing jobs.
  • Docs. docs/operations/rgctl.md with the three commands and the cutover usage; DESIGN-0032's runbook steps 3 and 6 gain a pointer to this tool.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
There is no database. The record file written by prs list --format json and read by prs close --from is:

Field Type Meaning schema_version int 1 generated_at RFC 3339 when the list ran selection object the flags that produced it: repo, org, config path, branches, exhaustive bot_login string the App login matched prs[].repository string org/name prs[].number int PR number prs[].url string HTML URL prs[].head_branch string head ref prs[].head_sha string head at listing time, compared at close time and reported if moved prs[].title string as seen prs[].created_at, prs[].updated_at RFC 3339 from the PR prs[].edited bool a commit by someone other than the bot prs[].edited_by []string the logins found, when edited prs[].reconcile_log bool the v1 sticky comment marker was present summary object hits, verified, dropped, clean, edited, incomplete

prs close writes the same shape plus a result per PR: planned, commented, closed, branch_deleted, already_closed, skipped_edited, skipped_not_ours, error with a message.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• GitHub API mocks with httptest.Server, the pattern of internal/github/client_test.go, covering: search pages and a 1000th hit, incomplete_results, a stale hit that verifies as closed, a hit whose author is not the bot, a fork head, a PR with a human commit on page two, close idempotency (marker comment present, PR already closed, branch already gone), and the comment-close-delete order under a failure at each step.
  • Identity rule table test over author, branch, state and head-repository combinations, including case differences in the login.
  • Config reader goldens: every v1 example in examples/ and the chart's default policy decode to a golden JSON; a file with an unknown block lands it under unrecognised with a location; a file that does not parse exits 2 with the HCL diagnostic.
  • Exit code tests for each of the four codes.
  • Lint probe, once: add import _ "github.com/donaldgifford/repo-guardian/internal/policy" to tools/rgctl/main.go, confirm make lint fails with the rule's message, remove it.
  • Homelab smoke (human): prs list --org <org> against the homelab installation, compare with the GitHub UI, then prs close --from on one throwaway PR with --yes.

docs.title: Migration / Rollout Plan
docs.text:
1. Land rgctl on main so it is installable with go install at any later tag, before anyone turns v1 off anywhere.
  2. Use it whenever v1 is removed from an org: prs list --org X --format json > X.json, review, prs close --from X.json --yes.
  3. At the v2.0.0 cutover it is runbook steps 3 and 6 (DESIGN-0032): the step-3 record is the step-6 input. Edited PRs are left for the controls engine to adopt as tracked PRs.
  4. After v2 fast-forwards main, the tool keeps building because it never imported the deleted packages; the lint rule is what makes that true rather than lucky.
  5. In v2 the in-app CLI, and later a TUI, replace it as a fast follow, running against repo-guardian's API rather than against GitHub; rgctl then either becomes that first-class tool with a goreleaser entry or is retired (D12, D13).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• D1 Identity is author plus branch prefix — a PR is repo-guardian's when the App's bot login authored it and its head branch starts with repo-guardian/; titles and bodies are operator-templated and the reconcile-log marker is absent on first-reconcile PRs, so neither can be required. The same two facts hold for v2's per-control branches, so the tool is not v1-only.
  • D2 Search finds, the Pull Requests API decides — every search hit is re-read before it is listed and again before it is acted on; the index is a shortcut, never evidence.
  • D3 Dry run is the default and every write re-reads first — --yes is required to act, and comment, close and branch deletion are each idempotent so a re-run after a partial failure is safe.
  • D4 The tool imports nothing under internal/ — enforced by the module boundary (no requirement on the parent module) and restated by depguard, probed once; this is the whole reason it can outlive v1.
  • D5 The record file is the cutover contract — step 3 writes it, step 6 reads it, and the close pass acts on exact identities rather than on a fresh search.
  • D6 tools/rgctl as its own Go module, named rgctl — in this repository but outside the product module: its own go.mod that never requires the parent, its own dependencies, go install-able on its own, movable later. The module boundary is the guard; depguard restates it (OQ1 amended and OQ2, resolved 2026-10-05).
  • D7 cobra — the maintainer's standard for new command-line tools; completion and help for free, one new dependency (OQ3, resolved 2026-10-05).
  • D8 Search first, verify always — org scans search then read every hit through the Pull Requests API; --exhaustive is the opt-in full walk (OQ4, resolved 2026-10-05, restating D2).
  • D9 Edited PRs need --force — a PR with a commit by anyone other than the App is skipped and reported; --force closes it anyway; its branch is never deleted. The cutover leaves edited PRs for the controls engine to adopt (OQ5, resolved 2026-10-05).
  • D10 App key or operator token — both credential shapes; the bot login is discovered under App auth and required under token auth (OQ6, resolved 2026-10-05).
  • D11 Branch deletion is opt-in — --delete-branch, never for an edited PR (OQ7, resolved 2026-10-05).
  • D12 A loose reader, and a bounded lifetime — config show renders what the file says without the v1 loader. The tool exists to troubleshoot v1 and to cut over to v2; in v2 an in-app CLI, and later a bubbletea TUI, replace it against the API as a fast follow (OQ8, resolved 2026-10-05).
  • D13 go install only on this line — no goreleaser entry until the tool is first-class in v2 (OQ9, resolved 2026-10-05).
  • D14 A default pointer comment — fixed text behind the tool's marker line, --comment to replace it (OQ10, resolved 2026-10-05).
  • D15 Human-readable logs through charmbracelet/log — an slog handler, coloured on a terminal, on stdout beside the table; on stderr only while a JSON record is being written to stdout (2026-10-05).

docs.title: OQ1: Where does the tool live?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: other. tools/rgctl as its own Go module: the same repository as (a), but outside the product module, so go install works on its own, its dependencies stay out of the product's go.mod, and it can be moved or retired without touching v1 or v2 (D6).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: cmd/rgctl in this repository, private packages under cmd/rgctl/internal, guarded by the depguard rule. One repository, one release pipeline, the dependencies already present, and the lint rule makes the "outlives v1" promise mechanical.
  • (b) A separate repository (repo-guardian-tools). Cleaner separation, but a second goreleaser, signing and renovate setup for one small binary, and nothing stops it importing this module later.
  • (c) A prs subcommand of cmd/repo-guardian. Rejected by the premise: it would be deleted with the v1 code or rewritten with the controls CLI.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ2: What is it called?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: (a). rgctl (D6).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: rgctl. Short, does not collide with rg (ripgrep) or the user's forge, and reads as "repo-guardian control" beside kubectl.
  • (b) rg-prs. Says what it does today, but config show and any later subcommand do not fit the name.
  • (c) repo-guardian-cli. Unambiguous and long.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ3: Which command-line framework?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: (b). cobra is the standard for new tools here (D7).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: the standard library flag package with hand-written subcommand dispatch, as cmd/repo-guardian does. Three subcommands and a dozen flags do not need a framework, and no new dependency enters go.mod.
  • (b) spf13/cobra. Completion and help for free, one more dependency and a different style from the main binary.
  • (c) urfave/cli. Same trade as (b).
  • other:

docs.title: OQ4: How does an org scan find PRs by default?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: (a). Search then verify, --exhaustive opt-in (D8).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: search first, verify every hit through the Pull Requests API, --exhaustive as an opt-in that lists every repository. One request per 100 PRs instead of one per repository, with the index's two failure modes (timeout, 1000-result cap) surfaced as warnings that name the fallback.
  • (b) Exhaustive by default, search never. Always correct, but one request per repository per org, which at twenty-plus orgs is thousands of calls for a handful of PRs.
  • (c) Search only, no verification. Fewer calls, but a stale index hit could be acted on.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ5: What happens to a PR a human has pushed to?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: other. As (a), with the flag named --force: edited PRs are skipped and reported, --force closes them, their branch is never deleted (D9).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: skipped and reported, with --include-edited to close it anyway and its branch never deleted. This matches DESIGN-0032's runbook, which adopts edited PRs as tracked PRs rather than closing them.
  • (b) Closed like any other, with the comment. Simpler, but discards human work that v2 would otherwise pick up.
  • (c) Commented but never closed, even with a flag. Safest, and leaves the operator doing the close by hand.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ6: Which credentials?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: (a). Both (D10).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: both an App id plus private-key file (installation tokens per org, bot login discovered from GET /app, repository set equal to what v1 could see) and a GH_TOKEN operator token (then --bot-login is required). App auth is the natural cutover shape; token auth is what an operator reaches for on a laptop.
  • (b) App auth only. One code path, but every use needs the key file.
  • (c) Token only. Simplest, but the closing comment and the close itself are attributed to a person, and listing an org's repositories needs the token's own org access.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ7: Is the branch deleted when a PR is closed?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: (a). Opt-in with --delete-branch (D11).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: only with --delete-branch, and never for an edited PR. Closing is reversible, deleting a branch is not, and GitHub keeps a closed PR's branch restorable only while the PR exists.
  • (b) Always delete. Tidier, and the default most people want at cutover, but one flag away either way.
  • (c) Never delete. Leaves repo-guardian/* branches behind in every repository.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ8: How much of the v1 policy does config show understand?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: (a). A loose reader is enough: the tool is a troubleshooting and cutover aid for the v1 line, replaced in v2 by the in-app CLI and TUI as a fast follow (D12).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a loose reader, the six top-level block types and the attributes of rule and reconcile blocks, with everything else listed as unrecognised and no evaluation. Enough to answer "what orgs, what rules, what mode" from any v1 file, and nothing to keep in step with the v1 schema.
  • (b) A vendored copy of the v1 schema and merge rules. Exact, but a second copy of code that is being deleted.
  • (c) No config show; orgs come from --org flags only. Smaller, and loses the "what did v1 say" answer the tool is partly for.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ9: How is it distributed?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: (b). go install only; the tool moves into goreleaser when it is first-class in v2 (D13).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a second builds: entry in .goreleaser.yml, shipped, signed and attached to the same release as repo-guardian, plus go install github.com/donaldgifford/repo-guardian/tools/rgctl@<tag>.
  • (b) go install only. No release work, but no signed artifact and a Go toolchain required on the operator's machine.
  • (c) Its own release cadence and tags. Only worth it if the tool moves to its own repository (OQ1 b).
  • other:

docs.title: OQ10: What does the default pointer comment say?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-05: (a). Fixed default text, --comment to replace it (D14).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a fixed text naming the tool, the date and that the repository is now managed by repo-guardian v2's per-control PRs, overridable with --comment, always preceded by the tool's marker line so a re-run never posts twice.
  • (b) --comment required, no default. Forces the operator to write something accurate, and makes the cutover command longer.
  • (c) No comment, just close. Leaves readers of the closed PR with no explanation.
  • other:

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• DESIGN-0032 Evaluation and remediation workflows: cutover runbook (steps 3 and 6), D4, D26, D27.
  • DESIGN-0029 D8 and D11: cutover is a reset on a fresh database.
  • DESIGN-0033 AR-0033-07: evaluate CLI exit codes, reused here.
  • internal/checker/engine.go (BranchName, PRTitle), internal/reconciler/custom_properties.go (PropertiesBranchName, CatalogInfoBranchName), internal/checker/drift.go (reconcileLogMarker), TestPRIdentity_IsFrozen.

  • cmd/rg-burst: precedent for a side binary in this repository; tools/rgctl differs by being its own module.

docs.title: Frontend design cleanup and refresh for the v2 UI
DESIGN-0036: Frontend design cleanup and refresh for the v2 UI
docs.text:
Approved 2026-10-16. Implemented by IMPL-0031; the mockup ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html is kept in step with it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The v2 business UI shipped in IMPL-0025 Phases 20 to 22 with shadcn's default light palette, a text-link header, native <select> filters and a single line chart. It works, and it looks like a scaffold. Two source mockups informed what it should become. A sizzle reel settled the look: one dark charcoal theme, a mono-and-sans type pairing, 3px radii, filled tinted badges, dense tables. A platform mockup contributed layout ideas: an icon sidebar with grouped entries and counts, a page header with breadcrumbs and range controls, a compliance card that puts the KPIs and the trend in one frame, sparklines in the rules table, an expandable org grid with heat-shaded cells, a two-thirds plus one-third repository page, and a draft status page.

Neither source is kept. Their decisions are folded into one artifact, ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html: a single self-contained page, no build step and no network, that renders every route of the redesigned UI from an in-page fake of today's read-only API. Every number on it comes from a field api/openapi.yaml serves now; a panel that would need a field the API lacks renders as a one-line "deferred" note naming the open question, so the gap is visible instead of drawn over. "The mockup" below means that file. This document is the specification; the mockup is the picture of it, and the two are kept in step.

This design takes the look from the reel, the layouts from the platform mockup where they survive contact with real data, maps every panel to the field behind it, and names the handful of places where a panel needs a field the API does not have. The status page, which both sources treated as an afterthought, gets a proper design here because it is the one public surface and today's version is a list.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• One theme, declared once as Tailwind v4 @theme tokens taken from the sizzle, so components stop carrying their own colours.
  • A shell worth the name: icon sidebar with groups and counts, a top bar with search, time zone and account, breadcrumbs, and a consistent page header with the scope and range controls on the right.
  • Fleet, Rules, Orgs, Findings and Repository re-laid out on the platform mockup's patterns, each panel wired to a real API field.
  • A findings detail drawer with badges, evidence and a timeline, deep linkable, so "what is wrong and what was done" is a click.
  • A designed public status page: a state banner, components, fleet compliance with a sparkline, and nothing that names a repository.
  • Keep every security property DESIGN-0027 established: text-only evidence, links built from structured fields, no inline scripts, no external origins, a GET-only proxy.
  • Build the table, grid, drawer and chip components generically so the IMPL-0029 Controls views reuse them.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• No write path. The drawer gets an empty actions slot for IMPL-0029's re-evaluate button; this design adds no POST.
  • No light theme in this change. Tokens make it a later swap (OQ1).
  • No portal chrome. The platform mockup is a multi-app shell (app switcher, notifications bell, favourites). Repo Guardian ships alone; the shell is built so it can later sit inside that portal, but the switcher and the bell are not drawn.
  • No "compliance drivers" map. The mockup's initiatives → inputs → KPIs flow has no data behind it and no owner.
  • No BFF, session, OIDC or CSP changes beyond one optional config value for the documentation link. Where the CSP constrains the design (fonts, images) the design bends, not the CSP.
  • No Grafana, operator or system dashboards; those stay generated (DESIGN-0022).
  • No new tables or migrations. API additions are small, additive, and listed in one place.

docs.title: What the UI is today
docs.text:
ui/web/src/router.tsx renders a top header with a wordmark, horizontal text links (Fleet, Rules, Orgs, Findings, History, Policy), a native <select> org filter written to ?org=, the user's name as text and a POST sign-out button. There is no sidebar. index.css holds a light-only shadcn neutral palette in oklch plus four status colours; there is no dark mode and no font declaration. components/ui/ has Badge (five tones), Button, Card and Table. components/common.tsx has StatusBadge, ExternalLink, Evidence, Remediation, Tile, Section, Loading, Empty and TrendChart, the only Recharts use.

Fleet is four tiles, the 90d line chart, open-PR buckets as text, the worst five rules as a link list and parked-by-reason as text. Findings is native selects over a six-column table with Load-more and CSV export; there is no row detail. Repository has the only timeline and the recent-checks list. History is one small chart per org. Policy is tiles and a table. The public status page is a component list.

docs.title: Two sources, two jobs
docs.text:
Concern Taken from Not taken Colour tokens, type, radius, badge recipe, table density sizzle reel (--st-*, .badge, .tbl, .card) the mockup's navy palette and its HSL variables Sidebar structure (groups, icons, counts), top bar controls, breadcrumbs, page header with scope and range platform mockup app switcher, bell, favourites Fleet layout: combined compliance card, PR-age bars with threshold link, finding-age distribution, worst rules, parked-by-reason bar list, findings-by-status bar, by-rule and by-org tables platform mockup drivers map, PR throughput (no endpoint yet, OQ15), donuts (replaced by bar lists, see Charts) Rules: kind tabs, KPIs, stacked bar, table; rule detail with per-org bars, top-reasons bar list, oldest failures platform mockup Orgs: expandable grid, heat-shaded cells, tabs, totals row, export platform mockup repository-level rows under an org (OQ13) Findings table and detail drawer, evidence block, timeline sizzle reel (drawer), mockup (filter bar and result count) the reel's sort = pr_age chip until the API sorts Repository two-column page platform mockup Status page: banner, components, compliance with sparkline platform mockup draft, redesigned here changelog (no source)

The synthesis, and the thing to open when a sentence below is unclear, is ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html. It is deliberately built with hand-written CSS and SVG rather than the SPA's stack so that it stays a design document: the implementation copies its tokens, layouts and chart rules into Tailwind, React and Recharts, not its code. Its fake API (api.* in the script) mirrors the operation set and field names of api/openapi.yaml, so a mockup panel that reads a field the schema lacks is a bug in the mockup, not a proposal.

The reel's application frame uses the sans face for page titles and the drawer; its display face (Bricolage Grotesque) appears only in the marketing scenes. The app ships two families, not three.

docs.title: Constraints already in force
docs.text:
• CSP. ui/server/static.ts sends default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; script-src 'self'. With no font-src, style-src or img-src, each falls back to 'self'. External fonts are blocked, and so is any data: URI Vite inlines for assets under 4 KB (assetsInlineLimit). Remote avatar images are blocked; /me carries no avatar anyway.
  • Evidence is text. ESLint bans every HTML sink; evidence.ts renders only reasons it knows. Every evidence surface in this design is a styled container around that output.
  • Links are built, never trusted. lib/pr.ts builds PR and repository URLs from host, org, name and number.
  • Org scope lives in the URL as ?org=, retained across links; the Playwright scoping test depends on it.
  • Findings have no id. Identity is (repository_id, rule_kind, rule_name). There is no /findings/{id}; events are per repository and record status transitions only; checks are per repository.
  • No server-side sort on /findings, and no aggregates beyond /summary, /rules, /orgs and /orgs/{org}.
  • History is per (org, rule) and capped client-side at 4,000 points; 90 days across six orgs and eight rules already exceeds it.
  • The status page is public and privacy-guarded. TestStatus_PrivacyGuard fails on any string field in the Status schema outside an allowlist. Anything added to it must be a number, a timestamp or an enum.

docs.title: The controls rework is coming
docs.text: IMPL-0029 task 8.7 replaces the Rules and Findings views with Controls views, Policy with /policies, and gives Repository a controls tab and an evaluation log; INV-0021 marks rules.tsx, findings.tsx and evidence.ts as rule-shaped and slated for replacement; IMPL-0030 adds a Remediations view. The durable deliverables here are the tokens, the shell, the page anatomy, the Fleet page and a set of generic components; the rule-shaped views become thin consumers so that 8.7 swaps data and columns, not chrome (OQ12).

docs.title: Design language
docs.text:
One theme, dark, declared once in index.css as Tailwind v4 @theme variables. The sizzle's stage tokens map as follows.

Token Value Reel source Used for --color-background #17191d --st-bg page, evidence block, inset panels --color-panel #1f2227 --st-panel cards, top bar, sidebar, drawer --color-panel-2 #262a30 --st-panel2 current nav item, selected tab, meter track, hover rows --color-border #31363d --st-line every 1px rule and border --color-foreground #e8eaed --st-fg text --color-muted-foreground #9aa1ab --st-muted labels, sublines, inactive nav --color-accent #5fa8f5 --st-accent links, brand mark, primary series, current timeline node, focus ring --color-ok #3fb950 --ok compliant, applied, operational --color-warn #d9a020 --warn foreign_pr, degraded, reason badges, unknown --color-bad #f2554d --bad non_compliant, failing, down --color-info #7aa7ff --info pr_open, secondary series --color-avatar #3a4c6d --avatar initials avatar --radius-lg 3px --st-radius cards, tabs, nav items, avatar, inputs

Chart series colours are derived from the same set: accent for the primary series, info for a second, ok/warn/bad where a series means good, caution or bad, and muted-foreground for not-applicable. The mockup's categorical palette is not adopted; a chart never needs more than the five tones above plus muted.

The existing --color-compliant, --color-non-compliant, --color-not-applicable and --color-unknown become aliases of ok, bad, muted-foreground and warn while views are converted, and are removed with the last consumer.

Type. Sans: IBM Plex Sans 400/500/600. Mono: JetBrains Mono 400/500. Root 14px; tables, nav, chips and filters 13px; card and KPI labels 12px, uppercase with 0.06em tracking for stat-strip labels as in the mockup; KPI values 22px/600 with tabular-nums; page titles 20px/600 in the sans face. Monospace is semantic: identifiers (repository and rule names, reason codes, PR numbers, timestamps, filter values, query names in subtitles) are mono; prose is sans.

Badges (the reel's .badge): mono 12px, 5px 7px, no radius, background color-mix(in srgb, <tone> 18%, transparent), text color-mix(in srgb, <tone> 65%, white) (75% in the first draft; IMPL-0031 6.1's axe run put the bad tone on a selected row under AA). One tone table in lib/format.ts covers every documented value, with mute for anything unknown (both enums are open):

Field Value Tone status compliant ok status non_compliant bad status not_applicable mute status unknown warn remediation pr_open info remediation applied ok remediation foreign_pr warn remediation disabled, dry_run, none mute (none renders "—" in tables) reason any, in the drawer warn under non_compliant, else mute component state operational / degraded / anything else ok / warn / bad rule kind file, setting, branch_protection, … outline (border only, muted text)

Surfaces. A card is panel, 1px border, 3px radius, a header of a 13px/600 title and a 12px muted subtitle, then a body. Cards may carry a stat strip under the header (the mockup's compliance card): a row of label-over-value cells separated by hairlines. No shadows except the drawer edge; no gradients except the chart area fill.

Density. Tables at 13px with 9px 10px cells and hairline rows; numeric columns right-aligned tabular; a hover tint of panel-2; a selected row tinted accent at 12%.

Motion. None of the reel's entrance animations ship. Drawer slide and popover fades at 200ms, off under prefers-reduced-motion.

docs.title: Fonts under the CSP
docs.text: Fonts are bundled: @fontsource/ibm-plex-sans (latin, 400/500/600) and @fontsource/jetbrains-mono (latin, 400/500), imported from main.tsx so Vite emits hashed woff2 files under /assets/, which the BFF already caches for a year. build.assetsInlineLimit: 0 keeps every asset a file rather than a data: URI, and a build test fails if dist/ contains a data: URL or a fonts.googleapis.com reference. font-display: swap. Both families are SIL OFL; licences ship with the other third-party notices. The CSP does not change (OQ2).

docs.title: Shell
docs.text:
The frame is a 40px top bar over a two-column body: a 220px sidebar (the mockup's width, a little wider than the reel's 196px to fit icons and counts) and a scrolling main area. Both bars are panel on a background page.

Top bar, left to right:

  • Brand: the shield mark in accent, "Repo Guardian" in foreground 600, and the mockup's muted qualifier compliance · read-only. The brand links to /. There is no app switcher; the slot to the left of the brand is reserved so a portal can add one later.
  • Right: a search button labelled ⌘K that opens the command palette; a time-zone control; the avatar.

Command palette (⌘K / Ctrl-K): a dialog with one input that searches repositories through GET /repositories?q= (name prefix, scoped by ?org=), and matches rules and orgs from the already-loaded /rules and /orgs lists. Results are grouped (Repositories, Rules, Orgs); Enter navigates. It is the primary way to reach a repository page and replaces the mockup's placeholder "Repository (example)" nav entry (OQ11).

Time zone. Timestamps render in the browser's zone by default. The control toggles Local / UTC, persisted in localStorage, and every timestamp goes through one formatTime helper that honours it. Hovering a timestamp shows the other zone.

Avatar: a 20px avatar-coloured square with initials from me.name (first letters of the first two words, else the first two characters of subject). It opens a menu with the display name, the subject in mono, the docs link when configured, and Sign out, which stays a POST form to /auth/logout so the BFF's Origin check keeps working.

Sidebar: groups with 10.5px uppercase tracked labels, each entry an icon, a label and an optional right-aligned mono count.

  • BUSINESS: Fleet (grid icon), Rules (list), Orgs (boxes), Findings (activity, count = summary.findings.non_compliant).
  • PUBLIC: Status page (check).
  • DOCS: Documentation (book), shown only when the BFF's /ui/config carries a docs_url (new optional UI_DOCS_URL env; the one BFF change in this design).

The current item is panel-2 with foreground text and an accent left rule; others are muted-foreground. The nav is one array (label, to, icon, group, optional count selector) so IMPL-0029 renames entries by editing data. A footer line in 11px mono shows the policy version prefix and rollout state from /policy and links to /policy (OQ4). Below 900px the sidebar collapses behind a top-bar button.

Org scope is a page-header control (below), not a top-bar one: the mockup places it beside the range control, and that is where the eye looks for "what am I looking at". It writes ?org= exactly as today; the label is All orgs (N) where N is orgs.items.length when me.all_orgs, else me.orgs.length.

docs.title: Page anatomy
docs.text:
Every authenticated page uses the same header block:

  1. Breadcrumbs in 12px: Repo Guardian / <Section> [/ <item>], derived from the route (and the drawer state on Findings).
  2. Title at 20px/600, with an optional outline badge after it (a rule's kind, org, active/parked).
  3. A one-line muted subtitle that says what the page measures, in plain words, naming the endpoint in mono where the mockup did ("Fleet compliance % from /compliance/history").
  4. Right-aligned controls: the org scope popover; where the page has a time dimension, a segmented range 1d | 7d | 30d | 90d; page actions as outline buttons (Export, Findings for this rule).

Range and scope are URL state (?range=, ?org=), so every page is a shareable link and the browser back button works.

docs.title: Navigation map
docs.text: Nav Route Today Change Fleet / fleet.tsx re-laid out Rules /rules, /rules/$kind/$name rules.tsx re-laid out Orgs /orgs, /orgs/$org orgs.tsx re-laid out (expandable grid) Findings /findings findings.tsx re-laid out, drawer added ⌘K → repository /repos/$id detail only re-laid out; reached by palette and links Status page /status status.tsx redesigned (footer) /policy policy.tsx restyled, reached from the sidebar footer (OQ4) (link) /history history.tsx restyled, reached from the compliance card (OQ4)

docs.title: Fleet
docs.text:
The mockup's layout, top to bottom, with the data behind each panel.

Compliance card (two-thirds width). Title Compliance (<range>), subtitle "Fleet compliance % from /compliance/history; compliant ÷ (compliant + non_compliant) over active repositories." Then:

  • A stat strip of five cells: Tracked (summary.tracked repos), Compliant (summary.compliant_percent with a delta against the previous snapshot), Failing (summary.findings.non_compliant and the number of rules with any failure from /rules), Parked (sum of summary.parked[].count and the number of reasons), Snapshots (point count in range and the cadence word derived from the median gap between points). A null percent reads "unmeasured", never 100%.
  • Legend pills for the four series the history points carry: compliant %, failing findings, not applicable, unknown. The pills are a radio group: exactly one series is drawn at a time and the y axis rescales to it. There is no right axis and never two scales in one frame; a reader who wants two series side by side opens History, where each gets its own small chart. The pill shows the series' current value, so the strip, the pills and the chart agree by construction. Pills are buttons with role="radio" and aria-checked.
  • The area chart over the fleet series within ?range=: line and fill in accent, mono 11px axes, y from a nice floor below the minimum to 100, x ticks at a cadence that fits the range. The series comes from /compliance/history aggregated to one point per snapshot; until the aggregate parameter exists it is complianceSeries() over the per-rule points, with the truncated notice when the cap trips (OQ6). A "full history" link goes to /history.

Deltas (compliant, failing) are computed in lib/viewmodel.ts from the same series the chart draws, so the strip and the chart cannot disagree. The reel's "+38 this week" on Tracked has no source and is not drawn (OQ7). Stat values use proportional figures (they are read one at a time); every number in a table column is tabular so the digits align.

Open PRs by age (one-third width). Subtitle "Remediation PRs opened by repo-guardian[bot]. <stale_after>+ counts as stale.", threshold from summary.stale_after. A bar chart over summary.open_prs in bucket order; below it, the mockup's one-liner <stale_prs> PRs over threshold → findings?pr_stale=true as a link.

Finding age distribution (full width). Subtitle "How long non-compliant findings have been open. Under 30 days is the healthy threshold." A single horizontal stacked bar with six segments (<1d, 1-7d, 7-30d, 30-90d, 90-180d, 180d+) shaded ok → warn → bad, a pill <p>% under 30d · healthy threshold, and a legend row of label and share. This needs a histogram of status_since over non_compliant findings, which no endpoint returns; it ships with the finding_age addition to /summary (OQ8) and is hidden until then.

Second row, three cards:

  • Worst rules: worstRules(rules, 5) as name, kind, percent with the previous_percent trend, and a meter whose fill is bad under 70%, warn under 90%, else ok. Rows link to the rule.
  • Parked by reason: a bar list over summary.parked[], sorted descending, each row the reason in mono, the count and its share, and a single-colour bar scaled to the largest row. Parking is a repository state, not a finding, so rows do not link to Findings; they link to a repository list filtered by park_reason once one exists (OQ11), and are static until then.
  • Findings by status: one horizontal stacked bar over the sum of /rules counts (compliant ok, non_compliant bad, not_applicable muted, unknown warn) with the total at its end and a legend row. Its subtitle says the percent counts only the first two, which is the one sentence that stops "why is 84% not 25,000 of 33,000".

PR throughput (14d), opened versus closed remediation PRs per day, has no source: events are per repository. The card is not drawn in the mockup and is not built until an aggregate exists (OQ15).

Third row, two tables:

  • Compliance by rule from /rules: Rule, Kind (outline badge), Compliant, Failing, N/A, %, Trend (a 20-point sparkline from the rule's history, fleet-aggregated). Rows link to the rule.
  • Orgs from /orgs: Org, Tracked, Failing, Parked, and a Compliance column that is a meter plus the percent. Rows link to the org.

With ?org= set, the same layout reads from /orgs/{org} and the Orgs table becomes Not applicable by reason (not_applicable[]).

docs.title: Rules and rule detail
docs.text:
Rules. Header with kind tabs (All | file | setting | branch_protection, values from the kinds present). A KPI row of the four worst rules (name, percent, failing and n/a counts, trend). A stacked bar per rule (compliant ok, non_compliant bad, not_applicable muted, unknown warn), rendered as flex div segments with a 2px surface gap rather than SVG so the bars stay 10px tall at any width, a row total at the end and one legend. Then the full table: Rule, Kind, Compliant, Failing, N/A, Compliance, Trend in points, chevron. All from /rules.

Rule detail. Title is the rule name with a kind badge; subtitle is the policy description from /rules/{kind}/{name}. Right: an outline button "Findings for this rule" → /findings?kind=&rule=. KPIs: Compliance with trend, Compliant, Failing with "oldest: N days" from oldest_failures[0].status_since, Not applicable. Two-thirds: the per-org table (orgs[]) with meter columns. One-third: a Top reasons bar list over top_reasons[] and an Oldest failures list over oldest_failures[] (repository, "failing for N days"), each linking to the repository.

docs.title: Orgs and org detail
docs.text:
Orgs is the mockup's expandable grid. Above it a totals line of badges (Tracked, Failing in bad, Parked in warn) summed from /orgs, then tabs that choose which columns are heat-shaded: Compliance (Compliant ok, Failing bad), Parked (Parked warn), and PR activity once an open-PR count per org exists (OQ14). A toolbar holds the org scope, a parked toggle (All | Hide parked), and Expand/Collapse all. Export writes the visible grid as CSV through the existing defused CSV helper.

Each org row shows the org name, <pct>% compliant · <n> parked, and the row count badge, with numeric columns Tracked, Compliant (count and percent), Failing (count and percent), Parked. Cells shade by share of tracked: the tone at an opacity proportional to the percentage, so a column reads as a heat map. Expanding an org fetches /orgs/{org} and lists its rules as child rows with the same columns (OQ13: the platform mockup drew repositories here, but no endpoint gives per-repository counts cheaply, and per-rule rows answer "where in this org is the problem" with data that exists). A totals row closes the grid.

Org detail (/orgs/$org): title with an org badge, KPIs (Tracked, Compliance, Failing, Parked), two-thirds compliance area chart over the org's history and the rules table with meters, one-third Not-applicable-by-reason and Parked-by-reason bar lists from OrgDetail.not_applicable[] and OrgDetail.parked[].

docs.title: Findings and the detail drawer
docs.text:
Filter bar. A card holding filter chips (the reel's key = value style, mono) for status, reason, remediation, kind, rule, org and pr_stale, a trailing + filter chip, and on the right the mockup's result count: <loaded> of <summary.findings.non_compliant> when the status filter is non_compliant, else just the loaded count. Chips open a popover with that filter's options; state stays in the URL through patchSearch, so every existing deep link works. A sort = pr_age desc chip appears only once the API sorts (OQ5). CSV export is an outline button in the page header.

Table. Repository (org/name mono, foreground, with the org as a muted second line as in the mockup), Rule (mono), Status badge, Reason (mono text, "—" when absent), Remediation badge ("—" for none), PR (#n built with prLink, "—" when absent), Age (PR age from pr.created_at via ageDays; "—" otherwise), Since (status_since, relative, exact on hover). Rows are keyboard activatable; the selected row is tinted. Load-more and the infinite query are unchanged.

Drawer. A 470px right panel in panel with a left border, pushing the table at 1600px and wider (the Age and Since columns hide so the rest fit without a scrollbar) and sliding over it behind a scrim below that. Opening writes ?open=<repository_id>/<kind>/<name>; a reload or shared link looks the row up in loaded pages or fetches it through /repositories/{id} (OQ9). Escape, the close button and the scrim close it; focus moves in on open and back to the row on close. Contents:

  1. Title org/repository as an external link built with repoLink; mono subtitle rule <name> (<kind>) · since <status_since>. Findings have no id, so identity is the subtitle.
  2. Key/value block: Status badge; Reason badge; Remediation badge, then #<number> as a prLink and the branch (pr.head) in mono when present; matched_term after the number for a foreign PR.
  3. Evidence: a background inset, mono 12px, rendering describeEvidence(finding) exactly as today, ✗ in bad tint before a failed assertion. Unknown reasons show the code alone.
  4. Timeline: a left-rule list with square nodes, newest last, latest in accent. Composed client-side from /repositories/{id}/events filtered to source = finding for this rule plus repository events of kind parked, unparked, renamed, transferred, and from /repositories/{id}/checks since status_since, rendered as re-checked · <outcome>; a check after an open PR's created_at adds PR #n still open (<age>). Capped at 20 with a "full timeline" link to the repository.
  5. Footer: an empty actions slot reserved for IMPL-0029's re-evaluate control, and "Open repository".

docs.title: Repository
docs.text: The mockup's two-column page. Header: org/name with an active/parked badge; subtitle checked <relative> · installation <id> · owner <custom property when known>; right, "Open on GitHub". Left two-thirds: the Findings table (Rule, Status, Reason / evidence, Remediation), then Recent checks (Time, Trigger badge, Outcome badge, Duration, Error). Right one-third: a Repository facts card (default branch, park state and reason, catalog parse state, policy version of the last check, from RepositoryDetail), and the Timeline sharing the drawer's component over the merged events. Repository is reached from the palette, the findings drawer, the org grid and the rule detail's oldest failures; /repos as a standalone list is deferred (OQ11).

docs.title: Status page
docs.text:
Public, unauthenticated, outside the shell, aggregate-only. Today it is a component list. The design is the platform mockup's draft made deliberate, within what the Status schema allows and with the additions the page is worth.

Layout, centred at 760px on the background page:

  1. Header row: the shield mark and "Repo Guardian status"; right, a muted updated <relative> · refreshes every 30s matching the API's refresh cadence.
  2. State banner: a card whose border takes the overall tone. A pulsing dot, the headline (All systems operational, Degraded performance, or Service disruption mapped from state), the subline "Public, aggregate-only. No org, repository or rule names appear here." and the state badge.
  3. Components (left): one row per components[] entry with a tone dot, the component name, its detail string and a state badge. The names are the API's (webhooks, backlog per queue, and the rest the status page already reports); webhooks keeps its informational footnote.
  4. Fleet compliance (right): the percent at 40px, a 10px meter in ok, the footnote measured: <bool> · compliant ÷ (compliant + non_compliant), and a 30-day sparkline. The sparkline needs a numeric series on the public schema: compliance.history[] of {at, percent} (OQ10). Until it exists the card shows the number and the meter.
  5. Operations strip (full width, OQ10): three cells that the sizzle asked for and the schema lacks, each a number or enum and so admissible under the privacy guard: Repositories checked in the last 24h as checked / tracked, Last policy rollout as <rollout_state> · <completed_at>, and Last snapshot as a relative time. Hidden until the fields exist.
  6. Footer: GET /api/v1/status · served from an in-process cache in muted mono, and a link to the public documentation when docs_url is configured. No changelog: there is no source for one in the API, and a hand-maintained list on a status page goes stale.

unknown before the first refresh renders the banner in muted tone with "Status not yet available". The page carries no string the schema does not give it; TestStatus_PrivacyGuard keeps policing the schema, and a Playwright test asserts the page text contains no org or repository name from the seed.

docs.title: Component inventory
docs.text:
New or changed primitives in components/ui/, shadcn-style and hand-copied as before; radix-based ones use radix-ui for focus and keyboard behaviour (OQ3).

Component Role Badge tones ok/warn/bad/info/mute plus outline; StatusBadge, RemediationBadge, ReasonBadge, KindBadge, StateBadge wrap it with the tone table Kpi label, value, subline, delta; replaces Tile StatStrip hairline-separated label/value cells inside a card header Pill legend toggle with a colour dot and aria-pressed Card header with title, subtitle and right slot; body PageHeader, Breadcrumbs the page anatomy Table, DataTable density, numeric alignment, selectable and keyboard-activatable rows, column spec and row key GroupGrid expandable parent/child rows, heat-shaded numeric cells, totals row, expand/collapse all Drawer (radix Dialog, side right) and DetailDrawer 470px panel, focus trap, URL-backed open state; title/subtitle/kv/actions layout Popover, DropdownMenu, CommandPalette (radix) org scope, chip editors, avatar menu, ⌘K Tabs segmented range and kind/heat tabs; values mirrored to the URL Chip, FilterChips key = value filters over search params Meter, DistBar threshold-toned bar; six-segment distribution bar with legend Avatar initials square; no image path Sidebar, TopBar shell; data-driven nav array Timeline left-rule event list shared by drawer and repository TrendChart, BarBuckets, StackedBars, BarList, Sparkline the chart set TimeZoneToggle, formatTime Local/UTC

components/common.tsx shrinks to ExternalLink, Evidence, Loading, Empty and Section; the rest move to their own files.

docs.title: Charts
docs.text:
Recharts stays (DESIGN-0027 fixed shadcn charts). Five chart components: TrendChart (area, one series at a time), BarBuckets (single series bars), StackedBars (per-category stacked status counts, plain elements), BarList (ranked rows with count, share and a single-colour bar), Sparkline (20-point line, no axes). Meter and DistBar are plain elements. All read colours from the theme variables, use the mono face for axes at 11px, draw solid hairline grid lines in border, and ship an accessible alternative: an aria-label summary and a table toggle in the card header that swaps the plot for the same data as a dense table.

The rules the mockup follows, which the implementation keeps:

  • One axis per chart. Two measures of different scale get two charts (History's small multiples), never a second y axis.
  • No categorical palette. The theme's accent and info are too close to tell apart for a colour-vision-deficient reader (an OKLab distance of about 3, against a floor of 8), so no chart asks a reader to separate series by hue. Magnitude is drawn in accent; status in the four status tones, and nowhere else; shares as ranked bar lists rather than donuts, where the label does the identifying.
  • Marks. Lines 2px with a 4.5px end dot ringed in the panel colour; area wash at 10% opacity; bars at most 24px wide with a 4px rounded data end; 2px surface gaps between stacked segments; the end-of-line value is the one direct label, never a number on every point.
  • Hover by default. Line and area charts get a crosshair and a tooltip, bars and cells a per-mark tooltip; hit targets are the full column, not the mark.
  • Percent axes never start at zero when the series lives in a narrow band, and a nice floor and ceiling bracket the data so the trend is legible; the end label states the current value.
  • Bar lists are sorted descending, show count and share, and never carry more than eight rows; the rest fold into "other".

docs.title: Surviving the controls rework
docs.text:
• DataTable, GroupGrid, DetailDrawer, FilterChips, Timeline, Kpi, StatStrip and the charts know nothing about rules or findings. They take column specs, row keys and render props.
  • findings.tsx and rules.tsx become column specs, filter specs and a drawer body. The Controls views are other specs against other endpoints.
  • evidence.ts is untouched except for its container; INV-0021 replaces its renderers, not this design.
  • The sidebar nav is an array; renaming Rules to Controls and Findings to Evaluations is a two-line edit and the count moves with the entry.
  • The drawer's actions slot is where 8.7's re-evaluate button lands, so the BFF's eventual POST route needs no layout change.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
• Contrast against the actual hex values: muted-foreground on panel 6.1:1, foreground on background 14.6:1, every badge tone at 65% toward white on an 18% tint clears 5:1. Heat-shaded cells keep their text in foreground and never rely on the shade alone (the number and the percent are printed). @axe-core/playwright runs on Fleet, Orgs, Findings with the drawer open, Repository and Status.
  • Focus is a 2px accent ring with 2px offset on every interactive element, including table rows and legend pills.
  • The drawer and the palette are dialogs: labelled, focus-trapped, Escape closes, focus returns.
  • Charts carry text alternatives; colour is never the only signal (badges carry text, deltas carry arrows, meters print the percent, distribution segments have a legend).
  • No motion beyond drawer and popovers, none under prefers-reduced-motion.

docs.title: API / Interface Changes
docs.text:
The shell, tokens, page anatomy, Fleet compliance card, Rules, Orgs grid (compliance and parked tabs), Findings table, drawer, Repository and the status page banner, components and compliance number all ship on today's API. The panels below each need one additive change; each is independent, each is an open question, and each panel is hidden until its field exists so the UI never shows a placeholder.

Addition Backs OQ GET /compliance/history?aggregate=none\|fleet\|org (sum per snapshot_at in SQL, percent floored in SQL like ComplianceByRule) Fleet area chart and rule sparklines without the 4,000-point cap OQ6 GET /findings?sort=default\|pr_age with the cursor bound to the sort the sort = pr_age chip OQ5 Summary.finding_age[] {bucket, count} over non_compliant findings' status_since, six buckets Finding age distribution OQ8 Status.compliance.history[] {at, percent} (30 daily points), Status.operations{checked_24h, tracked, rollout_state, rollout_completed_at, last_snapshot_at} status sparkline and operations strip OQ10 OrgSummary.open_prs (count of pr_open findings per org) Orgs "PR activity" tab OQ14 A PR throughput aggregate over finding_events (opened/closed per day) Fleet PR throughput card OQ15

Every addition goes through api/openapi.yaml first, regenerates the server (make generate-api) and the client (make generate-ui-api), and is drift-gated by make lint-api and make lint-ui. New status fields are numbers, timestamps and enums only, so TestStatus_PrivacyGuard passes without widening its allowlist.

BFF: one optional env, UI_DOCS_URL, surfaced as docs_url in /ui/config; nothing else. Chart: the matching optional value ui.docsUrl. ui/package.json grows by radix-ui, @fontsource/ibm-plex-sans, @fontsource/jetbrains-mono and, as a dev dependency, @axe-core/playwright.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text: None. No table, column or migration changes. The optional API additions are new sqlc queries over existing columns (compliance_snapshots, findings.status_since, finding_events, checks, policy_versions).

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Unit (bun test ./web). Table-driven tests for the new viewmodel.ts functions: deltas from a series (one point, two points, a gap at the range edge), snapshot cadence word, fleet aggregation, heat-shade opacity, the timeline merge (ordering, "still open" synthesis, the cap), initials, the org-count rule, formatTime in Local and UTC, and the badge tone table over every documented value plus an unknown one.
  • Component tests. Badge tones; DataTable row activation on Enter; GroupGrid expand/collapse and totals; Drawer focus trap, Escape and focus return; FilterChips round-trip through search params; Pill aria-pressed; Kpi delta colouring by direction.
  • Build guard. A test over dist/ asserts no data: URL and no Google Fonts reference, so an inlined asset cannot break the CSP.
  • Playwright. Existing specs updated where selectors change (Sign out in the avatar menu; chips instead of selects; the breadcrumb row). New specs: drawer from a row and from ?open=; range tabs change the chart query; org scope popover writes ?org=; ⌘K finds the seeded repository; Orgs grid expands an org to its rules; status page contains no seeded org or repository name; axe passes on five pages. Screenshot tests for Fleet, Orgs, Findings with the drawer, Repository and Status under Chromium with the seeded stack (OQ16).
  • Contract drift. ui/scripts/check-api.ts keeps failing on any divergence from api/openapi.yaml; each API addition regenerates both sides in the same change, with a sqlc test and an apitest case.
  • Security regressions. The ESLint HTML-sink ban and eslint-ban.test.ts are unchanged and cover every new component; the "HTML in evidence renders as text" e2e test is re-pointed at the drawer.
  • Chart. A helm-unittest case for ui.docsUrl rendering into the UI env; nothing else changes.

docs.title: Migration / Rollout Plan
docs.text:
A UI-image change with no data migration, shipped in a v2 release candidate. The IMPL that follows is expected to phase it as:

  1. Tokens, fonts, Vite inline limit, build guard, primitives and charts.
  2. Shell: top bar, sidebar, palette, time zone, avatar menu, page anatomy; Playwright selector updates.
  3. Fleet (on today's API), Rules and rule detail.
  4. Orgs grid and org detail; Findings filter bar, table and drawer; Repository.
  5. Status page redesign on today's schema.
  6. Axe, screenshots, docs/usage/ui.md text and screenshots.
  7. API additions, each its own task, each un-hiding its panel: history aggregate, findings sort, finding age, status fields, org open PRs.

Rollback is the previous UI image tag; the API stays backward compatible throughout. This should land before IMPL-0029 task 8.7 so the Controls views are built on the new components (OQ12).

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
OQ1. Theme scope.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: dark only, the sizzle's "settled Platform UI"; tokens make a light theme a later swap. The platform mockup's sun icon is not drawn.
  • (b) dark and light following prefers-color-scheme; doubles contrast and screenshot work for a surface nobody has asked to see in light.
  • (c) a user toggle persisted in localStorage; (b) plus state.
  • other:

OQ2. Fonts.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: bundle IBM Plex Sans and JetBrains Mono via fontsource (about 150 KB of woff2), CSP untouched; do not ship Bricolage Grotesque, which the application frame never uses.
  • (b) system fonts only; zero bytes, but the look depends on the mono/sans pairing and tabular numerals.
  • (c) also ship Bricolage for page titles; a third family for a face the reel reserves for marketing scenes.
  • other:

OQ3. Primitive base for dialog, popover, palette and tabs.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: radix-ui, which shadcn's own components wrap; focus trapping, typeahead and ARIA come for free and the copied components stay close to upstream.
  • (b) native <dialog> and the popover attribute, hand-rolled; no dependency, but focus return, scrim and keyboard handling are ours to get right and test.
  • other:

OQ4. History and Policy, which neither mockup puts in the nav.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: keep both routes out of the primary nav; the range control and a "full history" link cover History, and a sidebar footer line (policy version and rollout state) links to Policy.
  • (b) a third nav group holding both; two reference pages promoted to daily navigation.
  • (c) delete History; loses the per-org, per-rule series the Fleet chart cannot show.
  • other:

OQ5. Findings sort.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: sort=pr_age on GET /findings with the cursor bound to the sort; the only correct "oldest PR first" across pages.
  • (b) sort loaded pages client-side; wrong as soon as Load-more appends, and the chip would lie.
  • (c) no sort; rely on pr_stale=true.
  • other:

OQ6. The history cap on Fleet and the rule sparklines.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: aggregate=fleet|org on /compliance/history, summed and floored in SQL; ninety points for ninety days, and a sparkline per rule is one small query.
  • (b) raise maxPages and show the truncated notice; still quadratic in orgs × rules.
  • (c) a dedicated /compliance/history/fleet path; the same SQL behind a second route and a second scope predicate to lint.
  • other:

OQ7. "+38 this week" on Tracked.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: do not draw it; Tracked shows repos and the parked count, and the compliance and failing deltas come from the snapshot series client-side.
  • (b) add discovered_7d to /summary from repository_events; a small query, but a new number to keep honest across report, API and snapshot.
  • other:

OQ8. Finding age distribution.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Summary.finding_age[], six buckets over status_since for non_compliant findings, computed in SQL with the same scope predicate as every api_* query; the panel is hidden until it exists.
  • (b) compute client-side from /findings?status=non_compliant pages; thousands of rows for one bar, and wrong until every page is loaded.
  • (c) drop the panel; it is the clearest "are we getting better at fixing things" view either mockup has.
  • other:

OQ9. Drawer deep-link key.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: ?open=<repository_id>/<kind>/<name> as a search param; one route owns both filters and detail, and a missing row is fetched through /repositories/{id}.
  • (b) a child route /findings/$repo/$kind/$name; cleaner in the router, but the drawer owns a path while its parent owns filter state, and retainSearchParams has to carry both.
  • (c) no deep link; "now it's a click" loses its shareable URL.
  • other:

OQ10. Status page additions.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: extend Status with compliance.history[] (30 daily {at, percent}) and an operations object (checked_24h, tracked, rollout_state, rollout_completed_at, last_snapshot_at), all numeric, timestamp or enum, so the privacy guard passes unchanged; the sparkline and the operations strip are what make the page worth a bookmark.
  • (b) ship the redesign on today's schema only (banner, components, percent and meter) and add fields later.
  • (c) also add a changelog; no source in the API, and a hand-kept list on a status page goes stale.
  • other:

OQ11. How a repository is reached.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: the ⌘K palette over GET /repositories?q= plus rules and orgs from loaded lists; no standalone /repos page yet, and the mockup's "Repository (example)" placeholder is not a nav entry.
  • (b) a /repos list page with search and park filters as well; a second surface to build and test, worth doing when the parked list needs a home (DESIGN-0027's replacement table promised one).
  • (c) links only; a repository is reachable only from findings, orgs and rule detail.
  • other:

OQ12. Sequencing against IMPL-0029 task 8.7.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: land this first, with generic table, grid, drawer and chips, so Controls views are built on the new components; 8.7 then edits column specs and nav data.
  • (b) fold the restyle into 8.7; one larger change that restyles pages while replacing them.
  • (c) wait for IMPL-0029; the rc keeps the scaffold look for however long the controls work takes.
  • other:

OQ13. What an org row expands to in the Orgs grid.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: the org's rules from /orgs/{org}, fetched on expand; the data exists and it answers "where in this org".
  • (b) repositories, as the mockup draws; needs per-repository status counts the API does not aggregate, or one /repositories/{id} call per row.
  • (c) both, as nested levels; the grid's second level becomes a tree and the heat map stops reading at a glance.
  • other:

OQ14. Orgs "PR activity" tab.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: add open_prs to OrgSummary (count of pr_open findings per org) and ship the tab with it; until then the tab is hidden.
  • (b) derive it from /findings?org=&remediation=pr_open per org; N paged queries for one column.
  • (c) drop the tab.
  • other:

OQ15. PR throughput card.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: defer; design the card, build it when an aggregate over finding_events exists (DESIGN-0027 promised the series under History), and keep the Fleet second row at two cards until then.
  • (b) add a /compliance/pr_throughput endpoint now; a new aggregate query inside a styling change.
  • (c) drop the card for good.
  • other:

OQ16. Visual regression tests.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Playwright toHaveScreenshot for five pages, Chromium only, 0.2% threshold, snapshots committed; bundled fonts and seed data make them deterministic and the e2e job already runs Chromium.
  • (b) axe only; catches accessibility, not a broken layout.
  • (c) a hosted visual-diff service; an external dependency for one SPA.
  • other:

OQ17. Where the mockup lives, and what happens to its sources.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html tracked in the repository, referenced from this doc by path and kept in step with it; the two source files (the sizzle reel and the platform mockup) are not committed, since every decision taken from them is written down here and drawn in the mockup, and the reel links Google Fonts, which the published site should not serve. ui/design/ sits outside ui/web/, so Vite, ESLint and the generated-types gate never see it.
  • (b) commit the sources beside it for provenance; two more files to explain, both already superseded.
  • (c) docs/design/assets/0036/; discoverable from the doc, but published by mkdocs.
  • other:

OQ18. Time zone control.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a Local | UTC toggle in the top bar persisted in localStorage, every timestamp through one helper, the other zone on hover; cheap and it ends "which zone is this" in incident threads.
  • (b) browser zone only, no control.
  • (c) a full zone picker as the mockup draws; a list of 400 zones for a question that has two useful answers.
  • other:
