docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
rc.11 put the UI on the controls schema (IMPL-0029 Phase 8) and, to get there, removed every page and panel that read the findings model. This design brings the useful ones back on the controls model: a findings page filterable by control, an expandable org tree, the richer fleet panels, CSV export, and a changelog on the status page. It names the API each needs, marks what waits on remediation (IMPL-0030), adds the Remediations view, and ships the INV-0023 repository-page fixes in a small pull request ahead of the rest.

The mockup is part of this design. ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html is updated in the same pull request to the controls line and to every page below, and is accepted with the design: the implementation builds from an accepted mockup, it does not draw one (OQ10).

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• A findings page: every non-compliant (repository, control) result across the visible fleet, filterable by control, rule, org and decision, keyset-paged, exportable as CSV.
  • An orgs tree: one grid of orgs that expand to their repositories, with compliant/non-compliant counts and shares per row, a parked tab, repository search, and a totals footer.
  • Fleet panels: a range selector driving the compliance card, a KPI strip with deltas, a finding age distribution, worst controls, parked by reason, and a compliance-by-control table with trend sparklines.
  • CSV export on every table card again.
  • A changelog on the status page with a source that cannot silently go stale.
  • The panels that need remediation data (open PRs by age, PR throughput, the remediation column, the stale-PR filter) are designed now and switched on by IMPL-0030.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• The compliance drivers map (initiatives → inputs → north star → KPIs with correlations). It needs data repo-guardian does not hold (GitHub Projects, initiative state) and correlation analytics; it stays deferred as in DESIGN-0036 (OQ15) and wants its own design.
  • Writes beyond the existing re-evaluate POST. The UI stays read-only.
  • A new design language. DESIGN-0036's tokens, primitives and tone table stay; this design adds pages and panels to them.
  • Per-repository metrics labels. "Which repository" stays an API and log question (IMPL-0023 Finding G); nothing here touches Prometheus.

docs.title: What rc.11 shows
docs.text: Page rc.11 content Fleet assignments posture card, controls table, orgs table Controls control list, control detail with per-org breakdown Orgs org list; org detail with controls, worst controls, exclusions Repositories list (org, active, park reason, policy state, name prefix); detail with Controls / Evaluation log / Events tabs History compliance history by control and days Policy the visible policy layers Status components, compliance, deployment card, apps, overdue

docs.title: What IMPL-0029 removed
docs.text: IMPL-0029 deleted the findings-era views and their helpers rather than port them: views/findings.tsx (+ drawer), views/rules.tsx, the org expand/collapse grid usage (orgs.test.tsx), views/repository.tsx, lib/csv.ts (the defused CSV writer), lib/range.ts + page/RangeTabs.tsx, lib/pr.ts, the timeline and the command palette. The GroupGrid primitive survived unused. Those files are the starting point for this design's components; their data hooks are not, because they read /findings and /rules, which no longer exist.

Each mockup panel (ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html, the findings-era platform mockup) against the controls API:

Panel Data today Needs Findings page nothing cross-repository; /repositories/{id}/controls per repository GET /results Orgs tree, org rows GET /orgs (OrgSummary: tracked, parked, compliance, open_prs) nothing Orgs tree, repository rows GET /repositories?org= without posture Repository.compliance Orgs parked tab GET /repositories?active=false nothing Compliance card + range GET /summary, GET /compliance/history?days= (one row per day, org, control and decision) aggregate=fleet on history KPI: failing controls, parked reasons partial Summary.parked_by_reason, controls with any non-compliant Finding age distribution control_results.last_changed_at exists, not exposed Summary.finding_age Worst controls (fleet) GET /controls delta from aggregate=control history Parked by reason not exposed Summary.parked_by_reason Compliance by control + trend GET /controls; history unaggregated aggregate=control on history Orgs table with bars GET /orgs nothing Open PRs by age Summary.open_prs count only IMPL-0030 + Summary.open_prs_by_age PR throughput (14d) nothing IMPL-0030 + GET /remediations/activity Status changelog nothing a source (OQ4) Compliance drivers map nothing non-goal

docs.title: The mockup and DESIGN-0036
docs.text:
ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html is the UI's reference (DESIGN-0036 OQ17), but until this design it was still the findings-era mockup: IMPL-0029 replaced the pages underneath it and did not touch it. This design's pull request redraws it; the tables below record what it showed, what rc.11 shows and what the redraw makes of each. Out of step with rc.11 itself, before anything here:

Mockup today rc.11 / controls line Rules and rule detail; rows are (kind, name) rules Controls and control detail; rows are slug@version controls Finding statuses, reason codes (file_missing, setting_mismatch, …), remediation pr_open/applied/foreign_pr/disabled/dry_run result buckets, rule statuses pass/fail/error, evidence kinds; remediation states arrive with IMPL-0030 One reconcile branch repo-guardian/add-missing-files per repository per-control pull requests (IMPL-0030) Repository page: Findings, Recent checks, Repository (installation and rate limit), Timeline Controls / Evaluation log / Events tabs, Repository card, Re-evaluate Status: github api budget component; sparkline and operations strip marked deferred no budget component; sparkline, operations, deployment, apps, coverage, overdue shipped Policy: one rules table policy layers (enterprise, catalogue, orgs) History: per-org small multiples by rule history by control and days Tone table knows finding statuses only the same gap as INV-0023 F1

Already drawn, made real here. The findings-era mockup already drew most of this design, on the findings model; the redraw moves each onto results and controls:

Mockup This design Orgs grouped grid: heat cells by share, Tracked/Failing/Parked chips, Compliance/Parked tabs, totals row, Export CSV Orgs tree; children become repositories (see below) Findings: filter chips with "+ filter", "N loaded of M", Export CSV, drawer with evidence, timeline and an "actions slot (IMPL-0029 re-evaluate)" Findings page with the drawer; the actions slot becomes Re-evaluate Fleet: KPI strip with deltas, series pills, open PRs by age, worst rules, parked bar list, findings-by-status stacked bar, compliance by rule with sparklines, orgs (or N/A by reason when one org is scoped) Fleet panels Rule detail: top reasons, oldest failures, "Findings for this rule" Control detail Header org scope and 1d/7d/30d/90d range kept; the range tabs come back

The mockup's deferred banners, and what happens to each:

Banner Outcome Finding age distribution (DESIGN-0036 OQ8) here, Summary.finding_age over control_results.last_changed_at PR throughput (OQ15) here, gated on IMPL-0030 "+N discovered this week" (OQ7) stays out, as OQ7 (a) decided Repository rows under an org (OQ13) here, superseding OQ13 (a) PR activity tab (OQ14) here, gated on IMPL-0030 sort = pr_age (OQ5) here, as a /results sort (API in IMPL-0030) Status sparkline and operations strip (OQ10) shipped in rc.10, carried onto the controls schema in rc.11

Not in the committed mockup at all. The status changelog, the compliance drivers map and the "Stale PR (>30d)" checkbox come from the platform mockup, a source DESIGN-0036 OQ17 chose not to commit. The changelog and the stale-PR filter are designed here; the drivers map stays a non-goal.

The redraw in this pull request. The mockup now draws the controls line and every page here: Fleet (panels 1–8), Controls and control detail, the Orgs tree with its Parked and PR activity tabs, org detail, Findings with filters, sort, drawer and Re-evaluate, Repositories and the repository page (Controls / Evaluation log / Events, the rule tone, the name crumb, next due, the remediable hint, the remediation panel), Remediations (views, filters, hold sentences, drawer), History, Policy layers, and the status page with deployment, operations, the remediation backlog and the changelog. Its in-page api mirrors api/openapi.yaml plus the additions in API / Interface Changes, so a panel the mockup draws is a panel the API can back. A top-bar switch marked "mockup" previews the remediation-gated panels with a Remediation App installed; it is not a product control. Export buttons download real CSV through the lib/csv.ts rules.

DESIGN-0036's API additions on the controls line. All six were findings-era endpoints or fields; IMPL-0029 removed or carried them:

DESIGN-0036 addition Controls line /compliance/history?aggregate= (OQ6) removed with /findings; the controls history is unaggregated again, so it comes back here as aggregate=none\|fleet\|org\|control /findings?sort=pr_age (OQ5) /results?sort=pr_age, IMPL-0030 Summary.finding_age (OQ8) here, same name and buckets, over results Status.compliance.history, Status.operations (OQ10) carried, shipped OrgSummary.open_prs (OQ14) carried; reads 0 until IMPL-0030 PR throughput aggregate (OQ15) GET /remediations/activity, IMPL-0030

DESIGN-0036 decisions this design supersedes: OQ13 (an org row expands to repositories, not rules; the rules-in-org view stays on /orgs/$org), §Status page's "No changelog" (the source is now CHANGELOG.yaml with a release gate), and OQ11's palette-only repository access, which IMPL-0029 already replaced with the /repositories page (OQ9 here asks whether the palette comes back).

DESIGN-0032 decision this design supersedes: the D32 row "Findings view is removed; its filters move to the Remediations view". Findings and remediations answer different questions: a finding is a non-compliant result, whether or not anything is being done about it; a remediation is the pull request or API change repo-guardian makes. Most findings have no remediation (an evaluate-mode control, a rule that is not remediable, a deployment without the Remediation App), so folding findings into the Remediations view would hide them. Both pages exist: the Findings page over /results, and the Remediations view over DESIGN-0032's /remediations with the filters D32 gave it. Each links to the other's row.

docs.title: Vocabulary
docs.text:
Two words, two meanings (OQ1):

  • A result is the outcome of one assigned control on one repository (control_results: status, rule results, evidence, last_changed_at), whatever its status.
  • A finding is a result in the non-compliant posture bucket (IMPL-0030 OQ15): status non_compliant and not stale, parked or suspended, so the Findings page, its total and Summary.compliance.non_compliant count the same rows.

The API serves results (GET /results, any status, filterable); the Findings page lists findings, which is /results?status=non_compliant. Neither word means a rule: the failing rules are the detail inside a finding.

docs.title: Findings page
docs.text:
Route /findings, nav entry under Business with a count badge (the findings in the visible orgs, Summary.compliance.non_compliant). The page always asks /results for status=non_compliant; there is no status filter, because a compliant row is not a finding.

Filters, each mapping 1:1 to a /results query parameter and persisted in the URL search (the History page's numeric-search rule applies):

Filter Parameter Values Control control a control slug from /controls Rule rule enabled once a control is chosen; a rule id of that control, matched against rules whose status is fail or error Org org an org from /orgs Decision decision baseline, replaced, org_added Stale PR pr_stale IMPL-0030

Columns: Repository (name, org beneath), Control (slug, version), Failing rules (rule ids with the first failing rule's evidence headline from describeEvidence), Remediation (IMPL-0030; — until then), Since (last_changed_at, relative with absolute on hover). A row opens the finding drawer (OQ8), deep-linked as ?open=<repository_id>/<control> per DESIGN-0036 OQ9: the control's rule table with each failing rule's evidence (text only), the control's events from /repositories/{id}/events, Re-evaluate (the mockup's actions slot, now the existing POST) and "Open repository →".

Paging is keyset (cursor, limit 50) like /repositories, with a "Load more" button and "N of M" from a total the endpoint returns for the current filter (OQ3). Sort is last_changed_at ascending by default (oldest problems first), toggled to descending.

docs.title: Control detail
docs.text: /controls/$id gains the mockup's rule-detail cards on results: Top failing rules (a bar list of the control's findings by failing rule) and Oldest findings (/results?control=<slug>&sort=since_asc, ten rows, opening the drawer), plus a "Findings for this control" button to /findings?control=<slug>.

docs.title: Orgs tree
docs.text:
/orgs becomes one GroupGrid: org rows are groups, repositories are children loaded per org on expand (/repositories?org=<org>&active=true, keyset, "Load more" inside the group).

Column Org row Repository row Org / repository org, "N% compliant · M parked" name Tracked active repositories assignments Compliant count, share of measured, shaded count, share, shaded Non-compliant count, share, shaded count, share, shaded Open PRs OrgSummary.open_prs IMPL-0030 Parked parked repositories parked badge or blank

Cells shade by share of measured (compliant + non_compliant), the same denominator as percent, so a cell's colour and the row's percentage never disagree. Unmeasured rows render "no data", never 0% or 100% (Posture contract).

Above the grid: the KPI chips (Tracked, Non-compliant, Parked), tabs Compliance / Parked (and PR activity after IMPL-0030), an org filter, a repository-name search (q), Expand all / Collapse all, and Export. The footer row sums the visible rows with addPosture, never by averaging percentages. The Parked tab lists parked repositories with reason and parked-at, grouped by org. The org detail page (/orgs/$org) stays and is reached from the org name.

docs.title: Fleet panels
docs.text:
Header gains a range selector (1d / 7d / 30d / 90d, restored RangeTabs, ?days=) that drives every history-backed panel.

  1. Compliance card: KPI strip (Tracked repositories · Compliant % with delta in points over the range · Non-compliant results and the number of controls with any · Parked and the number of reasons · Snapshots and cadence), series pills (compliance %, findings, not applicable, unknown) choosing what the area chart draws, and the chart from /compliance/history?aggregate=fleet. The delta is last point minus first point in the range; fewer than two points renders no delta.
  2. Finding age distribution: a segmented bar over <1d, 1–7d, 7–30d, 30–90d, 90–180d, 180d+ of now − last_changed_at for non-compliant results, with a "N% under 30d" pill. Buckets are fixed; they are not a tuning knob.
  3. Worst controls: the five lowest measured percentages from /controls, each with its delta over the range from aggregate=control history, linking to the control.
  4. Parked by reason: a bar list from Summary.parked_by_reason (bar lists, not donuts, per DESIGN-0036 §Charts; OQ5).
  5. Compliance by control: Control, type (KindBadge), Compliant, Non-compliant, N/A, %, and a sparkline over the range from aggregate=control history.
  6. Orgs: the existing table with a meter per row; with one org in scope it becomes Exclusions by reason from OrgDetail.exclusions (the mockup's "Not applicable by reason").
  7. Assignments: rc.11's bucket card stays, as the controls form of the mockup's "Findings by status" stacked bar.
  8. Open PRs by age and PR throughput (14d): see Remediation-gated panels.

Every table card carries Export.

docs.title: Status page changelog
docs.text:
DESIGN-0036 left the changelog out because the API had no source and a hand-kept list goes stale. The source proposed here is a curated CHANGELOG.yaml at the repository root (OQ4):

- version: 2.0.0-rc.11
  date: 2026-10-17
  title: Controls evaluation
  summary: Policies are a directory of controls; each repository is evaluated against its resolved assignments.
  tags: [new, policy, ui]

It is embedded into the UI bundle at build time and rendered as the status page's Changelog card (newest five, then "All releases" linking to the GitHub releases page). Staleness is a test, not a promise: lint-ui fails when the newest entry's version is not the chart's appVersion, so the release-bump PR cannot land without an entry. Tags are a closed set (new, improved, fixed, breaking, plus an area from fleet, findings, policy, ui, api, chart) so they tone through toneFor. Nothing goes through /status, so TestStatus_PrivacyGuard keeps its allowlist unchanged.

docs.title: CSV export
docs.text: lib/csv.ts comes back as it was: RFC 4180 quoting plus formula defusing (a cell starting =, +, -, @, tab or CR gets a leading '), with its tests. Tables export the rows they show. The findings page exports the whole current filter by paging /results in the browser up to a cap of 10,000 rows, with a notice when the cap cuts it short (OQ6). Filenames carry the page, filter and date (findings-renovate-2026-10-18.csv).

docs.title: Remediation-gated panels
docs.text:
These render in the layout now and fill in when IMPL-0030 writes remediations rows (OQ7):

  • Open PRs by age (fleet): <1d, 1–7d, 7–30d, 30d+ of open pull-request remediations by created_at, with "N over threshold → findings?pr_stale=true".
  • PR throughput (14d) (fleet): per day, pull-request remediations opened (created_at) vs closed (closed_at).
  • Remediation column and Stale PR filter (findings), PR activity tab and repository-row Open PRs (orgs).
  • The Remediations view, the repository remediation panel and the status page's remediation backlog (next section).

Until then each shows an empty state naming why ("Remediation is not enabled on this deployment"), decided from Status.apps (no remediate App) rather than from an empty result, so a deployment with remediation and nothing open reads "No open pull requests" instead.

docs.title: Remediations view
docs.text:
/remediations lists what repo-guardian is doing about findings: one row per remediations row, over DESIGN-0032's GET /remediations (IMPL-0030). The mockup draws it at #/remediations.

  • Nav: a Remediations entry under Findings, its count the outstanding rows (reserved, open, recommended, failed) in the org scope. Gated like every remediation panel: with no remediate App in Status.apps the page is the "Remediation is not enabled" empty state and the nav count is blank.
  • KPIs: Open PRs (with how many are stale at 30 days), outstanding Recommendations, Held (with a count per hold reason), Failed applies.
  • Views and filters: segmented views All / Open PRs / Recommendations / Held / Failed, then filter chips for kind, state, org, control, hold and age (older_than days), each mapping 1:1 to a /remediations query parameter and round-tripping through the URL.
  • Columns: Repository (name over org), Control, Kind (pull_request or api), State (the schema's states; a pull request links its number), Hold (badge plus the human sentence below), Age (from created_at, with the stale badge on an open PR at 30 days), Updated.
  • Drawer (?open=<remediation id>): state, the pull request and its repo-guardian/<control> branch, hold with its sentence, age, the proposal for a recommendation (the failing rules and what each needs), the steps journal for a direct apply, and the result's timeline; links to the finding and the repository.
  • Export: the current filter, through lib/csv.ts.

Hold reasons are sentences, not codes. The UI maps each to what an operator does about it:

Hold Shown as pr_cap the repository is at max_open_prs; waits for a slot foreign_branch a repo-guardian/ branch exists that the bot did not create; rename or delete it to resume stale_branch branch left from a closed PR; delete it to resume conflict the PR branch conflicts with the default branch and could not be updated permission the Remediation App lacks permission for this change

remediations.hold is permission only; the branch holds live on control_results.hold and are set before any pull request exists, so the Held view needs those results too. Whether /remediations returns them (as rows with no pull request) or the view reads them from /results?hold= is an IMPL-0030 question.

Repository remediation panel. Each control card on the repository page shows its remediation under the rules: the state badge, pull request link and age, the hold sentence, the apply steps when there are any, and "details →" to the Remediations drawer.

Status page backlog. The operations strip gains a Remediation backlog cell (outstanding remediations, aggregate only, so the privacy guard holds) when a Remediation App is installed.

docs.title: API / Interface Changes
docs.text:
All additions except one: aggregated history relaxes HistoryPoint's org, control_id and decision to optional, stating per aggregate which are present (IMPL-0030 OQ14). Every new SQL query carries the scope predicate (TestAPIQueries_AreScoped) and every new operation gets a case in TestEndpoints_ValidateAgainstTheSpec.

Change Shape Phase GET /results query bucket, control, rule, org, decision, sort (since_asc, since_desc), cursor, limit; returns ResultPage{items: [ResultRow], total, next_cursor}. ResultRow: repository id/org/name, control id/version, decision, status, failing_rules: [rule_id], reason (first failing rule's evidence reason or evidence_kind), last_changed_at IMPL-0030 Repository.compliance Posture over the repository's assignments, on list and detail IMPL-0030 Summary.parked_by_reason [{reason, count}] over visible orgs IMPL-0030 Summary.finding_age [{bucket, count}], the six fixed buckets IMPL-0030 Summary.controls_failing count of controls with any non-compliant result IMPL-0030 /compliance/history?aggregate= none (today's rows, default) | fleet | org | control; sums per day in SQL with floor_percent, never averaged; DESIGN-0036 OQ6 on the controls schema IMPL-0030 Summary.open_prs_by_age [{bucket, count}] IMPL-0030 GET /remediations/activity days (1–90, default 14) → [{day, opened, closed}] IMPL-0030 /results pr_stale, ResultRow.remediation remediation state, PR number/url, PR age IMPL-0030 GET /remediations DESIGN-0032's endpoint: kind, state, org, control, hold, older_than_days, cursor, limit; the Remediations view reads it as specified there IMPL-0030 Status.operations.remediation_backlog count of outstanding remediations IMPL-0030

/results is the API's first cross-repository row list over control_results; it reads through rg_api_ro like everything else and its RLS stays PUBLIC read.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
No new tables. Everything reads existing columns: control_results(status, last_changed_at, control_id) and its rule results, repositories(active, park_reason), compliance_snapshots (per org, control, decision, day) for trends, and remediations (kind, state, created_at, closed_at) once IMPL-0030 writes it.

/results filters by control and status and sorts by last_changed_at; if the perf fixture (TestAPIPerf) shows a sequential scan at fleet size, add control_results (control_id, status, last_changed_at) in a controls migration. Decide from the plan output, not up front.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Go: store integration tests per new query (scope, keyset paging with ties on last_changed_at, the age buckets at their boundaries, total matching the filter); TestEndpoints_ValidateAgainstTheSpec cases for every new operation and field; the two-org authz test extended to /results (a globex row never appears for an acme-only caller).
  • UI unit: view models for the tree (footer sums via addPosture, share shading, "no data"), the age distribution, deltas with fewer than two points, CSV defusing, the changelog version check.
  • e2e: the seed gains several controls with failing rules and distinct evidence, parked repositories with three reasons, last_changed_at spread over every age bucket and 30 days of snapshots. Specs per page (filters round-trip through the URL, export downloads the expected rows, tree expand/collapse, globex never appears), axe on every new page, visual snapshots in the pinned Playwright image.
  • Tone: one assertion per badge family that a failing value carries the bad tone (the INV-0023 F1 gap).

docs.title: Migration / Rollout Plan
docs.text:
UI and API ship together in rc releases from v2 (Rule 6). The mockup is not a phase: it was updated and accepted with this design. Each phase builds its pages to the accepted mockup, and a page that has to differ from it changes the mockup in the same pull request. The work splits three ways (decided 2026-10-18):

  1. The INV-0023 fixes, a small pull request now (IMPL-0032 Phase 1): F1 (rule tone), F2 (crumb), F4 (remediable wording), F7.3 (status screenshot).
  2. Every API addition in the table above, and persisting next due, in IMPL-0030 beside the remediation API they share the schema and the EvaluationWorkflow version gate with.
  3. The UI in IMPL-0032 once IMPL-0030 merges: foundations (restore csv.ts and RangeTabs, Export, the IMPL-0031 6.3 keyboard pass), Findings page, Orgs tree, Fleet panels, the Remediations view and the other remediation panels, and the changelog (CHANGELOG.yaml seeded with rc.9 to rc.11, the lint-ui version check, the status card).

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
OQ1. What the page and the API call a row.

  • (a) page Findings, API /results and ResultRow; operators search for "findings", the schema has results.
  • (b) both Results; consistent, but loses the word people look for.
  • (c) both Findings; reintroduces a type name the controls line deleted on purpose.
  • other: keep both words with distinct meanings: a result is any control outcome, a finding is a result that failed.

Decision (2026-10-18): other. /results serves results of any status; the Findings page lists findings (status=non_compliant) and has no status filter. See Vocabulary.

OQ2. Repository rows in the orgs tree.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: load per org on expand from /repositories with compliance added; the page stays fast at hundreds of repositories per org.
  • (b) one /orgs?include=repositories call; one request, unbounded payload.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-18): (a).

OQ3. A total on /results.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: return total (a count(*) over the same filter in the same read-only transaction) for "N of M" and the export cap notice.
  • (b) no total, "Load more" only; cheaper, but the page cannot say how much is left.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-18): (a).

OQ4. The changelog's source.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: curated CHANGELOG.yaml, embedded in the UI bundle, gated by a lint-ui check that the newest entry is the chart appVersion.
  • (b) generated from the git-cliff CHANGELOG.md; no upkeep, but the entries are commit subjects, not release notes.
  • (c) a link to GitHub releases only; nothing to maintain or render.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-18): (a).

OQ5. Parked by reason chart.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a bar list, as DESIGN-0036 settled for every share chart.
  • (b) the mockup's donut; one exception to the chart rules.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-18): (a).

OQ6. Exporting the findings filter.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: page /results in the browser up to 10,000 rows, with a notice when capped; no new endpoint.
  • (b) a server-side GET /results.csv streaming the whole filter; unbounded, and a second representation to keep defused.
  • (c) export the loaded rows only.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-18): (a).

OQ7. Remediation-gated panels before IMPL-0030.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: render them with an empty state decided from Status.apps; the layout is final and nothing moves when remediation lands.
  • (b) hide them until a remediate App exists; a sparser page that changes shape on upgrade.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-18): (a).

OQ8. Where a findings row goes.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: the finding drawer, deep-linked with ?open=, as the mockup and DESIGN-0036 OQ9 drew it; triage stays on one page with its filters, and Re-evaluate sits next to the evidence.
  • (b) navigate to the repository page's Controls tab; no drawer to build, but every row is a page load and the filter context is lost.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-18): (a).

OQ9. The ⌘K command palette.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: bring it back (ui/command.tsx survived) over /repositories?q=, controls and orgs; the mockup draws it and the fleet is too big to reach a repository by browsing.
  • (b) leave it out; the /repositories search covers the need.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-18): (a).

OQ10. How the mockup catches up.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: update the one mockup in place to the controls line and this design's pages; one reference, as DESIGN-0036 OQ17 chose.
  • (b) a new controls mockup beside it, the findings-era one archived; a clean start, two files to explain.
  • (c) stop maintaining a mockup; the design docs and e2e screenshots are the reference.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-18): (a), with the mockup updated inside this design's pull request rather than in an IMPL phase: the mockup is what specifies the UI, so it is accepted together with the design, before any implementation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The v2 line has shipped sixteen release candidates from the v2 branch and is running the controls model, remediation and the controls UI in the homelab. This design settles what has to happen for v2 to become main and ship v2.0.0: how the two branches converge, how the GA tag is produced so that a binary release, two registries and the chart all come out of one push, what the public docs site and the landing pages must say, and which of the IMPL-0030 soak gates still apply. It also closes the one operator-facing gap the audit found on the way: the API and UI are documented for Keycloak only, and three small assumptions in the code and the chart would trip an operator on Okta, Entra ID or Auth0. Part B makes the identity-provider contract explicit, adds the knobs those providers need, and ships recipes for each. Two further parts were added at review: Part C moves the public docs site off the drifted MkDocs copy onto a generator that renders what the docs actually contain (39 mermaid diagrams render as code today), and Part D evaluates the repository's supply-chain security (scanners, signing, SBOMs, provenance, pinning, branch rules) and tiers the gaps into what GA needs and what follows.

The design is planning only. It produces four IMPLs: Part B (small, additive, shipped as an rc before GA), the GA cutover (Part A with Part D's first tier as a phase), the docs site (Part C, after GA), and supply-chain hardening (Part D's remaining tiers, after GA). See OQ1, OQ14 and OQ19.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• v2 becomes main through pull requests the main ruleset allows, with every rc tag still reachable and no history rewritten.
  • One v2.0.0 release: a signed goreleaser release, images on GHCR and ECR with SLSA provenance, the UI image, and the chart, all from one push to main, with jobs that visibly run (the June 2026 startup_failure post-mortem).
  • The public docs site publishes the v2 pages the moment main is v2; no page a new user reaches describes the v1 engine as current.
  • The soak gates IMPL-0030 set for GA are honoured, not re-derived.
  • An operator can run the API and UI against Okta, Entra ID or Auth0 from the docs alone, and the code and chart no longer assume Keycloak where they do today.
  • Every mechanical "v2 branch entry" (CI triggers, chart-testing target, CLAUDE.md rule 6) is listed with what changes at GA.
  • The public docs site is built from the same docs/ tree as TechDocs, renders mermaid, and is deployed from an Actions artefact rather than a long-lived gh-pages branch.
  • Every release artefact (binaries, two images, chart) carries a signature, provenance and an SBOM a consumer can verify from one documented page; the repository's scanners cover Go, TypeScript, containers, the chart and the workflows; and a red check blocks a merge.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• An in-place upgrade from 1.x or from the pre-controls rcs. DESIGN-0032 D27 made 2.0 a fresh install; docs/operations/v2-migration.md is the runbook and this design only fixes its contradictions.
  • Supporting providers whose access tokens are not JWTs (Google) other than through a broker, or ID-token authentication at the API.
  • Nested group-claim paths (realm_access.roles); see OQ9.
  • IMPL-0026 (Temporal credential reload, OpenBao certificates) and DESIGN-0034 (CODEOWNERS ownership) stay post-GA, as IMPL-0030 recorded.
  • A Go module path change to /v2; see OQ11.
  • Changing the authorization model (groups → orgs, defaultOrgs, clients). It is provider-neutral already; only the claim it reads the client from is made configurable.

docs.title: Where the two branches stand
docs.text:
As of 2026-10-24, v2 is at 517f0cd (chart and appVersion 2.0.0-rc.16, PR #239) and main is at 1a825c0 (v1.14.1). The merge-base is 5bd96bb. main carries five commits v2 does not:

Commit PR What it is Needed on v2 because 1cbac0c #203 tools/rgctl, DESIGN-0035, IMPL-0027 v2-migration.md steps 3 and 6 run rgctl prs list / prs close; the tool is untracked on v2 0c89424 #227 Go 1.26.9, x/text v0.42.0 superseded by #229 and v2's own bumps; merges clean b3c7785 #225 docs/operations/rgctl.md the runbook links it 93c21ba #228 release.yml base-branch: true without it the bump reads every tag in the repository; that is how #227's patch label cut a v2.0.0 from v1 code 1a825c0 #229 Go 1.26.10 v2 already has it (c65d66c); merges clean

The main ruleset requires a pull request and forbids deletion and non-fast-forward pushes, with no bypass actors. git push origin v2:main is refused, so IMPL-0030 OQ12's "fast-forward main to v2" cannot be done literally; it has to be a pull request, and the merge method matters (A1).

The bogus v2.0.0 from #227 has been deleted: the remote has v2.0.0-rc.1 through rc.16 only and gh release view v2.0.0 is "release not found".

docs.title: What IMPL-0030 already decided
docs.text:
IMPL-0030 owns the cutover's operational half. Its decisions stand and this design builds on them rather than reopening them:

  • Phase 9 (9.1–9.10): tag the remediation rc, create the Apps, stop the old writers, delete the old schedules, record the old PRs with rgctl, install fresh, verify evaluation and KEDA, remediate one org, then the rest, keep the old databases. All human-run, none ticked.
  • OQ7: donaldgifford in remediate for 7 days with every hold explained, then the remaining orgs, then GA after 7 more days with no unexplained conflict, foreign_branch or permission hold.
  • OQ8: old databases kept until 2.0.0 has run 14 days.
  • OQ12: tag v2.0.0 on main after converging, dont-release on the merge PR, tag pushed by hand. A2 shows that the hand-pushed tag publishes only the chart and proposes a revision (OQ2).
  • Phase 10: chart 2.0.0, changelogs regenerated, in-place homelab upgrade from the rc, docz statuses, memory.

docs.title: What the readiness audit found
docs.text:
A read-only audit of the tree on 2026-10-24 found four things that would break or mislead if v2 were flipped today, plus a set of smaller items. In order of blast radius:

  1. No workflow produces the v2.0.0 binary release as planned. release.yml runs goreleaser only off the semver bump; with dont-release the bump is skipped, the release job is skipped, and publish-ghcr/publish-ecr run with an empty tag, so their image jobs are gated off. prerelease.yml matches v*-* only. The only workflow a hand-pushed v2.0.0 tag triggers is changelog-update.yml.
  2. The public docs site would publish v1. gh-pages.yml deploys mkdocs-ghpages.yml on every push to main. That file's nav has Getting Started and Policy Reference under Usage, DESIGN/IMPL entries up to 0009 and no Operations section; none of controls-reference, ui, api, v2-* is in it. mkdocs.yml (the TechDocs config) has them all.
  3. The landing pages describe v1. README.md, docs/index.md, docs/usage/getting-started.md, docs/ADDING_RULES.md, docs/operations/{aws,scaling,ent-setup}.md and the chart README's introduction still describe reconcilers, guardian.hcl, Valkey, watch = true and chart values the 2.x chart fails the render on.
  4. v2-migration.md contradicts itself on RECONCILE_FRESHNESS (read by migrate at line 225; "none" at 271) and migrate.freshness (a replacement at 236; removed at 295).

Smaller: changelog-update.yml does a full git-cliff regeneration on the tag push, which IMPL-0029 9.5 noted would drop the hand-written 1.x entries; the UI changelog gate needs a 2.0.0 entry beside the chart bump; IMPL-0028 is Draft with every task ticked, IMPL-0025's body says Draft while its frontmatter says Completed, DESIGN-0036 is Approved; #232 and #235 are fixed in code but open; the deploy/MIGRATED.md tombstone is due 2026-11-30; two Dependabot alerts on main are already fixed on v2.

docs.title: How the API and UI authenticate today
docs.text:
DESIGN-0027 specified a provider-neutral contract: the API takes an OIDC access token for its audience, reads a name claim and a groups claim, and maps groups to orgs in a YAML file. The implementation is faithful to that:

  • internal/api/authn.go: go-oidc discovery, RS256/ES256 only, iss equal to OIDC_ISSUER, aud containing OIDC_AUDIENCE (string or array), 60s skew on exp/nbf, refuses tokens carrying nonce, at_hash or typ: ID, then reads OIDC_NAME_CLAIM (default preferred_username) and OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM (default groups) as top-level keys. Claims.Client is read from azp and nothing else.
  • internal/api/authz.go: groups → orgs, defaultOrgs, and clients keyed on that azp for IdPs that put no groups on client-credentials tokens (DESIGN-0027 OQ22).
  • ui/server/: authorization code + PKCE S256 with state and nonce, scopes from OIDC_SCOPES (code default openid profile email offline_access), token endpoint authentication hard-coded to client_secret_post, no audience/resource parameter, access token forwarded to the API, refresh within 60s of expiry, RP-initiated logout when discovery advertises end_session_endpoint, revocation when it advertises revocation_endpoint.
  • Chart: api.auth.{issuer,audience,nameClaim,groupsClaim}, api.authz.*, ui.oidc.{clientId,scopes} with the scopes default [openid, profile, groups, offline_access] (which differs from the code default), ui.existingSecret. The UI's issuer is api.auth.issuer. values.schema.json declares api.auth.enabled, issuer, audience only.
  • Docs: the authentication rules in docs/usage/api.md are neutral; the only setup walkthrough is "Keycloak example", and docs/usage/ui.md points at it. Okta and Entra appear only in DESIGN-0027's diagram and in the Temporal client-credentials discussion (DESIGN-0028, INV-0020).

So the code is close to neutral. What would stop an Okta operator is a clients block that silently does nothing (Okta issues cid, not azp), an app that has to be switched to client_secret_post, a chart scope default (groups) that Okta's custom authorization servers reject as undefined, and no page telling them any of that. Auth0 adds one more: without an audience parameter it returns an opaque access token, which the API refuses as malformed. Google's access tokens are always opaque, so Google only works behind a broker.

docs.title: A1 Branch convergence
docs.text:
Two merges, both merge commits, both through pull requests:

gitGraph
  commit id: "5bd96bb (merge-base)"
  branch v2
  checkout main
  commit id: "#203 rgctl"
  commit id: "#227 #225 #228 #229"
  checkout v2
  commit id: "rc.12 … rc.15"
  commit id: "517f0cd rc.16" tag: "v2.0.0-rc.16"
  merge main id: "M1: main → v2 (sync PR)"
  commit id: "IMPL identity providers (rc.17)" tag: "v2.0.0-rc.17"
  commit id: "GA prep: chart 2.0.0, docs, reverts"
  checkout main
  merge v2 id: "M2: v2 → main (merge commit, labelled)" tag: "v2.0.0"

M1, main into v2. A sync PR against v2 that brings rgctl, the rgctl runbook and the base-branch: true guard. Conflicts are expected only in release.yml (keep the guard) and go.mod/go.sum (keep v2's newer versions). After M1, v2 is a superset of main and the final merge is conflict-free by construction.

M2, v2 into main. A PR against main, merged with the merge commit method. Squash would collapse the whole v2 history into one commit and leave every rc tag pointing at commits no longer reachable from main; rebase would rewrite them. A merge commit keeps the rc tags reachable, which A2 depends on, and keeps git log main honest about what shipped in each rc. The repository's default merge method for feature PRs is squash; M2 is the one PR where the maintainer picks "Create a merge commit" by hand (D1).

Everything that must be true of main at GA (chart 2.0.0, the docs rewrite, the branch-entry reverts, the 2.0.0 changelog entry) lands on v2 before M2, in the GA-prep PR, so that M2 carries a tree that is already GA-shaped and the push to main can be the release.

docs.title: A2 The release mechanism
docs.text:
The pipeline on main is release.yml: bump-version (jefflinse/pr-semver-bump, mode bump) reads the merged PR's labels, tags, and hands the tag to release (goreleaser) and to ghcr.yml / ecr.yml (image, UI image, chart, three SLSA jobs each). The action chooses the version to bump from by parsing every tag as semver (loose, so pre-releases parse), sorting descending, and with base-branch: true taking the newest one whose commit is reachable from the base branch; annotated tags are dereferenced.

After M2, the newest tag reachable from main is v2.0.0-rc.16 (or rc.17, see A1), because the rc tags point at v2 commits that the merge commit makes reachable. node-semver's increment rules for a pre-release of 2.0.0 are:

Label on the merge PR semver.inc("2.0.0-rc.N", …) major 2.0.0 minor 2.0.0 patch 2.0.0

So a labelled M2 produces exactly v2.0.0, and the whole pipeline designed for 1.x releases runs: goreleaser builds and signs the binaries and creates the GitHub release; ghcr.yml and ecr.yml receive tag: v2.0.0, build and push both images with latest and 2.0 tags (!contains(tag, '-')), publish the chart, and attach SLSA provenance to all three. Nothing is pushed by hand.

This revises IMPL-0030 OQ12(a) (dont-release + hand tag), which would have left release skipped and both image jobs gated off; the hand tag would have triggered only changelog-update.yml. The label is major (OQ2), because that is what the release is, and because major is the only label whose semantics survive if the rc tags were ever unreachable (a minor or patch from 1.14.1 would cut 1.15.0 or 1.14.2, silently, from v2 code). The pre-merge checklist therefore includes: git tag --merged <M2 head> shows v2.0.0-rc.16; no v2.0.0 tag or release exists; release.yml on the merge head has base-branch: true; the PR carries exactly one semver label.

sequenceDiagram
  participant PR as M2 merge (label: major)
  participant R as release.yml
  participant B as bump-version
  participant G as goreleaser
  participant P as ghcr.yml / ecr.yml
  PR->>R: push to main
  R->>B: pr-semver-bump (base-branch: true)
  B-->>B: newest reachable tag = v2.0.0-rc.N
  B-->>R: tag v2.0.0
  R->>G: release --clean @ v2.0.0 (GPG-signed)
  R->>P: tag=v2.0.0
  P-->>P: image, ui-image, chart + SLSA ×3; latest & 2.0 tags
  P-->>R: digests

Two guards from the release post-mortem carry over unchanged: confirm the push-triggered run creates jobs (a startup_failure has none and is only visible on the run's web page), and read digests from the expression layer, never from a shell-inlined metadata blob.

prerelease.yml keeps working for future vX.Y.Z-rc.N tags on main: the v*-* filter does not match v2.0.0 and the file is harmless on main. Its comment ("lives on v2 until v2.0.0") is updated (A6).

docs.title: A3 The public docs site
docs.text:
mkdocs.yml and mkdocs-ghpages.yml differ only in that the TechDocs config has exclude_docs and plugins, and the GitHub Pages config has theme: material; their navs have drifted because docz updates only mkdocs.yml. The fix is one source of truth: mkdocs-ghpages.yml becomes

INHERIT: mkdocs.yml
theme:
  name: material

so the nav docz maintains is the nav the public site deploys, and the Pages-specific theme stays where it is (D2). make lint-docs (or the existing docs job) gains mkdocs build --strict --config-file mkdocs-ghpages.yml so a broken inherit or a nav entry pointing at a deleted page fails CI instead of the deploy. OQ3 offers deleting the second file instead.

The nav itself is reorganised in the same PR: Usage leads with the v2 pages (Getting Started rewritten, Policy reference, Control-type reference, UI, API, the identity-provider page from Part B), Operations gets a section (v2 overview, onboarding, migration, rgctl, ingress, monitoring generation, scaling, ECR publish, AWS), and the pre-v2 pages that remain useful as history are grouped under a "Historical (1.x)" heading rather than deleted (A4).

docs.title: A4 The documentation rewrite
docs.text:
The rule for every page is: a new reader must not be able to reach a page that presents the v1 engine as the current product without the page saying so in its first paragraph. Three dispositions:

Page Disposition Notes README.md Rewrite Two Apps, controls and policy root, evaluate/remediate, Temporal + Postgres, UI/API; chart install at 2.0.0; architecture diagram from docs/operations/v2-overview.md docs/index.md Rewrite Mirror the README's opening; link v2 overview, onboarding, UI, API docs/usage/getting-started.md Rewrite Fresh install walk: Apps, policy root, chart values, first evaluation, turning on remediation per org docs/ADDING_RULES.md Replace Becomes "Adding a control type": controls/builtin, Semantics(), TestRevisionGolden, repo-guardian controls docs; the old content moves under Historical docs/operations/aws.md Rewrite sections Drop ElastiCache/Valkey; RDS for the controls database with rg_evaluator/rg_remediator; Temporal is the operator's docs/operations/scaling.md Rewrite sections Drop staleSweep.*/queue.valkey.*; KEDA per queue, evaluator.*/remediator.*, pool sizing; keep the posture/max by section docs/operations/ent-setup.md Rewrite sections Two Apps with policy-derived permissions (registerRemediation logs them); webhook URLs per App charts/repo-guardian/README.md.gotmpl Rewrite intro Never the rendered README (IMPL-0012 post-mortem) docs/operations/v2-migration.md Fix RECONCILE_FRESHNESS → "none"; staleSweep.freshness → EVAL_INTERVAL, drop migrate.freshness as a replacement docs/operations/{absent-rules,annotation-properties,chart-0.5.0,pr-convergence,template}-migration.md, custom-properties-security-fix.md, delayed-requeue-runbook.md, property-name-charset.md, compliance-reports.md Mark historical One admonition at the top: "1.x only; v2 has no equivalent" with the v2 pointer where one exists docs/overview.html, docs/design/*.html Leave Design artefacts, already dated deploy/MIGRATED.md Delete at GA Its own tombstone date is 2026-11-30; GA is after that or close enough that the fresh-install rule makes it moot (OQ10)

CLAUDE.md's v1 sections ("Key design patterns" through the IMPL-0023 entries) are already labelled historical by the controls paragraph and stay; they are for Claude, not for users.

docs.title: A5 Changelogs
docs.text:
Three changelogs, three rules:

  • ui/CHANGELOG.yaml: the GA-prep PR adds the 2.0.0 entry at the top (summary: the controls line, remediation, the UI; tags new, breaking, fleet, findings, policy, ui, api, chart) and regenerates changelog.json. check:changelog already enforces this against Chart.yaml.
  • Root CHANGELOG.md: changelog-update.yml currently runs git-cliff --output CHANGELOG.md, a full regeneration that would replace the hand-curated 1.x entries. It changes to git-cliff --latest --prepend CHANGELOG.md (header suppressed when prepending) so each tag adds its own section above the existing file, and the dont-release/chore PR it opens stays reviewable (D3). The 2.0.0 section is generated once from v1.14.1..v2.0.0; the rc sections already in the file stay as history.
  • Chart CHANGELOG.md: regenerated by the publish workflow before helm package, unchanged.

docs.title: A6 The v2 branch entries
docs.text:
CLAUDE.md says "at v2.0.0 v2 fast-forwards main and the v2 branch entries are reverted". Concretely:

File Today At GA .github/workflows/ci.yml branches: [main, v2] [main] .github/workflows/license-check.yml [main, v2] [main] .github/workflows/security.yml [main, v2] + a pull_request trigger main lacks [main]; keep the pull_request trigger ct.yaml target-branch: v2 main .github/workflows/prerelease.yml "lives on v2 until v2.0.0" keep; reword the comment: hand-cut -rc tags on main .github/workflows/changelog-update.yml ref input "main or v2"; comment about rc tags on v2 input default main only; comment reworded; --prepend per A5 .github/workflows/release.yml base-branch: true on main only present on v2 after M1; unchanged at GA docker-bake.hcl, ghcr.yml, ecr.yml latest gated on no - unchanged; this is what moves latest at GA CLAUDE.md §"The v2 branch (IMPL-0025)" describes the rc flow replaced by a short "Release line" paragraph: rc tags by hand with dont-release and prerelease.yml, GA releases by label CLAUDE.md rule 6 dont-release for rcs unchanged in substance; add "a GA release is cut by its semver label, never a hand tag" cliff.toml, renovate.json5, labeler.yml, CODEOWNERS, dependabot.yml, .goreleaser.yml no v2 references unchanged

After GA the v2 branch is deleted once the IMPL records the ship; any branch protection on it goes with it.

docs.title: A7 The soak gate and the homelab tasks
docs.text:
This design adds no gate and removes none. The GA clock is IMPL-0030 OQ7, and the state of its inputs is:

flowchart LR
  A["rc.16 running<br/>(2026-10-23)"] --> B["IMPL-0030 9.7<br/>evaluation verified"]
  B --> C["9.8 donaldgifford<br/>mode = remediate"]
  C -->|7 days, holds explained,<br/>no PR over the cap| D["9.9 remaining orgs"]
  D -->|7 days, no unexplained<br/>conflict / foreign_branch / permission| E["GA: M2 labelled major"]
  E --> F["10.3 homelab in place<br/>rc → 2.0.0"]
  F -->|14 days| G["OQ8: archive and drop<br/>the old databases"]

The unchecked human tasks that feed it, gathered from the four IMPLs so the GA IMPL can list them once: IMPL-0030 9.1–9.10 and 10.3; IMPL-0029 8.9 (Keycloak group split), 9.7 (fresh evaluate-only install), 9.8 (posture comparison); IMPL-0031 8.3 and IMPL-0032 9.2–9.3 (the UI walk and the group split on /results, /remediations and the tree). IMPL-0032 9.1 is done in substance (rc.16 from #239) and is ticked by the GA IMPL. The group-split checks collapse into one item that B6's verification procedure covers.

docs.title: A8 Bookkeeping at GA
docs.text:
• docz statuses: DESIGN-0029, 0030, 0031, 0032 → Implemented; DESIGN-0036 → Implemented; IMPL-0028, 0029, 0030, 0031, 0032 → Completed (IMPL-0025 body line fixed to match its frontmatter); DESIGN-0034 and IMPL-0026 stay Draft by IMPL-0030's decision; this design → Implemented.
  • Issues: close #232 and #235 after the homelab confirms the fixes; close #199, #200 and #73 as "v1 only, component removed in 2.0".
  • internal/controls/file/file.go:331 FIX: (quadratic duplicate-key check) is a real repository-controlled cost; the GA IMPL carries it as a should-fix, not a gate.
  • Memory and CLAUDE.md: record the ship date; move the "v2 branch" memories to history.

docs.title: A9 Consequences of latest moving
docs.text: latest is 1.14.1 today. The GA publish retags it to 2.0.0 and adds 2.0. Anyone running repo-guardian:latest gets a release that is a fresh install only, with a new chart major that fails the render on every 1.x value. The chart defaults the image tag to appVersion, so chart users are unaffected unless they pinned image.tag: latest. No repository doc points at :latest. The release notes and the rewritten README say so in their first lines, and the 1.14 line stays available under its own tags. No code change.

docs.title: B1 The identity-provider contract
docs.text:
This is the page an operator reads before touching their IdP. It states what the API and UI require and nothing about any one product. It becomes docs/operations/identity-provider.md (D4), linked from api.md, ui.md, v2-onboarding.md and the chart README.

Requirement API UI (BFF) Why OIDC discovery at the issuer URL reads jwks_uri reads authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, optional end_session_endpoint, revocation_endpoint both use discovery, nothing is hand-configured Access tokens are JWTs signed RS256 or ES256 verifies forwards the API never calls an introspection endpoint iss equals the configured issuer exactly checks — trailing slash and v1/v2 endpoint variants matter aud contains the API audience checks — the IdP must put the API's audience on the UI client's tokens A groups claim as a top-level key, array or string reads OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM — nested paths are out of scope (OQ9) A name claim (any string claim) reads OIDC_NAME_CLAIM display name from the ID token: name, preferred_username, email, sub logs and /me A client claim on machine tokens reads OIDC_CLIENT_CLAIM (new) — api.authz.clients; the claim name differs per provider Authorization code + PKCE S256 for a confidential client — always the BFF holds the secret; the browser holds only the session cookie Token endpoint authentication method — client_secret_post or client_secret_basic (new) providers default differently Refresh tokens on the UI client — offline_access or the provider's equivalent the session is 8h; access tokens are shorter Redirect URI <public URL>/auth/callback; post-logout <public URL>/ — fixed must be registered on the client Optional audience/resource at authorize time — OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_PARAMS (new) Auth0 returns opaque tokens without it No ID tokens at the API refuses nonce, at_hash, typ: ID sends the access token only DESIGN-0027

docs.title: B2 The token flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Br as Browser
  participant BFF as UI BFF (Bun/Hono)
  participant IdP as Identity provider
  participant API as repo-guardian api
  Br->>BFF: GET /auth/login
  BFF-->>Br: 302 authorize (PKCE S256, state, nonce, scopes, [audience])
  Br->>IdP: authenticate
  IdP-->>Br: 302 /auth/callback?code
  Br->>BFF: GET /auth/callback
  BFF->>IdP: POST token (code, verifier; client_secret_post | client_secret_basic)
  IdP-->>BFF: access token (JWT, aud = API), refresh token, ID token
  BFF-->>Br: Set-Cookie __Host-rg_session (sealed)
  Br->>BFF: GET /api/v1/…
  BFF->>API: Authorization: Bearer <access token>
  API->>IdP: JWKS (cached by go-oidc)
  API-->>API: iss, aud, alg, exp/nbf, not an ID token; name, groups, client claims
  API-->>BFF: scoped response (groups → orgs)
  BFF-->>Br: response

Nothing in the flow changes for Keycloak; steps 2 and 6 gain the two optional knobs and step 13 reads the client claim by name.

docs.title: B3 Code changes
docs.text:
B3.1 The client claim (internal/api). AuthnConfig gains ClientClaim string; config/api.go reads OIDC_CLIENT_CLAIM (default azp); verify sets Claims.Client from all[a.cfg.ClientClaim] via stringClaim instead of the typed AZP field, which is removed from tokenClaims. The chart exposes it as api.auth.clientClaim. The existing clients semantics and the "never map the UI's client ID" warning are unchanged; the warning is generalised to "whatever claim names the client, every user token from the UI carries the UI's client in it". A single configured name is chosen over an ordered fallback list (azp, client_id, cid, appid) because it matches nameClaim/groupsClaim, is explicit in the authz file's threat model, and cannot surprise an operator whose provider emits two of those claims with different values (OQ4).

B3.2 The ID-token check. isIDToken is unchanged in behaviour; its comment and the api.md bullet stop naming Keycloak: "a typ claim of ID, which some providers put in the payload".

B3.3 Token endpoint authentication (ui/server). OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD with values client_secret_post (default, today's behaviour) and client_secret_basic; oidc.ts picks client.ClientSecretPost or client.ClientSecretBasic accordingly. Config validation rejects anything else. The default stays post so rc deployments do not change behaviour on upgrade (OQ5).

B3.4 Extra authorization parameters (ui/server). OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_PARAMS, a JSON object of string → string, merged into buildAuthorizationUrl's parameters after the fixed ones (redirect_uri, scope, code_challenge*, state, nonce), which cannot be overridden: validation refuses those keys. Chart value ui.oidc.authorizationParams: {}. This covers Auth0's audience, RFC 8707 resource, Entra's domain_hint/prompt, and anything a future provider wants, without a knob per parameter (OQ6).

B3.5 Scopes. No code change; defaultScopes in config.ts stays openid profile email offline_access. The chart default moves to match it (B4).

B3.6 Test fixtures. internal/api/oidctest gains token shapes for Okta (cid, scp, uid, no azp, aud as a string), Entra (roles, GUID groups, appid), and a namespaced groups claim (https://example.com/groups); TestAuthn_* table cases drive each through verify with the matching ClientClaim/GroupsClaim and assert Claims.Client and Claims.Groups. The e2e mock issuer keeps its Keycloak-shaped token and gains a TOKEN_AUTH=basic option so the client_secret_basic path has one end-to-end run.

docs.title: B4 Chart changes
docs.text:
Value Change api.auth.nameClaim, api.auth.groupsClaim declared in values.schema.json (they are rendered today but unschema'd, so a typo is silent) api.auth.clientClaim new, default azp, schema'd, rendered as OIDC_CLIENT_CLAIM api.authz.clients comment "by the claim api.auth.clientClaim names" ui.oidc.scopes default [openid, profile, email, offline_access], matching the BFF; the Keycloak recipe notes that the audience and group mappers do not need a groups scope (OQ7) ui.oidc.tokenAuthMethod new, enum client_secret_post / client_secret_basic, default client_secret_post, rendered as OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD ui.oidc.authorizationParams new map, default {}, rendered as OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_PARAMS JSON; schema forbids the reserved keys validateUI refuses authorizationParams naming redirect_uri, scope, state, nonce, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, response_type, client_id

helm-unittest cases: each new value renders to its env var; the reserved-key refusal fails the render naming the key; the one existing assertion of the scopes default string (tests/ui_test.yaml, OIDC_SCOPES) is updated to the new default.

docs.title: B5 Provider recipes
docs.text:
Each recipe in identity-provider.md has the same five headings (issuer and audience, UI client, groups, machine clients, chart values) so an operator can diff them. The content, as the audit established it:

Keycloak (moved from api.md, unchanged): API client as audience, UI confidential client with PKCE and the two redirect URIs, Audience mapper, Group Membership mapper with full path off, service-account clients mapped by azp. Issuer https://<host>/realms/<realm>.

Okta: a custom authorization server (API Access Management) is required; tokens from the org authorization server cannot be validated by third parties. Issuer https://<org>.okta.com/oauth2/<server id>, audience the server's audience (api://default or a chosen one). Add a groups claim to access tokens on that server (filter by group); group names are the api.authz.groups keys. UI app: web app, authorization code, refresh tokens on, client authentication client_secret_post (or set ui.oidc.tokenAuthMethod: client_secret_basic), redirect and sign-out URIs registered. Scopes: the chart default; do not add groups unless the server defines it. api.auth.nameClaim: Okta access tokens carry sub and uid, not preferred_username; set sub or add a custom claim. Machine clients: api.auth.clientClaim: cid, or a groups claim on client-credentials tokens.

Entra ID: app registrations for the API (expose a scope, set accessTokenAcceptedVersion: 2 so iss matches the v2 discovery document) and the UI (web platform, redirect URIs, client secret). Issuer https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0, audience the API app's client ID (or api://<id>). Put the API scope in ui.oidc.scopes so the access token is for the API. Groups arrive as object-ID GUIDs; keys in api.authz.groups are GUIDs, or use app roles with groupsClaim: roles. More than 200 groups produces an overage claim and no groups, which falls to defaultOrgs; document it. Machine clients: clientClaim: azp works on v2 tokens. Many groups inflate three tokens in the session cookie; the ten-chunk limit in session.ts is the ceiling and is documented, not raised.

Auth0: issuer https://<tenant>.<region>.auth0.com/ (trailing slash), an API registered with an identifier that becomes the audience, ui.oidc.authorizationParams: {audience: <identifier>} so the access token is a JWT, a post-login Action adding a namespaced groups claim (https://example.com/groups) set as groupsClaim, RP-initiated logout enabled on the tenant for end_session_endpoint, offline_access enabled on the API. Machine clients: clientClaim: azp (Auth0 sets it).

Google: not supported directly; its access tokens are opaque. Use a broker (Keycloak, Dex, Auth0, Okta) federating to Google and follow that broker's recipe.

docs.title: B6 Verifying a provider
docs.text: GET /me already returns the caller's name, groups and visible orgs as the API resolved them; the recipe page ends with a procedure: sign in, open /me through the UI, confirm groups and orgs; then repo_guardian_api_auth_failures_total{reason} for refusals (issuer, audience, algorithm, id_token, signature, expired), each mapped to the recipe step that fixes it. The same procedure is IMPL-0029 8.9 / IMPL-0032 9.3's "group split" check, so the GA IMPL points there instead of restating it. No new endpoint.

docs.title: Part C: the public docs site
C1 Two consumers, one source
docs.text:
docs/ has two readers. Backstage TechDocs builds mkdocs.yml with the techdocs-core plugin (catalog-info.yaml points at dir:.), and that cannot change: TechDocs is MkDocs. The public site at donaldgifford.github.io/repo-guardian is built by gh-pages.yml on every push to main from mkdocs-ghpages.yml, with an unpinned pip install mkdocs-material, committed to the gh-pages branch and served with the Pages "legacy" build type. The two configs have drifted (A3), and neither enables pymdownx.superfences with a mermaid fence, so the 39 mermaid blocks in 15 documents render as code on the public site today. The Pages build is also the only @latest Python install in the repository.

flowchart LR
  D["docs/ (122 .md, docz frontmatter,<br/>39 mermaid blocks, 473 relative .md links)"]
  D --> M["mkdocs.yml + techdocs-core<br/>(Backstage TechDocs, unchanged)"]
  D --> G["mkdocs-ghpages.yml<br/>(today: drifted nav, no mermaid,<br/>gh-pages branch, legacy Pages)"]
  D -. "Part C" .-> S["site/ Astro Starlight<br/>(bun, mermaid at build,<br/>Pagefind, Actions → Pages)"]
  G -. "retired by C5" .-> S

docs.title: C2 What the move has to carry
docs.text:
Measured against the tree on 2026-10-25:

Property Count Consequence for a generator Markdown pages 122 all must build, with docs/README.md excluded as today Pages with a frontmatter title 87 of 122 Starlight requires title; the 35 without it are the docz section READMEs, index.md, ADDING_RULES.md, every docs/operations/*.md and every docs/usage/*.md; usage/controls-reference.md is generated by repo-guardian controls docs, so the generator must emit it Mermaid blocks 39 in 15 files must render at build time or on the client Relative .md links 473 MkDocs rewrites them to routes; Astro does not, so a remark/rehype link-rewrite plugin and a link validator are required docz <!--toc:start--> blocks 76 plain lists; render anywhere; the right-hand page TOC duplicates them, acceptable MkDocs admonitions (!!!) 1 file (operations/migrations.md) rewrite as a Starlight aside (:::note) or plain text Raw HTML in markdown 14 files (<details>, <br>, tables) fine in .md content; no MDX needed Standalone HTML artefacts docs/overview.html, two docs/design/*.html copied through public/ so their URLs survive Images 1 (usage/img/ui/status.png) relative image paths resolve from the page

docs.title: C3 Generator comparison
docs.text:
Astro Starlight Zensical Hugo MkDocs Material (fixed) Toolchain already in the repo yes: bun 1.3.14 via mise, the UI is Astro's ecosystem (Vite, TS) no: Python, like today no: Go binary, but the maintainer has Hugo experience yes: Python in CI only Mermaid plugin (rehype-mermaid at build time, Playwright already pinned; or client-side) native shortcode or client-side script enable pymdownx.superfences custom fence Relative .md links plugin + starlight-links-validator native needs render-link hook or plugin native Search Pagefind, built in, static built in needs Pagefind or similar built in Frontmatter title required yes (35 pages to add) no no (falls back) no Versioned docs starlight-versions plugin not yet manual mike Theming and components first-class, TS, shadcn-adjacent look achievable to match the UI Material look Theme-dependent Material look Maturity 1.x, large community new (late 2025), MkDocs-config compatible, from the Material team mature mature Config drift risk with TechDocs separate config by design; nav from the directory tree plus a sidebar config could share mkdocs.yml separate the A3 inherit removes it

Starlight is the recommendation (OQ13): it runs on the toolchain the UI already pins, gives the docs the same visual family as the product, renders mermaid at build time with the Playwright image the UI tests already use, and has a search that needs no service. Its two costs are real but bounded: 35 titles (one docz-style frontmatter block each, plus a one-line change to controls docs) and the link-rewrite plugin. Zensical is the cheapest move and keeps one config for both consumers, but it is months old and the user's stated preference is to leave the MkDocs line. Fixing MkDocs Material in place (mermaid fence, pinned install) is the fallback if the Starlight IMPL slips, and A3's inherit already does the drift half of it.

docs.title: C4 The Astro Starlight shape
docs.text:
• Location site/ at the repository root, a bun workspace separate from ui/ (different dependency set, different release cadence), with make docs-build, make docs-dev, make lint-docs (strict build + links validator) in the single Makefile.
  • Content site/src/content/docs is a symlink to ../../../docs, which Astro's content layer follows; docs/README.md is excluded by the loader pattern as exclude_docs excludes it today. No markdown moves; TechDocs keeps reading the same files.
  • Sidebar generated from the directory tree with per-section ordering (Usage, Operations, Design, Implementation Plans, Investigations, ADRs, RFCs, Historical (1.x) per A4/OQ12), so adding a docz document needs no nav edit; mkdocs.yml keeps docz's nav for TechDocs.
  • Markdown a remark plugin rewrites relative .md links to routes; starlight-links-validator fails the build on a dead one; rehype-mermaid renders diagrams to SVG at build time (client-side mermaid is the fallback if the headless browser is a CI cost); the one admonition becomes an aside.
  • Frontmatter docz templates already emit title; the 35 pages get one; repo-guardian controls docs emits a title line and make lint-controls-docs keeps it.
  • Deploy gh-pages.yml becomes a bun build plus actions/upload-pages-artifact and actions/deploy-pages (Pages build type "workflow"); the gh-pages branch is deleted once the first Actions deploy serves, and the CLAUDE.md note that gh-pages serves the docs is updated. The build runs on pull requests too (strict), so a broken link fails before merge.
  • Theme Starlight defaults with the UI's typeface and accent from DESIGN-0036; no custom components in the first cut.

docs.title: C5 Relationship to the GA cutover
docs.text: The Starlight site is its own IMPL after GA (OQ14). GA still needs the public site to publish v2 pages on the first push to main, and A3's inherit is a two-line change that does that, so it stays in the GA IMPL as the interim and is retired when the Starlight deploy serves. Whether the public site should carry a 1.14 snapshot as a version (starlight-versions) rather than a "Historical (1.x)" group is OQ15; the recommendation is no, because the 1.x pages are already marked and the 1.14 chart README is the 1.x reference consumers actually install from.
