docs.title: How the phases are ordered
docs.text:
New code lands alongside the rule engine first and is exercised by tests against the controls chain, not by the running rc binary. One phase then switches the binary over and deletes what it replaces, and the phases after it add what is new on top of the switched binary:

  1. Build (Phases 1–6): framework, policy, types, schema, workflows, then posture and monitoring. Each phase keeps make ci green. Nothing is registered on a worker or served by the API yet.
  2. Switch (Phase 7): register the controls workflows, delete the rule engine, the findings model, the rc schema code and the API endpoints and UI views that read them, and move the chart onto a policy directory.
  3. Add (Phases 8–9): the D32 API and UI views, docs, the rc and the homelab run.

The branch is not tagged between the start of Phase 1 and Phase 9; the last tagged rc is IMPL-0028's (or IMPL-0026's) and stays usable. Each phase ends with make lint and make test green plus the phase's own gates, one commit per numbered task, and its tests shown to be non-vacuous (neutralize the code, watch the test fail, restore).

The type-building order follows DESIGN-0031: codeowners first as the reference, then file, catalog_info, dependency_updates, then the API types. Policy resolution comes after the framework because the loader calls Type.Build.

docs.title: Phase 1: Control framework and the codeowners reference type
Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 1.1 Starting check: confirm the IMPL-0028 skeleton is on v2 (internal/control compiles with the Reader, PRObserver and Writer interfaces and their value types; the Writer implementation sits in its own package; PRConfig and PRTemplate live in internal/template; the depguard edges of DESIGN-0031 D17 are in .golangci.yml). List anything missing in this task and finish it here before 1.2. Done 2026-10-16. Present: Reader/PRObserver/Writer and their value types in internal/control (client.go), the Writer in internal/github/write, the writer and writer-evaluator-side depguard rules. Missing and finished here: PRConfig and PRTemplate moved to internal/template/pr.go (aliases stay in the old internal/policy until Phase 7 deletes it); depguard rules template-leaf, control-leaf, controls-types and controls-consumers (lax mode, so the package's own allow wins over the module-wide deny), and control, controls, policy added to the workflows rule. Probe: an import of store in control and in a controls/* type, of findings in template, of a control type in report, and of control in workflows each failed lint; removed. (A blank-import probe does not trip depguard: use a named import.)
  • [x] 1.2 Value types in internal/control/types.go, exactly as DESIGN-0031 § Supporting types: Definition, BuildEnv, TemplateSource, ID (with String() giving slug@N and ParseID), Resource, RuleKind, RuleID, RuleKindSpec, ParamSpec, Rule, RuleStatus and its five constants, RuleResult, ReadState, ResourceRead, Evaluation, RepoContext, EvalInput, RemediationInput, FileChange, APIChange, ChangeSet, WorkflowApply, and Status (compliant, non_compliant, unknown, not_applicable). One exported ValidSlug regexp (^[a-z][a-z0-9]*([_-][a-z0-9]+)*$) serves control slugs and rule ids. Done: also the Type and Control interfaces (Validate and the registry need them), Resource.String, the Kind* constants and ChangeSet.IsRecommendation; FileChange already existed in client.go. Status constants are Status* so they do not collide with the rule statuses. template.Vars is new: Common (.Owner, .Repo, .DefaultBranch) plus .Org and .Catalog, so the embedded templates render unchanged.
  • [x] 1.3 resource.go: Canonical(kind, key) (Resource, error). File keys go through path.Clean and are rejected when absolute, containing .. or an empty segment, or starting with ./, then compare byte for byte; label: keys are lower-cased; other kinds compare exactly; unknown kinds are an error. Table tests (.github/./CODEOWNERS equals .github/CODEOWNERS; ../x, /x, a//b rejected; Bug equals bug) and FuzzCanonicalFile (canonical output is a fixed point, and never escapes the root). Done: Canonical and MustCanonical (for keys fixed in code); . is rejected as naming the root. FuzzCanonicalFile ran 15.8M inputs in 20s with no failure.
  • [x] 1.4 validate.go: Validate(c, ev) (one result per declared rule; a missing result becomes error{reason=missing_result}; a result for an undeclared id or a duplicate fails as a bug; closed status enum; evidence is scalars and arrays only, at most 16 KiB per rule, with evidence_kind and evidence_version present) and StatusOf(ev) in the table's order. Tests: every row of the status table, unknown included; each Validate failure mode, including nested and oversized evidence. Done: Validate returns results in declared rule order and wraps every bug in ErrInvalidEvaluation; "flat" evidence is scalars and arrays of scalars. StatusOf with no results is unknown, so an empty evaluation never reads as compliant. FrameworkEvidence writes the framework's own missing_result.
  • [x] 1.5 revision.go and fingerprint.go: Revision(t, def, env) as sha256 over a canonical JSON encoding of id, version, type name, Semantics(), rules with parameters, apply, the template bytes and every referenced file's bytes, excluding title, description and pr {}; Fingerprint(revision, ev) over sorted (rule id, status) and sorted (resource, state, digest). Tests: title, description and pr {} edits leave the revision unchanged; a parameter, template byte, apply or Semantics change moves it; an API value moving between two wrong values moves the fingerprint with statuses unchanged; an absent property and a present null differ; evidence wording and ObservedAt do not move it. Done, both in revision.go. Rule numbers and titles are display-only and excluded with the definition title and pr {}; type-level Params are included. A type whose definitions reference other store files implements FileReferencer, and those bytes are hashed too.
  • [x] 1.6 changeset.go: ValidateChangeSet(c, ev, cs): unique canonical paths; every file and API resource within c.Owns(); at most 100 files and 1 MiB per file (or the limits the IMPL-0028 spike measured, as named constants citing it); regular files only, so a path the reader reported as a symlink or submodule must be in Blocked; every failing rule of ev in exactly one of Fixed, Manual, Blocked; every Manual and Blocked rule explained by a note. Table tests for each rejection. Done: MaxChangeSetFiles = 100 and MaxFileBytes = 1 MiB, citing spike 1. A symlink or submodule reaches the change set through the new ErrNotRegularFile sentinel, which the evaluation reader records as a read error with Err = NotRegularFile; writing that path is refused. Also refused: a rule named in two lists or undeclared, and a Fixed rule that is not failing. "Explained by a note" is at least one note per Manual and Blocked rule.
  • [x] 1.7 reader.go: NewEvalReader(base Reader, now func() time.Time) wraps the per-repository adapter (already pinned to one commit by IMPL-0028's constructor), caches every read for the evaluation, and records a ResourceRead per resource (file digest = blob SHA, API digest = sha256 of canonical JSON, ObservedAt for API reads, absent reads recorded too). Reads() returns them sorted. Tests: two controls reading one file make one underlying call; an error read is recorded with State = error; a 403 on one endpoint surfaces as ErrPermission for the caller to map to unknown{reason=permission}. Done: failed reads are cached too, so every control sees one answer. Files key on file:<canonical>, listings on tree:<path> (tree:. for the root, absent when empty), settings on one setting:<json name> per field (nil = absent), and rulesets, properties and labels per item; a failed list is one <kind>:* error read. The org schema is cached but not recorded (org-level). control.ErrPermission is produced by the GitHub adapter (classifyRead: a 403 that is not a throttle), which also returns ErrNotRegularFile for a symlink or submodule.
  • [x] 1.8 file.go: FileSpec, LocateFile (first location found wins; every location recorded, absent ones included), and the file-control adapter that turns a type's Parse, Check, Fix and Render into Evaluate and Remediate per DESIGN-0031's flowchart: absent → rules needing the file fail with file_missing and the template is rendered to Canonical; unparseable → unknown{parse_error} and every rule Blocked with a note; present → Check each rule, Fix the failing remediable ones at the found path, the rest Manual. A parser size cap is a required field of the adapter. Done: NewFileControl[M](FileControlConfig[M]) over a generic FileType[M] (Parse, Check, Fix returning the ids it fixed, Render); it refuses a missing MaxBytes, an empty or non-canonical FileSpec, a Canonical outside Locations, and a remediable rule with no template. LocateFile reads every location; a read error at or above the found one is returned, one below it ignored. Beyond the flowchart: an oversized file is unknown{file_too_large}, a 403 unknown{permission}, a symlink or submodule unknown{not_regular_file} and a transient read failure error{read_error}, all never written and every rule Blocked. A *ParseError puts its line in the evidence. A Fix that leaves the bytes unchanged fixes nothing (the rules go to Manual).
  • [x] 1.9 registry.go: Registry with Register, Type(name) and Build(def, env). Build fails on an unknown type, an unknown rule kind, a parameter not in RuleKindSpec or of the wrong type, a missing required parameter, a definition with no rules, remediate = true on a non-remediable kind, an apply value the type does not support (workflow without WorkflowApply), and a template whose render with the sample variables (org example-org, repository example) fails one of the control's remediable rules. Each error carries the definition's slug@N and rule id. Done: NewRegistry, Register (a duplicate name is an error), Type, Build. Build also refuses a rule id outside the slug grammar or declared twice, and an apply other than recommend/direct/workflow; an empty Kind defaults to the rule id. Parameter types accept what an HCL decode can produce ([]any/[]string, map[string]any/ map[string]string, any numeric kind). The template check remediates an in-memory empty repository with SampleVars, applies the files and re-evaluates; it runs only when the definition names a template.
  • [x] 1.10 controltest: Run(t, typ, fixtures) runs DESIGN-0031 properties 2–6 (remediation property, idempotence, minimal edits, template passes its rules, two rules failing together) against a FakeRepo that implements Reader from a map of files and API values, and an Apply(repo, cs) helper that applies file changes and an API overlay. A notes-only change set passes the property and is asserted to be a recommendation. Done: Fixture{Name, Def, Env, Repo, Vars, Want, WantFiles}; Run builds through a Registry, so every fixture also passes Build's checks. Property 4 is WantFiles byte-exact plus "no write that leaves a file unchanged"; property 6 fails the run when a type with two or more remediable kinds has no fixture failing two remediable rules at once. Idempotence means no writes and nothing in Fixed (a Manual rule keeps its note). FakeRepo serves NotRegular paths and per-read Errors; Apply overlays settings (by JSON name), properties, labels and rulesets. control.OpSet/OpDelete were added for APIChange.Op. Probe: a Fix that appends where it should prepend fails properties 2, 3 and 4.
  • [x] 1.11 internal/controls/codeowners: the type as DESIGN-0031's table (three locations, exists only, write the template to .github/CODEOWNERS when no location has a file, never edit an existing file), Semantics() = 1, the embedded fallback template sourced as the IMPL-0028 template spike decided, fixtures for no file, each location, a comment-only file and two files at once, the conformance suite, and a golden Revision. Done: the type looks its template up by name through BuildEnv.Templates, which Phase 2 builds as the policy root's templates/ over the embedded rules.TemplateStore (spike 7); the catalogue definition names codeowners (the embedded store's name; 2.3's template source also accepts codeowners.tmpl). The test reads the shipped internal/rules/templates/codeowners.tmpl from disk (depguard keeps rules out of a control type), so the conformance suite and the golden cover the real fallback: editing it moves the golden, as D20 intends. Parser cap 3 MiB (GitHub ignores a larger CODEOWNERS). Fixtures: no file, each location, comment-only, two files with the first comment-only (fails: GitHub uses the first), two files both valid.
  • [x] 1.12 Non-vacuous check: swap the fail/unknown order in StatusOf, drop the Owns() check from ValidateChangeSet, and make the reader skip its cache; confirm the matching tests fail; restore. Record the failing test names here. Done: fail/unknown swapped → TestStatusOf/any_fail, TestStatusOf/fail_outranks_unknown; Owns() check dropped → TestValidateChangeSet/file_not_owned; reader cache skipped → TestEvalReader_SharedFileIsOneCall, TestEvalReader_AbsentAndErrorReadsAreRecorded. All restored. Phase 1 close-out: internal/control coverage 89.6%, controltest 72.4%, codeowners 86.2%; go list shows internal/control, controltest and codeowners import only internal/control and internal/template of this module.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• internal/control imports only internal/template of this module, and depguard enforces every DESIGN-0031 D17 edge.
  • codeowners passes the conformance suite and its revision golden.
  • Coverage of internal/control is at least 85%; 1.12 shows the framework tests fail without the code they test.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 2.1 Free the package path (OQ1): git mv internal/policy internal/rulepolicy and rewrite its importers' import paths, nothing else. make ci green. Phase 7 deletes internal/rulepolicy. Done: the package keeps its name policy, so importers carry an explicit policy alias (goimports adds it); comments and docs that name internal/policy are left alone.
  • [x] 2.2 internal/policy/load.go: Load(root string, reg *control.Registry, logger *slog.Logger) (*Snapshot, error) over the DESIGN-0030 layout (catalogue/*.hcl, templates/, exactly one enterprise.hcl, orgs/*.hcl), using hclparse.NewParser(). Only literals and file() are allowed in expressions; every referenced file is resolved with filepath.EvalSymlinks and must stay under the root; each file is capped at 1 MiB. Errors carry file:line. No hot reload. Done: every file under the root is read once (walking ..data when it exists and skipping ..* names, per spike 7) and every one is containment-checked, so an escaping symlink fails load even when unreferenced. file() reads from that same in-memory set, so its bytes are hashed with the rest. "Literals and file() only" is enforced uniformly: every attribute of every HCL file is evaluated against an EvalContext holding file and no variables, before any decoder runs. Any HCL file outside enterprise.hcl, catalogue/*.hcl and orgs/*.hcl fails load.
  • [x] 2.3 catalogue.go: decode each control "<slug>" block into a control.Definition (version, type, title, description, rules with kind defaulting to the id only when the id names a kind the type declares, template, apply, pr {}, type parameters), build it through the registry with a BuildEnv whose template source is the policy root's templates/ plus the embedded fallbacks, and store its revision. Duplicate slug@version and slug or rule-id grammar violations fail load. Done: a control block's known attributes are version, type, title, description, template; any other attribute is a type parameter (Definition.Params), and in a rule block any attribute beyond number/title/kind/remediate is a rule parameter; unknown blocks fail. Values convert to the shapes ParamSpec checks (int64, float64, []any, map[string]any). control.Definition gained a display-only Description. A template name resolves to templates/<name>.tmpl, then templates/<name>, then the embedded rules.TemplateStore entry, and the embedded names used are kept for 2.9's version hash. pr {} titles and bodies are compiled at load. Registry errors are prefixed with the control block's file:line.
  • [x] 2.4 enterprise.go and org.go: decode enterprise.hcl (orgs, mode, controls, remediation { max_open_prs, reopen_after }, and a load error naming the block if an exclusion appears) and each orgs/<org>.hcl (mode, controls, replace "x@1" { with, reason }, exclude "x@1" { reason }, control "x@N" { mode }, exclude_repos { match, reason }, labelled repos blocks, remediation). An org file for an org not in enterprise.orgs fails load. Done: org names compare case-insensitively (GitHub logins), so ACME and acme are one org: a second policy for it fails, naming the first. An org file may hold more than one org block. controls, replace and exclude are kept as one operation list per layer, sorted by source position so 2.7 can apply them in file order (a controls list keeps its own order). Values (mode, max_open_prs, reopen_after, reasons) are decoded raw and checked in 2.5. The enterprise policy names each forbidden block (exclude, replace, exclude_repos, repos, control) in its error.
  • [x] 2.5 validate.go: every error and warning in DESIGN-0030's validation list, one table-test row each, asserting the message and the source location. Warnings go to the logger once at load. Done: errors are joined so one load reports all of them. A replace in a repos block is checked against the org layer's result plus every earlier block's additions, since which earlier blocks a repository meets is unknown at load. The ownership-collision rows are 2.6's (warnings, per this plan). "A repos block matches no known repository" needs discovery, so it is (*Snapshot).UnmatchedReposBlocks for the discovery path to log rather than a load-time warning.
  • [x] 2.6 ownership.go: the conservative load-time pairwise Owns() enumeration over every pair of definitions any org could assign together; overlaps are warnings naming both definitions and the resource, never errors (the runtime check in 2.7 is the authority). Done: per org, the layers are actually applied (org alone, org plus each repos block, org plus each pair of blocks in file order), so a replace removes its source and never warns against its replacement; an onboarded org with no file is checked against the baseline. Each (org, pair, resource) warns once, naming the org, and only when the policy has no errors.
  • [x] 2.7 resolve.go: (*Snapshot).Resolve(repo Repository, access AppAccess) Resolution implementing DESIGN-0030 steps 1–7, pure and with no API calls: policy state managed/excluded/unmanaged/ parked with reason; baseline, then the org file in file order, then each matching repos block in file order; one row per slug; requested mode by specificity; effective mode evaluate with mode_reason remediation_app_no_access or remediation_app_suspended when the Remediation App cannot write; the write set as the union of Owns(), with any overlap marking both assignments conflict with an error; ordinal, decision, baseline_control and source_block on each assignment; resolved MaxOpenPRs and ReopenAfter. Epochs are not assigned here; the store assigns them (4.5). Done: AppAccess{Evaluable, Remediable, RemediationSuspended}: the third field picks remediation_app_suspended over _no_access, which two booleans cannot tell apart. The checks run in the diagram's order: unmanaged, then exclude_repos, then layers; a parked repository keeps its assignments, with reason the stored park reason (else archived or fork). mode_source is the layer's source string, default when nothing declares a mode. Excluded rows carry their would-be modes. A conflict error names every claimant (a and b, a, b and c). Org names and match globs compare case-insensitively.
  • [x] 2.8 Resolution goldens: internal/policy/testdata/resolution/<case>/ each holding a policy directory, a repo.json input and an expected.json, run by one table test with -update. Cases at least: baseline only; org addition; replace to @2; exclude with reason; repos blocks matching in file order; exclude_repos; mode by specificity (enterprise, org, control block, repos block); Remediation App absent and suspended; an ownership conflict; archived, fork and parked repositories; an org outside enterprise.orgs. Done: 23 cases under testdata/resolution/, the harness adding the shared test catalogue to each policy/ directory; repo.json is {repository, access}. Beyond the list: both orders of the worked example, a cross-slug replace, exclude-then-re-add of an older version, a specific early block beating a later general one, and org-over- enterprise remediation settings. control.ID gained MarshalText/ UnmarshalText so goldens read "codeowners@2". reopen_after is in nanoseconds (time.Duration).
  • [x] 2.9 snapshot.go: Snapshot with Version() (a hash over every loaded file, the template bytes and the embedded fallbacks actually used, so a template edit is a policy change), Control(id), Definition(id), Controls(), WatchedPaths() (the union of every definition's file: keys in Owns() ∪ Reads(), which ingest uses as its push filter), and Summarize() for /policies and policy_versions. Done: Version() is controls: + sha256 over the files, the embedded templates used and every definition's revision (so a type Semantics bump is also a policy change). Definition(id) returns (def, ok), and Revision(id) was added for the store. Summarize() returns a policy-package Summary (enterprise, per-org adds/replaces/excludes with reasons and block labels, exclude_repos, repos blocks, catalogue IDs/titles/types/revisions), with no template bodies, PR text or params. Phase 8's /policies filters it.
  • [x] 2.10 Example policies: write examples/policy/{minimal,full,multi-org,renovate,enterprise}/ as directories covering what the five v1 examples covered, and rewrite examples/examples_test.go to load each and compare Summarize() against a committed golden. The v1 guardian-*.hcl files stay until Phase 7, because rule-engine tests still read them. Deferred to after 3.9: the five v1 examples cover dependency updates, settings, rulesets, labels and custom properties, whose types land in Phase 3, and only codeowners exists until then. Done right after Phase 3's types, before 3.10. Done (after 3.9): five roots under examples/policy/ (enterprise.hcl, catalogue/, orgs/, and a templates/ in enterprise for a policy-root template); full uses every built-in type once. The new examples_test.go loads each through policy.Load with builtin.Registry(), fails on any load warning, and compares Summarize() with examples/policy/testdata/<name>.summary.json (-update rewrites). The v1 tests moved to examples_v1_test.go with the guardian-*.hcl files until Phase 7. New internal/controls/builtin (Types(), Registry()) is the one package importing every type, exempt from controls-types; controls-consumers now admits examples/*_test.go. Probe: apply = "workflow" on the labels example fails the load.
  • [x] 2.11 Non-vacuous check: reverse the specificity order and drop the EvalSymlinks containment check; confirm the goldens and the symlink-escape test fail; restore. Done: preferring org-level modes over repos blocks failed mode-org-control and mode-repos-block; dropping the containment check failed TestLoad_SymlinkEscapeIsRefused; both restored. Probing each step found two unpinned behaviours, now covered by goldens: exclude-beats-add within one layer (exclude-beats-add-in-layer) and a baseline slug re-added after a cross-slug replace (baseline-readd-after-cross-slug-replace). Each remaining step probe (no baseline set: 26 goldens; no replace lineage: 2; ignoring access: 2; no conflict marking: 1) fails at least one golden.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• Every resolution golden passes, and a deliberate change to any of steps 1–7 fails at least one golden.
  • Every DESIGN-0030 validation rule has a test with its message and location.
  • Resolve has no dependency on internal/github or the store (depguard).

docs.title: Phase 3: The remaining built-in control types
docs.text: Each type ships with its fixture table, the conformance suite, a golden revision and a Semantics() constant of 1.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 3.1 internal/controls/file: parameters path, template, mode (exists or exact, never both); exact compares YAML semantically for .yml/.yaml and bytes otherwise; owns and reads file:<path>. Done: a definition holds exactly one rule, whose kind is the mode; a mode parameter, when set, must match it. exact always needs the template (it is the comparison), remediable or not. The type implements control.Control directly rather than through NewFileControl, because exact renders per repository and FileType.Check has no Vars. A present file that is not YAML fails exact and is rewritten; a template that renders to invalid YAML is error. controltest gained OneRule: a type with one rule per definition is exempt from property 6, and every fixture must declare one rule.
  • [x] 3.2 internal/catalog: keep the YAML node tree and source spans beside the parsed Properties, with a size cap, so a type can edit minimally; the existing Parse callers keep working until Phase 7. Done: ParseDocument (cap MaxBytes 1 MiB → ErrTooLarge; YAML errors and a non-mapping root → *ParseError with the line) returns a Document holding the source, the yaml.v3 node tree and the decoded Entity. Lookup(path...) returns a scalar with its Span (line, rune column, byte range, Editable for single-line plain and quoted scalars only), and Replace(span, text) edits the bytes in place. Parse is unchanged and shares properties(). depguard: control types may import internal/catalog (a new catalog-leaf rule keeps it importing nothing of ours). That edge is beyond DESIGN-0031 D17's diagram, which this task implies.
  • [x] 3.3 internal/controls/catalog_info: two locations; rule kinds exists and kind (remediable) and field_set with contains, annotation_set and no_placeholders (remediate = false); an absent file gets the template with field rules in Manual; a present file is never edited (every failing rule Manual, kind included); an unparseable file puts every rule in Blocked. Done: field_set{field, contains?} checks a dotted path to a non-empty scalar; annotation_set{annotation} reads metadata.annotations (its keys hold dots); no_placeholders{fields?, placeholders?} checks the named fields, else every scalar. A value is a placeholder when it equals a token or starts with one followed by : or a space (default tokens TODO, TBD, FIXME, CHANGEME, CHANGE_ME, REPLACE_ME, XXX), or is wrapped in <…>. So the shipped fallback template passes exists, kind and field_set but fails no_placeholders, which is the point. Evidence lists offenders as parallel placeholder_fields/placeholder_lines arrays (evidence is scalars or arrays of scalars). control gained the Param* type constants.
  • [x] 3.4 internal/controls/dependency_updates: tool and renovate.extends; the Dependabot and Renovate locations owned and read; package.json read only; rule kinds configured, extends and exclusive; a node-preserving JSON span editor that adds the preset to extends; JSON5 gets a note, not an edit; deleting the other tool's config is in the same change set. Fixtures include configured plus extends failing together, and Dependabot plus a JSON5 Renovate config (partial: exclusive fixed, extends manual). Done: implements control.Control directly (several files, two tools). The preset is renovate = { extends = "..." } and is a template, so one catalogue entry serves every org. Locations are in Renovate's own read order. A package.json renovate key satisfies configured/extends for Renovate, fails exclusive for Dependabot, and is never edited (Manual). extends is evaluated on JSON5 too, via a normaliser (comments, single quotes, bare keys, trailing commas); a JSON5 failure is Manual (D5). The JSON span editor appends to the top-level list, matching a multi-line list's indentation, or inserts the key before the first one; extends that is not a list is Manual. Unknown/error rules go to Blocked. TestPartialRemediation pins the D14 example.
  • [x] 3.5 internal/controls/repo_settings: setting:<property> owned per declared property; rule kind equals; fix is APIChange{setting:<property>, set, value}. A 403 on the vulnerability-alerts read is unknown{reason=permission}. Done: properties are the scalar fields of control.RepositorySettings by JSON name plus vulnerability_alerts. equals{property, value} checks the value's kind against the property at Build (ParamAny is new); a property is pinned once per definition, and default_branch may be checked but not remediated. Vulnerability alerts are their own endpoint, so control.Reader gained GetVulnerabilityAlerts (recorded as setting:vulnerability_alerts; implemented by RepoReader, a 404 is false and a 403 is ErrPermission) and control.Writer gained SetVulnerabilityAlerts (PUT/DELETE). A field the response lacks is unknown{not_returned}. controltest property 5 now starts from EmptyRepository() (GitHub's defaults for a new repository) rather than a zero FakeRepo, so API types are proven against real settings. v1's vulnerability_alerts_enabled is vulnerability_alerts here.
  • [x] 3.6 internal/controls/branch_ruleset: owns ruleset:<name>; rule kinds exists and matches (YAML-semantic comparison of rules); a same-named ruleset whose Source is the organization or enterprise makes both rules unknown{reason=inherited} with a note and is never written. Done: one definition declares one ruleset by name plus ruleset = { enforcement, target, conditions, rules, bypass_actors } in the REST shape (enforcement defaults to active, target to branch; rules required; unknown fields refused). The declaration is a definition parameter, not a template: the registry's template check applies files only, so an API type cannot prove a template there. matches compares by value after a JSON round trip (HCL ints vs API floats): declared object keys must match, extra API defaults are ignored, lists match element by element, and rules are sorted by type on both sides first. One upsert by id fixes both rules; an inherited org or enterprise ruleset blocks both with a note, even beside a repository one of the same name. A remediable exists with a non-active enforcement fails Build. Golden 4daeb7c1….
  • [x] 3.7 internal/controls/labels: owns label:<name> for managed and retired labels, compared lower-cased; rule kinds present and absent; case handling on create and update as the IMPL-0028 label spike found. Done: one rule per label: present{name, color, description} and absent{name}, each owning label:<lower-cased name>; the same name in any case twice fails Build, and colours must be six hex digits (compared case-insensitively, written lower-cased). A case-only difference fails present and is fixed by a set carrying the declared name, which write.UpsertLabel turns into a PATCH (spike 10), never a create; a retired label is APIChange{delete}. An omitted description is not checked and an update keeps the label's own. Golden 885023bb….
  • [x] 3.8 internal/controls/custom_properties: properties with source, normalize, scope, rendered key and value pattern; the built-in Owner and Component; reads the two catalog-info paths; rule kinds matches, value_pattern and defined; the four source states of DESIGN-0031 D16 as fixtures with their exact per-property writes or retention; CatalogParseFailedTotal on an unparseable file; defined is not_applicable on a user-owned repository; each write is gated on its own property. WorkflowApply renders .github/workflows/repo-guardian-custom_properties.yml through the IMPL-0020 A2 env-indirection helpers (yamlq, propenv), with the injection regression test carried over from internal/rules. Done: definition params properties = { <name> = { source, normalize, scope, key, pattern } } (declares a property or overrides a built-in's facts; scope is an org list, key the rendered GitHub name defaulting to <name>, normalize one of none/entity_ref/lower) and v1's annotation_properties shorthand (source annotation:<key>). Built-in Owner is spec.owner with entity_ref (so group:default/platform and platform agree) and Component is metadata.name. A sourceless property never enters the managed set; duplicate rendered keys (case- insensitive), an annotation onto a built-in, a bad key, pattern or normalize fail Build. Rules may narrow to one key with property. An empty derived value clears. matches evidence carries properties, sources, differs, withheld and withheld_gates (value | schema); a withheld property blocks the rule while its siblings are still written. A schema read error closes the schema gate (v1 failed open; the controls model never lets unknown open a write). Deviations: control.RepoContext gained AccountType (AccountUser makes every rule not_applicable{account_type=user}, D10) for the activity layer to fill, and depguard controls-types now allows the internal/metrics leaf so CatalogParseFailedTotal{org} increments in Evaluate (not Remediate, so once per evaluation). The workflow template lives with the type (workflow.yml.tmpl), runs on a push to the repository's default branch whatever its name, and clears with -F ...=null. Golden ed80fe4e….
  • [x] 3.9 apply on the four API types: recommend (default), direct, and workflow only on custom_properties; the registry rejects the rest (covered by 1.9's error table, extended here). Done: a marker interface control.APIType (RemediatesByAPI()) on repo_settings, branch_ruleset, labels and custom_properties. checkApply refuses an unknown value first, then any apply on a type that is not an APIType ("remediates by pull request and takes no apply value"), then workflow without WorkflowApply. 1.9's table gained recommend/direct on an API type, workflow on an API type without WorkflowApply, and all three values on a file type; TestCatalogue_Apply covers the same through the loader (the codeowners decode fixture lost its remediation {} block).
  • [x] 3.10 Parser fuzzing: Render(Parse(x)) == x for the catalog-info YAML and the Renovate JSON editors, plus a test at each parser's size cap. Done: FuzzParseDocument_RoundTrip (bytes round-trip, and a metadata.name replace touches nothing outside its span), FuzzAddExtends (valid JSON out, preset present, one contiguous insertion) and FuzzNormaliseJSON5 (valid JSON keeps its value). Two real bugs: addExtends edited truncated JSON (now refused by json.Valid; the corpus entry is kept as a seed), and yaml.v3's struct decode checks duplicate keys pairwise, so a 50k-key catalog-info took

    20s — ParseDocument now walks the node tree linearly (TestParseDocument_WideMappingIsLinear). Size caps: catalog MaxBytes / MaxBytes+1, Renovate TestExtends_SizeCap (judged at the cap, unknown{file_too_large} one byte over). The file type's YAML exact compare and v1 catalog.Parse keep the quadratic decode; the former carries a FIX note, the latter goes in Phase 7.

  • [x] 3.11 Control-type reference generator: repo-guardian controls docs renders every registered type's RuleKinds() and parameters to docs/usage/controls-reference.md; make controls-docs writes it and make lint-controls-docs diffs it, wired into make lint like lint-monitoring. Done: builtin.WriteReference renders each type's semantics, how it remediates (API with its apply values, or pull request) and a rule kind table; repo-guardian controls docs [--out FILE] calls it. make lint now depends on lint-controls-docs, which renders into build/ and diffs, so CI's lint job runs it; appending a line to the committed reference fails the gate. The page is in the mkdocs nav.
  • [x] 3.12 Non-vacuous check: in each type, remove one Fix branch or one location; confirm the conformance suite or fixture table fails; restore. Record one line per type. Done (each restored with git checkout):
  • branch_ruleset: drop the ruleset OpSet → TestConformance/absent fails.
  • catalog_info: drop the catalog-info.yml location → TestConformance/the_.yml_location fails.
  • codeowners: drop docs/CODEOWNERS → TestConformance/docs/CODEOWNERS and TestExistingFileNeverEdited fail.
  • custom_properties: drop the property OpSet → the two clearing source-state fixtures fail.
  • dependency_updates: drop the other-tool delete → the dependabot-present and JSON5-partial fixtures fail.
  • file: drop the file write (body kept in a note so it compiles) → TestConformance fails.
  • labels: drop the label change → TestConformance fails from compliant/template on.
  • repo_settings: drop the setting OpSet → TestConformance fails from compliant/template on.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• All eight types pass controltest and their revision goldens.
  • Every multi-rule file type has a two-rules-failing fixture that passes.
  • make lint-controls-docs is green and fails on a stale reference.

docs.title: Phase 4: Controls schema and store
docs.text: IMPL-0028 provides the controls chain directory, its embed and goose wiring, 00001_core, and pgtest with an owner role plus rg_evaluator and rg_remediator. This phase adds the rest of the chain and the evaluator's store.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 4.1 00002_controls_policy.sql: repository_policy_state and control_assignments with the DESIGN-0030 and DESIGN-0032 columns (epoch, revision, requested_mode, effective_mode, mode_reason, ordinal, state including conflict, error, baseline_control, decision, source_block; PK (repository_id, control_id)), an epoch sequence, the assignment_changed repository_events.kind, and app_installations and app_repository_access with their row-level security policies (unless IMPL-0028 already created them, in which case this task records that). Done: IMPL-0028 had created neither access table, so 00002 does. Epochs come from assignment_epoch_seq (USAGE to rg_evaluator). Each access table pairs a FOR SELECT ... USING (true) policy with one write policy per App; TestControlsChain_AccessRowsAreFencedByApp pins that both roles see both Apps' rows and a cross-App delete affects zero rows, and the role test gained resolution, slot and refusal cases. ControlsSchemaVersion is 2 and the dry-run test derives 1..N from it.
  • [x] 4.2 00003_controls_results.sql (OQ7): control_results, rule_results, result_events, remediations, remediation_steps, remediation_events, the remediation_due and remediation_maintenance views, the append-only revokes, and the full DESIGN-0032 grant matrix to rg_evaluator and rg_remediator, verbatim from the design. Done: identity keys instead of the sketch's BIGSERIAL (no sequence grants). remediations carries RLS so the remediator's DELETE reaches only reserved rows, each write policy paired with the shared SELECT policy. The revokes are explicit though nothing granted them. The role test covers a result record, a reservation, PR observation and the refusals (acknowledging a head as the evaluator, writing evaluator columns as the remediator, rewriting either append-only table). ControlsSchemaVersion is 3.
  • [x] 4.3 00004_compliance.sql: compliance_snapshots keyed (org, control_id, decision, snapshot_at) with the posture buckets, the excluded count and coverage. Done: unmeasurable is split by reason into three columns, and assigned, percent and coverage are stored beside the buckets (NUMERIC(4,1), NULL on an empty denominator). The README and the ControlsSchemaVersion comment now say 00004 is IMPL-0029's (the IMPL moved it here from IMPL-0030). ControlsSchemaVersion is 4.
  • [x] 4.4 sqlc: a second block in sqlc.yaml reading the controls chain and internal/store/postgres/queries_controls/ into package controlsdb; make generate-sql and make lint-sql cover both blocks. Done: the second block writes controlsdb from migrations_controls + queries_controls/, with the same overrides as the first. make lint-sql rewrites every block's paths with .sql[] |= ... and diffs both packages. ControlsStore's two policy-activation statements moved into queries_controls/policy.sql, so the block has real queries from the start.
  • [x] 4.5 store.Controls interface and its Postgres implementation:
  • UpsertRepositories writes the repository row and its app = 'eval' access row in one transaction, then applies the resolution (below);
  • ApplyResolution(repoID, Resolution) upserts policy state and assignments, keeps the epoch of an unchanged active assignment and takes a new one from the sequence for a new or re-activated one, deletes the control_results row of a withdrawn or excluded assignment (cascading to rule_results) with a result_events row whose to_status is NULL, and writes assignment_changed events;
  • StageEvaluation / RecordEvaluation stage per-control payloads in checks.pending_result and commit them in one transaction fenced on the assignment epoch: a stale epoch discards the control's result and counts results_discarded_total{reason="stale_epoch"}; a first row inserts eval_generation = 1; a fingerprint change bumps the generation and writes result_events; evaluated_sha, evaluated_at and evidence refresh only for selected controls; recording is idempotent on the check key;
  • activation runs in the migrate Job, never at worker startup (INV-0022 Phase-0 OQ1 (a)): repo-guardian migrate loads the policy root, computes the controls version and calls IMPL-0028's ActivatePolicyVersion; workers read CurrentActivation and start the rollout for it. The rc's per-pod RecordPolicyVersion start path is deleted with the rc services. Done: store.Controls (internal/store/controls.go) is implemented by ControlsStore on sqlc queries in queries_controls/{repositories, resolution,evaluation}.sql. Identity is matched by provider id, then by name. Resolve re-reads the row and both Apps' access, and UpsertRepositories calls it inline. The epoch compare covers version, revision (which fixes the write set), both modes, source and state. intent_revision is computed at record time, because only the record step knows the generation. results_discarded_total{org,reason} is registered now and counted after the record's work commits, so a retry cannot count twice. repo-guardian migrate --chain controls [--policy DIR] loads the root with builtin.Registry() and activates its version; TestMigrateControls_ActivatesThePolicy covers first-seen and re-sync. TestControlsStore_EvaluationLifecycle and TestControlsStore_DiscoveryUnparks run as rg_evaluator. The rc's RecordPolicyVersion start path goes with the rc services in Phase 7.
  • [x] 4.6 Park with the result rule: archived, fork, removed and installation_removed clear results (with result_events); access_denied and unknown keep them; Evaluation App suspension is read from app_installations.suspended_at and is never a park. A table test per reason asserts rows kept or cleared. Done: ControlsStore.Park takes its reason from parkClears. A clearing reason withdraws every result through the same withdraw path as resolution (a to_status = NULL event), while assignments stay as desired state. suspended is refused, because suspension is access state, which accessOf reads from app_installations.suspended_at. TestControlsStore_ParkResultRule has one row per reason, plus the suspension refusal.
  • [x] 4.7 Compliance queries in queries_controls/compliance.sql, starting from active assignments with a LEFT JOIN to results at the matching epoch and revision: buckets compliant, non_compliant, pending, stale, unmeasurable (by reason), not_applicable, unknown, plus excluded; percent compliant/(compliant+non_compliant) floored to one decimal and NULL on an empty denominator; coverage over assigned; baseline, org-added and exclusions variants. store.CompliantPercent keeps the Go mirror, and a test feeds the same counts to both and asserts they agree. Done: queries_controls/compliance.sql has ControlCompliance (one bucket per assignment, grouped by (org, control_id, decision); lineage filter all/baseline/org_added; an excluded assignment counts under the lineage it would have had) and ControlExclusions. The percentage is one SQL function, floor_percent, added to 00004 and used for both percent and coverage. TestCompliantPercent_SQLAgreesWithGo feeds api/testdata/compliant_percent.json to it and to store.CompliantPercent. Repositories parked unknown count as unmeasurable access loss, alongside access_denied (D6's fail-safe). TestControlsStore_ComplianceBuckets covers every bucket in one fleet, and TestControlsStore_EmptyFleetIsNoData covers no rows / NULL.
  • [x] 4.8 Grant tests (pgtest, as the roles, never the owner): every transaction in 4.5–4.7 succeeds as rg_evaluator; as rg_remediator, writing any evaluator-owned column of control_results, control_assignments or repository_policy_state (except last_remediation_at) fails; nobody can UPDATE or DELETE result_events. Done: TestControlsChain_RecordIsNarrow walks every evaluator-owned column of the three tables. As rg_remediator each one is refused, and as rg_evaluator it is allowed. The remediator's own columns (last_remediation_at, remediated_generation, hold, hold_since) succeed, so the refusals are not vacuous. UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on result_events are refused as evaluator, remediator and rg_all. The 4.5–4.7 transactions run as rg_evaluator in the TestControlsStore_* tests.
  • [x] 4.9 Integration tests: epoch fencing (an assignment deleted and recreated during a record retry ends at generation 1); a policy revert A → B → A resolves under A again; the posture case (100 assigned, one result: 99 pending, coverage 1%, percent from one row); an empty fleet reads NULL, never 100%. Done (controls_compliance_integration_test.go, as rg_evaluator):
  • TestControlsStore_EpochFencingAcrossRecreate: a result staged before a withdraw-and-re-add is discarded on the retry, and the recreated assignment starts at generation 1.
  • TestControlsStore_PolicyRevertResolvesAgain: A → B → A activation leaves A current, and re-resolving returns A's revision.
  • TestControlsStore_PostureOfAMostlyPendingFleet: 100 assigned, 99 pending, coverage 1, percent from the single result.
  • The empty fleet reads no rows, and an all-pending fleet reads NULL (TestControlsStore_EmptyFleetIsNoData, from 4.7).
  • [x] 4.10 migrate --dry-run applies 00001–00004 to an empty database in one rolled-back transaction; SchemaVersion is 4. Done: ControlsSchemaVersion is 4. TestControlsChain_DryRunRollsBack derives 1..4 from it and checks that no table is left behind. TestMigrateControls_DryRun runs migrate --chain controls --dry-run and asserts pending [1 2 3 4], no activation and version 0. The chain is SQL only, so a new file is rehearsed simply by being in the directory.
  • [x] 4.11 Non-vacuous check: drop the epoch predicate from the record step, make withdrawal skip the delete, and remove the NULL guard from the percent; confirm 4.6, 4.9 and the agreement test fail; restore. Done (each restored with git checkout):
  • Epoch predicate dropped from fenced → TestControlsStore_EpochFencingAcrossRecreate (4.9) and TestControlsStore_EvaluationLifecycle fail.
  • withdraw skips the delete → TestControlsStore_ParkResultRule (4.6) fails in every clearing row.
  • NULL guard removed from floor_percent → TestCompliantPercent_SQLAgreesWithGo fails (division by zero on the 0/0 golden).

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 5.1 Names and types in internal/workflows: EvaluationWorkflowID (evaluation/<repository id>), ControlsDiscoveryWorkflowID (controls-discovery/installation/<id>/<delivery>), schedule ids controls-discovery and controls-snapshot, ControlsRolloutWorkflowID (controls-rollout/<version>/<activated_at unix seconds>, so a revert or rollback rolls out again); signals Recheck{Paths []string, Unknown bool, Priority} and PolicyChanged; PriorityManual Priority = 1. Done: names in names.go (workflow and activity names, the two schedule ids, EvaluationWorkflowID, ControlsDiscoveryWorkflowID, ControlsRolloutWorkflowID); Recheck gained Paths and Unknown (omitempty, so the captured rc histories replay unchanged); PolicyChanged is reused as is; PriorityManual = 1; TriggerPREvent/TriggerManual. TestControlsWorkflowIDs pins the ids and that a re-activation gets a new rollout id.
  • [x] 5.2 EvaluationWorkflow (evaluation.go), built from repoLoop: a jittered EVAL_INTERVAL timer, recheck and policy_changed signals, coalescing that unions changed paths with unknown dominating, the budget lease on installation/eval/<installation id>, deferral on throttle with nothing recorded, park on repository-level access loss, ContinueAsNew every 100 iterations carrying the coalesced set, and a drain of unread signals before ContinueAsNew. repoLoop stays for RepoWorkflow until Phase 7. Done: internal/workflows/evaluation.go (EvaluationWorkflow, evalLoop, coalesce) and evaluation_types.go. Deferrals reuse the check key and record nothing; a parked result runs ParkRepository and ends the run; the lease is on installation/eval/<id>. Tests in evaluation_test.go (schedule/record/park, deferral, in-flight signal coalescing, ContinueAsNew at 100, coalesce table). Not registered on a worker yet.
  • [x] 5.3 Evaluate activity (internal/activities/evaluate.go): read policy state and active assignments, skip unless managed; skip conflict assignments (reported unmeasurable{reason=conflict}); classify throttle first, then repository access loss; pin the default branch head through PRObserver.GetRef; select controls by Owns() ∪ Reads() against the changed paths (all on unknown, the schedule or policy_changed; API resources only on the schedule); run each through one NewEvalReader, then Validate, StatusOf and Fingerprint; stage the payload. A control-local 403 is unknown{reason=permission} and parks nothing. Done: internal/activities/evaluate.go (Evaluator, EvalStore, EvalPolicy, EvalRepo, EvalClients) and evalclients.go (GitHubEvalClients). The pin reads the default branch over REST so a lost repository is a 403/404 IsAccessDenied sees (the settings read is GraphQL first); throttles inside a control's reads are caught by throttleWatch under the shared EvalReader, because types fold read errors into results. Each control's fingerprint takes only the reads of its own Owns() ∪ Reads() (plus a failed * listing of a kind it reads), so another control's file never moves it. An assignment whose revision differs from the loaded policy waits for re-resolution. Deviations: ControlsStore.EvaluationTarget + query added for the read; app_installations.account_type added to 00002 (unreleased) to fill RepoContext.AccountType, and UpsertInstallation now takes a pointer. Tests: evaluate_test.go, TestControlsStore_EvaluationTarget.
  • [x] 5.4 Record and park activities: RecordEvaluation (4.5) and ParkRepository (4.6), with the checks.trigger values pr_event and manual accepted. Done: Evaluator.RecordEvaluation (counts recorded / changed / discarded, AlreadyFinal on a recorded key) and Evaluator.ParkRepository (store Park, which keeps results on access_denied; logs CheckRepo's park line at the same levels and keys). Evaluator.Register names the three activities; nothing calls it yet. pr_event/manual were already in 00001's trigger check: TestControlsStore_StageAcceptsControlsTriggers pins them.
  • [x] 5.5 ControlsDiscoveryWorkflow: lists the Evaluation App's installations and repositories, refreshes app = 'eval' rows of app_installations and app_repository_access, and calls UpsertRepositories, which resolves inline between the upsert and the SignalWithStart of evaluation/<id>; parks missing repositories; records a service_runs row; sets installation_info{app="eval"}. Done: ControlsDiscoveryWorkflow (internal/workflows/controls_service.go, DiscoveryWorkflow's shape on the Controls* activities, writing its run through the new ControlsRecordServiceRun activity) and activities.ControlsServices (controls_services.go). Listings keep archived and forked repositories (workflows.DiscoveredRepo carries the flags); resolution parks them with results cleared, so there is no discovery filter to keep in step. New or un-parked managed repositories get a policy_changed SignalWithStart of evaluation/<id> due at a random point in EVAL_INTERVAL. ghclient.Installation gained Personal and RepositorySelection for the eval installation row; the store gained ParkMissing and RecordServiceRun. Found by TestControlsStore_ParkMissingAndServiceRun: a nil seen slice is a NULL array and id = ANY (NULL) parks nothing, so the query coalesces it. Tests: controls_service_test.go, controls_services_test.go. Follow-up fix: upsertOne passed Active: true to resolution, so an archived or forked listing was un-parked and resolved managed; it now parks with that reason (results cleared) and never un-parks one (TestControlsStore_DiscoveryParksArchivedAndForks).
  • [x] 5.6 Controls rollout: every worker reads CurrentActivation at startup and starts controls-rollout/<version>/<activated_at> with REJECT_DUPLICATE (one rollout per activation, however many pods start), which re-resolves every repository, then signals policy_changed spread over POLICY_ROLLOUT_WINDOW, and marks the rollout complete. The evaluator's bootstrap ensures only the controls-discovery and controls-snapshot schedules. Done: ControlsRolloutWorkflow (resolve pass, policy_changed signal pass by now + window, sleep the window, ControlsCompleteRollout, a policy_rollout service run); ControlsServices.ResolveAll / SignalAll / CompleteRollout over the new store reads ActiveRepositories and CompletePolicyRollout. ResolveAll refuses a rollout whose version is not the worker's loaded policy, so a retry lands on a pod that has it. serviceStarter.startControlsRollout reads CurrentActivation and starts controls-rollout/<v>/<unix> with REJECT_DUPLICATE only when the loaded policy is the activated one; schedules(RoleEvaluator) ensures exactly controls-discovery and controls-snapshot (snapshot takes SnapshotInput). The evaluator role calls neither until 7.1, per the phase's "nothing registered" criterion. The task names no straggler pass, so the rc's is not carried over.
  • [x] 5.7 Webhook routing on /webhooks/github/eval: a default-branch push signals recheck at priority 2 with the changed paths filtered through Snapshot.WatchedPaths() (a push with no watched path signals nothing; 2048 commits, forced, or more than 256 filtered paths is unknown, DESIGN-0032 § history growth); repository created, renamed, transferred, archived, unarchived and deleted run discovery, resolution or park; installation and installation_repositories from either App re-resolve the affected repositories, because a Remediation App change moves the effective mode. This replaces the rc's drop of every Evaluation App delivery (IMPL-0028 task 9.1); delete TestRouteWebhook_EvaluationAppDropped with it. Done: activities.ControlsRouter (controls_route.go) takes every Evaluation App delivery through Router.WithControls; until 7.1 wires it the default unwiredControls logs and drops, so the rc binary is unchanged. Ingest puts the push change set on WebhookInput.Paths (watched, sorted) or Unknown (≥2048 commits, forced, >256 paths); a push touching no watched path is 204. Push rechecks a known active managed repository at priority 2, discovers an unknown one and never un-parks; repository events upsert with the payload's archived/fork flags (so discovery parks, not churns) and recheck in full, deleted and removed park removed, installation.deleted parks installation_removed. RecordAppAccess (Remediation App) re-resolves the named repositories, or the account's org, and signals policy_changed on a change. Known gap: the Remediation App's access rows are the remediator's to write (IMPL-0030), so re-resolution reads the access recorded so far. The watched set is still the rc's until 7.1/7.8 pass Snapshot.WatchedPaths(). TestRouteWebhook_EvaluationAppDropped deleted; tests in controls_route_test.go, ingest_test.go and TestControlsStore_RoutingReads.
  • [x] 5.8 Controls snapshot: controls-snapshot writes compliance_snapshots rows from 4.7's query. Done: ControlsSnapshotWorkflow runs the ControlsSnapshot activity (ControlsServices.Snapshot) stamped at the workflow's start, then records a snapshot service run with the row count. The controls line has no checks table, so SnapshotInput.Retention prunes nothing. ControlsStore.InsertComplianceSnapshot reads ControlCompliance (all lineages, every org) and inserts its rows in one transaction, so a snapshot never disagrees with the live query and a NULL percentage stays NULL. Tests: TestControlsSnapshotWorkflow_WritesAndRecords, TestControlsServices_SnapshotStampsTheRun, and TestControlsStore_ComplianceSnapshot (as rg_evaluator).
  • [x] 5.9 repo-guardian evaluate --repo <org>/<name> [--format json]: loads the policy directory, authenticates as the Evaluation App, checks access, resolves, evaluates with no store, and prints a table or JSON carrying schema_version and the evaluated commit. Exit codes: 0 compliant or nothing measured, 1 non-compliant, 2 usage or configuration error, 3 operational failure. Golden JSON for a fake repository; one test per exit code. Done: cmd/repo-guardian/evaluate.go. Loads the policy root (--policy, default $GUARDIAN_CONFIG) with the built-in registry, reads the Evaluation App's id and key path through the new config.LoadAppCredentials, finds the org's installation, checks access with GetRepository (which also supplies the archived/fork flags for resolution), then calls activities.Evaluator.EvaluateResolved. That method is new and store-free: the same selection and run as the scheduled evaluation, staging nothing, with epochs at zero. Output is a table, or JSON with schema_version, policy_version, branch and commit. Exit codes travel back through exitError, which main honours: 0 compliant or nothing measured, 1 non-compliant (silent), 2 usage, policy or credentials error, 3 no access, throttled or failed. Tests: TestEvaluate_ExitCodes (one case per code, plus nothing-measured and a missing policy root), TestEvaluate_GoldenJSON (testdata/evaluate.golden.json, regenerate with -update-evaluate) and TestEvaluate_Table.
  • [x] 5.10 Workflow tests (time-skipping environment): disjoint pushes coalesce to the union; one unknown signal selects every control; a parked repository is never read; a deferral writes no posture; ContinueAsNew history stays bounded under maximum-size signals (the bound the IMPL-0028 spike measured). Done: in evaluation_test.go.
  • TestEvaluationWorkflow_SignalsDuringAnEvaluationCoalesce: now sends disjoint {b} and {a} while an evaluation is in flight; they coalesce to [a b].
  • TestEvaluationWorkflow_UnknownSignalSelectsEveryControl
  • TestEvaluationWorkflow_ParkedRepositoryIsNeverReadAgain: an already-parked result ends the loop with no further reads, records or park.
  • TestEvaluationWorkflow_DeferralRecordsNothing (from 5.2) covers the deferral case.
  • TestEvaluationWorkflow_HistoryBoundedUnderMaxSignals: a 256-path, 60-byte-path signal during every one of the 100 evaluations, and two disjoint ones during the last, to measure the INV-0022 spike 5(c) bound.

Finding fixed: coalesce had no cap, so disjoint maximum signals grew the carried state without bound. A union past the new workflows.MaxChangedPaths (256, which ingest's filter now uses too) becomes unknown. The ContinueAsNew state stays under 1 KB; with the cap removed it read 32 KB and the test failed. A TestCoalesce row covers the cap. - [x] 5.11 Change-detection tables (activity plus store): status change, file blob change, API value change with unchanged statuses, revision change and a first evaluation bump the generation; a cosmetic title edit and an unrelated push do not; unselected controls keep their evaluated_sha. Done. TestPolicyRevision_CosmeticTitleEdit loads two policy roots that differ only in titles and gets one revision.

Store table, as rg_evaluator: TestControlsStore_ChangeDetection. - The first evaluation bumps both controls. - A repeated fingerprint bumps nothing. - A changed fingerprint bumps one. - The unselected renovate keeps its evaluated_sha. - [x] 5.12 TestIntegration_OneEvaluation (-tags integration): temporaltest, the controls chain in pgtest and the GitHub fake run discovery → resolution → evaluation → recorded results for a fixture org, and capture an EvaluationWorkflow history into internal/workflows/testdata/histories/evaluation_first_run.json, replayed in CI with the existing fixtures. docs.title: Phase 6: Posture, metrics, generated monitoring and the report
Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 6.1 Metrics in internal/metrics/metrics.go: evaluations_total{org, outcome}, evaluation_errors_total{org, control}, evaluation_changes_total{org, control}, results_discarded_total{org, reason}, evaluation_freshness_seconds{org} (histogram of the previous evaluated_at's age), store_pool_wait_seconds{role}, and the gauges controls_status{org, control, bucket} and controls_coverage{org, control}; producers wired in 5.3 and 5.4. installation_info gains app. No metric carries a repository label. Done: the seven series in metrics.go (TestMetricNames_ExactSet updated). Evaluate counts evaluations_total per attempt (deferred is not counted, parked is skipped) and evaluation_errors_total for a control returning an error or ending with an error rule (TestEvaluate_CountsOutcomesAndControlErrors). RecordEvaluation counts evaluation_changes_total per generation move and observes evaluation_freshness_seconds from the previous evaluated_at (LockResult reads it), both after commit (TestControlsStore_ChangeDetection). store_pool_wait_seconds{role} comes from observability.InstrumentPostgresConfig(cfg, role), whose tracer wraps otelpgx and is the pool's AcquireTracer, wired into the controls workers' pools. controls_status/controls_coverage are published by 6.3's exporter; installation_info already carries app (IMPL-0028 3.6).

Done: deployment_info gains version; SetDeploymentInfo(topology, version) runs once in bringUp with temporal.BuildID() (the module version of a tagged build, else the VCS revision, else dev).
  • [x] 6.3 Posture exporter (OQ8) over 4.7's query: read before reset; on a read error keep the previous values; publish nothing when not configured to export. Tests for each, and for a vanished org dropping its series. Done: api.PostureExporter (internal/api/posture.go), per OQ8 the api role's job. Export reads ControlCompliance(nil, LineageAll), sums the decisions per (org, control), then resets and republishes controls_status{bucket} (unmeasurable = access_denied + suspended + conflict) and controls_coverage (assigned). A read error returns and keeps the previous values; the reset drops a vanished org's series; a nil reader (not configured) publishes nothing and Run returns. Tests for each. Wiring it into the api role over the controls read-only store lands with the switch-over (Phase 7), when the api role gets that DSN.

docs.title: OQ1: Where does the new policy package live while the rule engine still builds?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

The old loader owns internal/policy until Phase 7, and the new one must end up there (DESIGN-0031 D17 names it).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: rename the old package to internal/rulepolicy at the start of Phase 2 (one mechanical commit), build the new one in place, delete rulepolicy in Phase 7. No rename at the end, and depguard rules name the final path from day one.
  • (b) Build the new one as internal/controlpolicy and rename it in Phase 7. The old code is untouched, but every new importer and depguard rule changes at switch-over.
  • (c) Delete the rule engine first and build on an empty path. Simplest code, but the branch cannot run anything until Phase 7.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ2: Do the control types implement Remediate in this plan?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

Remediate writes nothing (it returns a ChangeSet), and the conformance suite's properties 2–6 test it.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: yes, each type is built complete here, so one package and one conformance run cover a type, and the load-time template check and ValidateChangeSet are exercised before IMPL-0030 starts applying change sets. IMPL-0030 only applies them.
  • (b) Build Evaluate here and stub Remediate with an error; IMPL-0030 fills it in. This plan is smaller, but every type is reopened and properties 2–6 wait.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ3: Which control types must exist before the first controls rc?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

DESIGN-0031 says the first evaluate-only rc needs only the types v1's built-in defaults cover.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: all eight, because the homelab comparison with prod v1 (9.8) covers the settings, branch protection, labels and custom properties v1 manages there, and a policy naming an unbuilt type fails load.
  • (b) The four file types (codeowners, file, catalog_info, dependency_updates) gate the rc; the API types follow in a second rc from this plan.
  • (c) The four file types here; the API types move to IMPL-0030.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ4: Does this plan ship an evaluate-only rc, and where does it run?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: yes, and it replaces the homelab dev install: a fresh install in the dev namespace against a new database, with the Evaluation App only, beside prod v1. It cannot write, so it can watch every org, and its numbers are compared with v1 before IMPL-0030 turns anything on. The IMPL-0030 fresh install later replaces both.
  • (b) No rc from this plan: evaluation and remediation ship together at the end of IMPL-0030. One fewer release, but posture is first compared with v1 only when writes are possible.
  • (c) Tag an rc but do not deploy it.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ5: What does the evaluate-only rc do with mode = "remediate"?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

The rc has no remediator. Usually the Remediation App is absent too, so resolution already sets effective_mode = evaluate with remediation_app_no_access.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: load and resolve honestly; nothing consumes remediation_due. Evaluation does not start remediations until IMPL-0030 adds the activity, and /repositories/{id}/controls shows requested and effective mode as resolved.
  • (b) Fail policy load on mode = "remediate" in this release, and remove the check in IMPL-0030.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ6: How is the work split into pull requests?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a). The maintainer's direction: one PR per plan, so the agent does every task it can without waiting on a merge between phases. A task that needs the maintainer (homelab runs, GitHub App registration, approving a large git rm, release tags) is marked deferred - human required and done by the maintainer, during review or after the merge.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: one PR for the whole plan into v2, with dont-release, as IMPL-0027 did. Phase 7 deletes and re-points inside it, so v2 never holds a half-switched binary; the rc tag and the homelab runs in Phase 9 are deferred - human required.
  • (b) One PR per phase, with Phase 7 as a single PR. Smaller reviews, but every phase waits on a merge.
  • (c) Two PRs: build (Phases 1–6), then switch, API and release (7–9).
  • other:

docs.title: OQ7: Does 00003_controls_results land whole in this plan?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

DESIGN-0032 fixes the file split up front; 00003 holds the evaluation tables and the remediation tables, views and grants.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: yes, the whole file verbatim from the design, so the rc's schema is final, the grant matrix is tested once, and IMPL-0030 adds behaviour without a schema change. IMPL-0030 owns the remediation_due truth table and the remediator's grant tests.
  • (b) Split it: this plan writes 00003_controls_results with the evaluation tables; IMPL-0030 adds 00005_remediation. That breaks the design's numbering and leaves evaluation's remediations column grants for later.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ8: Which process exports the posture gauges?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

v2 has no SETNX leader; the v1 exporter is deleted with the v1 runtime.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: every api replica, on a ticker, from its read-only DSN. Every replica reads the same rows, so max by collapses them exactly; the api role runs continuously (the evaluator may scale to zero under KEDA). The gauges are absent when the api role is disabled, which the chart notes.
  • (b) A Temporal schedule activity on whichever evaluator runs it. One pod holds fresh values and the others hold stale ones, which max by cannot tell apart.
  • (c) Every evaluator pod on a ticker. Correct under max by, but nothing is published while the evaluator is scaled to zero.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ9: How much of the UI does this plan rebuild?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: every view D32 affects (8.7), leaving the Remediations view and the remediation fields of the Repository view to IMPL-0030. The homelab comparison (9.8) needs the controls views.
  • (b) The API here and every UI view in IMPL-0030. Smaller plan, but the rc ships with only a Status view.
  • (c) Controls, Repository and Status here; Orgs, History and Policy in IMPL-0030.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ10: When is the monitoring tier regenerated?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: in Phase 6 of this plan, over evaluation, so the rc ships with working E1–E4 and alerts and lint-monitoring stays meaningful; IMPL-0030 adds the remediation panels and alerts.
  • (b) Once, in IMPL-0030, for both halves. Less churn in the generator, but the rc ships with E1/E2 removed and Derive stubbed.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ11: How does the chart express a policy directory in a ConfigMap?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

ConfigMap keys cannot contain /, and the policy root has catalogue/, orgs/ and templates/.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: policy.files is a nested map by directory (enterprise.hcl, catalogue: {codeowners.hcl: ...}, orgs: {...}, templates: {...}); the template flattens keys (catalogue.codeowners.hcl) and mounts them back with items[].path. Values read like the directory, and the flattening is invisible.
  • (b) Flat keys with a separator in values (catalogue__codeowners.hcl), mapped back with items[].path.
  • (c) One ConfigMap per directory, or existingConfigMap only.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ12: Where does POST /evaluate keep its one-per-minute dedupe?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

The api role has a read-only DSN and no shared cache.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: in memory, per api replica, a TTL map keyed by repository id. With N replicas a repository can be signalled at most N times a minute, and EvaluationWorkflow coalesces signals anyway.
  • (b) In the workflow: the workflow ignores a manual recheck within a minute of the last one. Exact across replicas, but every request still reaches Temporal.
  • (c) A dedupe table the api role may write. Exact, but it breaks the read-only DSN.
  • other:
