docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Build the remediation half of the controls line and ship it as v2.0.0: per-control remediation PRs under a per-repository cap, run by a RemediationWorkflow per repository and control on the remediator role; API remediations under apply = recommend | direct | workflow; the remediation sweep and lifecycle maintenance; the metrics, alerts and API that show it, together with every API the controls UI (DESIGN-0037) reads; persisting next due and the two INV-0023 worker gaps; and the homelab fresh install that replaces the dev (v2 rc) and prod (v1) deployments with one v2 install.

Implements: DESIGN-0032 (Remediation, API remediations, the remediation tables, Failure semantics, the remediation rows of the Temporal mapping, Migration / Rollout Plan steps 2 to 4), the write side of DESIGN-0031 (Remediate, ChangeSet, Writer, WorkflowApply) and the remediation settings of DESIGN-0030 (max_open_prs, reopen_after, effective_mode); DESIGN-0037 §API / Interface Changes; INV-0023 F3, F7.1 and F7.2. The UI that reads all of it is IMPL-0032.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• The remediations, remediation_steps and remediation_events tables, the remediation_due and remediation_maintenance views, the remediator's column grants, and the store methods over them.
  • PR observation by the evaluator (merged, closed by a user, observed head) and the one batched activity per evaluation that signal-with-starts the due remediations.
  • RemediationWorkflow (remediation/<repository id>/<control slug> on repo-guardian-remediate): one run at a time, the re-check flag, the end-of-run re-read, epoch fencing before every write, durable operations with the step journal, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on overlapping attempts.
  • The PR path: find, adopt or hold; slot reservation; descent check; update-branch; fresh evaluation at the pinned head; closed_compliant; Remediate with the self-check; one commit through createCommitOnBranch; journaled reverts of obsolete bot edits; PR create, adopt or update; narrow recording.
  • API remediations: recommendations with proposals, journaled direct apply, and workflow apply for types that implement WorkflowApply.
  • The remediation-sweep schedule (sweep plus maintenance) and the controls-discovery-remediate schedule.
  • Remediation metrics, alerts, dashboard panels, the /remediations endpoint and the remediation object.
  • DESIGN-0037's API: GET /results, Repository.compliance, Summary.parked_by_reason/finding_age/controls_failing/open_prs_by_age, /compliance/history?aggregate=, /remediations/activity, pr_stale and ResultRow.remediation, the perf fixture, the spec description fixes (moved from IMPL-0032, 2026-10-18).
  • Persisting repositories.next_due_at (INV-0023 F3), the per-role store DSNs (F7.1) and pruning checks (F7.2).
  • The cutover code changes, the docs rewrite (v2-migration.md as the fresh-install runbook, the remediation parts of v2-overview.md and v2-onboarding.md, CLAUDE.md), the homelab fresh install, and the v2.0.0 release.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Everything in IMPL-0028 (client split, Writer package, GraphQL Commit, throttle classification, two Apps, per-App webhooks, two queues and worker deployments, roles, KEDA, the goose skeleton, database role provisioning, and every phase-0 spike).
  • Everything in IMPL-0029 (policy model, resolution, control types' evaluation, control_results, EvaluationWorkflow, the switch-over that deletes the old engine, the evaluate-only rc, posture).
  • The evaluate-mode remediation preview (DESIGN-0032 D7, "a later phase").
  • DESIGN-0034's CODEOWNERS valid rule; DESIGN-0034 stays Draft.
  • Deleting branches. repo-guardian never deletes a branch (D30); rgctl prs close --delete-branch stays an operator's opt-in.
  • Foreign-PR detection (D5).
  • Every UI change, the Remediations view included (IMPL-0032).
  • IMPL-0026 (Temporal credential reload, OpenBao certificates), which runs after IMPL-0028 on its own schedule.

docs.title: How the phases are ordered
docs.text:
Phases 1 to 7 are code, each ending with make lint and make test green and a commit per numbered task. Phase 1 is storage, so every later phase can run its tests as rg_remediator. Phase 2 lands the two evaluator-side pieces remediation depends on but that have no consumer before it. Phase 3 is the workflow shell and the GitHub fake the behaviour tests need. Phases 4 and 5 are the two write paths. Phase 6 is the scheduled half, which needs both paths to exist. Phase 7 makes it visible and adds the API the controls UI reads, so IMPL-0032 builds on a merged API. Phase 8 is the cutover code and the docs, written against the built behaviour. Phase 9 is human-run: the remediation rc and the homelab fresh install. Phase 10 is GA.

The plan lands as one PR into v2 with the dont-release label (OQ13). No assignment is in remediate mode until Phase 9, so merging Phases 1 to 8 changes nothing a running deployment does. Phases 9 and 10 (the homelab fresh install and the tags) are human-run and marked deferred - human required.

docs.title: Phase 1: Remediation schema, store and grants
Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 1.1 Confirm where the remediation DDL lives (OQ1). If IMPL-0029 already shipped remediations, remediation_steps, remediation_events, both views and the remediator grants in 00003_controls_results, diff them against DESIGN-0032 §Data Model and fix drift there; otherwise add them as the OQ1 answer says. The DDL is DESIGN-0032's verbatim: the three CHECKs on kind/state, remediations_one_open, remediations_slots, UNIQUE (remediation_id, seq). Done: IMPL-0029 shipped every table, both views, the RLS policies and the grant matrix in 00003. One drift: remediation_maintenance did not withdraw on an effective_mode = 'evaluate' downgrade (1.3). rc databases have applied 00003, so the fix is the additive 00005_remediation.sql (ControlsSchemaVersion 5), not an edit.
  • [x] 1.2 remediation_due view: the DESIGN-0032 predicate over repository_policy_state, control_assignments (active, matching epoch, effective_mode = 'remediate'), control_results (status non_compliant, remediable, eval_generation > remediated_generation or intent_revision differing from the latest remediation's, or observed_head_sha <> acknowledged_head_sha), and the latest remediation (closed_by_user eligible only when eval_generation > closed_generation or next_eligible_at <= now()). Ordered by ordinal. Done (IMPL-0029, 00003): the view matches; the 1.10 truth table pins it.
  • [x] 1.3 remediation_maintenance view: rows needing expire (reserved past reserved_until), withdraw (open PR or recommendation whose assignment is gone, excluded, parked, out of org, or effective_mode = 'evaluate'), supersede (recommendation whose intent_revision moved) and close_compliant (open PR whose control reads compliant; acted on only after a fresh read, 4.10). Done: 00003 plus the evaluate-downgrade withdraw arm in 00005 (1.1).
  • [x] 1.4 Grants: rg_remediator INSERT on remediations, UPDATE on every column except observed_head_sha, observed_at, closed_generation, next_eligible_at, DELETE on reserved rows (a row-level security policy FOR DELETE TO rg_remediator USING (state = 'reserved'), since a grant cannot restrict rows); INSERT on remediation_steps and remediation_events; UPDATE (remediated_generation, hold, hold_since) on control_results; UPDATE (last_remediation_at) on repository_policy_state; INSERT on service_runs; sequence USAGE. UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE revoked for both roles on remediation_steps and remediation_events. Done (IMPL-0029, 00003/00002/00001): every grant and the reservation-only DELETE policy exist. No sequence grant is needed: the remediation tables use identity keys. The 1.11 grant tests pin it.
  • [x] 1.5 internal/store/postgres/remediations.go: ReserveSlot(ctx, repo, control, epoch, opKey, intent, ttl) (one transaction: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on repository_policy_state, count open + reserved through remediations_slots, insert reserved or return ErrPRCap); ClaimOperation(ctx, opKey) (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, returning ErrOperationHeld when another attempt holds it; the transaction stays open for the activity and is released on return); LatestRemediation, AppendStep, AppendEvent, SetIntent. Done: postgres.RemediationStore (the rg_remediator pool) implements store.Remediations; the claim uses FOR NO KEY UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so journal inserts (FOR KEY SHARE on the parent) commit on their own connection, and writes to the claimed row go through ClaimedOperation. A retried reservation returns its own row before the cap check. Pinned by TestRemediationStore_ReserveSlot and TestRemediationStore_ClaimOperation.
  • [x] 1.6 RecordRun (record-is-narrow): remediated_generation to the generation read at run start, acknowledged_head_sha by compare-and-set against the head processed, intent_revision, last_run_at, hold = NULL; discarded and counted in results_discarded_total{reason="stale_epoch"} when the assignment epoch moved. Idempotent on operation_key. Done: the remediator has no UPDATE on control_assignments, so the fence locks the control_results row FOR UPDATE (withdrawal deletes it) and compares both epochs under that lock; remediated_generation is GREATEST, so a repeat is a no-op. Call it after ClaimOperation returns. TestRemediationStore_RecordRun.
  • [x] 1.7 SetHold(ctx, repo, control, epoch, hold) writing control_results.hold/hold_since, and the remediations.hold = 'permission' path for blocked cleanup when the result row is gone. Done: hold_since keeps the start of an unchanged hold; a stale epoch writes nothing; with the result gone only permission lands, on the newest remediation. TestRemediationStore_SetHold.
  • [x] 1.8 DueRemediations(ctx, batch) and MaintenanceCandidates(ctx, batch) over the two views; ExpireReservations(ctx, now) returning the count for remediation_reservations_expired_total. Done: the caller counts the metric (Phase 6 defines it). TestRemediationStore_DueAndMaintenance.
  • [x] 1.9 Pool: REMEDIATOR_DB_POOL_SIZE (default REMEDIATOR_CONCURRENCY + 4); startup refuses a pool smaller than the concurrency, since every running operation holds one connection for its row lock. store_pool_wait_seconds{role} from the pgxpool stats. Done: halfSizing in cmd/repo-guardian/controls.go (TestHalfSizing); store_pool_wait_seconds{role} was already produced by the pool tracer (observability.InstrumentPostgresConfig). Chart remediator.dbPoolSize comment updated.
  • [x] 1.10 remediation_due truth table as SQL against the view (DESIGN-0032 Testing Strategy): policy state, assignment state and epoch, effective mode and reason, status, remediable, generations including the first-evaluation 1 > 0 row, intent revision, latest state, observed versus acknowledged head, closed_generation, next_eligible_at. Done: TestRemediationDue_TruthTable (24 rows, each in a rolled-back owner transaction over one recorded fixture) plus TestRemediationMaintenance_Actions, which pins 1.3 and 00005's evaluate-downgrade withdraw.
  • [x] 1.11 Grant tests through the extended pgtest harness, run as rg_remediator and never as the owner: every stated transaction succeeds (reservation, claim, step, record, hold, expiry); every cross-writer operation fails (remediator writing eval_generation or observed_head_sha, deleting an open row, updating a step). Done: every TestRemediationStore_* runs as rg_remediator; TestRemediationStore_CrossWriterDenied adds the cross-writer cases beside TestControlsChain_GrantsHoldAsEachRole. Deleting an open row is not an error under RLS (the policy hides it), so it asserts zero rows affected.
  • [x] 1.12 Per-role DSNs (INV-0023 F7.1). startControlsWorker in cmd/repo-guardian/controls.go parses cfg.StoreDSN for both halves, so the evaluator and remediator connect as whatever STORE_DSN names and the chart's STORE_DSN_EVALUATOR/_REMEDIATOR are mounted but unread. Read the half's own DSN (config gains both, all falls back to STORE_DSN only when its own is unset), and log the role it connects as. Test: a remediator half refuses to start without a DSN it can resolve, and a split render's evaluator gets only its own. Done: Config.WorkerStoreDSN (own, else STORE_DSN — the fallback also applies to a split role, since store.controls defaults off and those pods carry only STORE_DSN); ingest refuses all three DSNs; openHalfPool logs dsn_env/db_user. Chart: with store.controls on, a split controls pod no longer gets STORE_DSN (only the migrate Job keeps the owner's). TestWorkerStoreDSN, controls_store_test.yaml.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• The truth table and grant tests pass as the application roles.
  • Sixteen concurrent ReserveSlot calls against one repository with max_open_prs = 3 produce exactly three reserved rows.
  • Two concurrent ClaimOperation calls on one key: one gets the row, the other ErrOperationHeld.

docs.title: Phase 2: Evaluator-side hooks: PR observation and starting due remediations
Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 2.1 PR observation in the evaluate activity, through the Evaluation App's PRObserver: ListPullRequests("repo-guardian/") (paginated to completion; a failed page is an observation error, not an empty list) plus GetPullRequest for each tracked PR not in the open list. Matching is by remediations.pr_number, never by branch name alone.
  • [x] 2.2 Observation writes, as rg_evaluator and only the columns it holds: observed_head_sha and observed_at on every open tracked PR; state = 'merged' with closed_at; state = 'closed_by_user' with closed_generation = eval_generation and next_eligible_at = closed_at + reopen_after (from repository_policy_state); a remediation_events row observed with the detail. A PR closed by the Remediation App is not reclassified (its row is already terminal). Done (2.1 + 2.2): activities.observePRs lists once and reads each tracked PR missing from the list; nothing is called when nothing is tracked. ControlsStore.TrackedPullRequests/ObservePullRequests guard every write on state = 'open', event state changes and moved heads only, and observation is best effort (a failure logs and never fails the evaluation). control.PullRequest gained ClosedAt, and Merged reads merged_at too (the list endpoint omits merged). TestControlsStore_ObservePullRequests (as rg_evaluator, with the remediator-column denials).
  • [x] 2.3 pr_event trigger: a pull_request webhook on a repo-guardian/ head signals the evaluation with trigger pr_event, which runs observation only and touches no evaluation column (DESIGN-0032 D24). Priority 2. Done: ingest routes pull_request synchronize/closed/reopened on a repo-guardian/ head (Evaluation App route only); ControlsRouter rechecks a known managed repository with pr_event and never discovers. A bare pr_event re-check (no paths, not unknown, no policy pending) sets EvaluateInput.Observe; Evaluate returns CheckObserved, which keeps the schedule and the iteration (also on failure). On a priority tie coalesce lets a pr_event give way.
  • [x] 2.4 Confirm control_results.intent_revision is computed by the evaluator as DESIGN-0032 D23 states (hash of epoch, generation, apply, effective mode, remediability, control revision); add it if IMPL-0029 did not. Done: intentRevision in internal/store/postgres/controls_evaluation.go hashes exactly D23's inputs; nothing to add.
  • [x] 2.5 StartDueRemediations activity: at the end of each evaluation, read remediation_due for that repository and call client.SignalWithStartWorkflow once per due control with id remediation/<repository id>/<slug>, signal recheck, task queue repo-guardian-remediate, priority 3, WorkflowIDReusePolicy allowing a new run after completion. One activity per evaluation whatever the number of due controls (DESIGN-0032 A1). Done: on RemediationStarter (beside IMPL-0028's StartRemediations, kept for the sweep), reading ControlsStore.DueRemediationsFor. RemediateSignal is now "recheck" (nothing ever sent "remediate"). TestStartDueRemediations.
  • [x] 2.6 Wire StartDueRemediations into EvaluationWorkflow after Record; a deferred or discarded evaluation skips it. Behind one workflow.GetVersion(ctx, "remediation-v1", workflow.DefaultVersion, 1) that 2.9 shares. Done: remediationChange is read once per run in newEvalLoop; version 1 runs StartDueRemediations after a record that recorded something (or was already final) with bounded retries (hookOptions), so a failure is logged and never holds the loop.
  • [x] 2.7 Tests: observation table (open with a new head, merged, user-closed, closed by us, a failed second page, a PR authored by someone else on a repo-guardian/ branch, which is ignored); signal-with-start into a completing workflow, against the result of IMPL-0028's spike; a no-change evaluation starts nothing. Done: TestObservePRs (the table; a remediator-closed row is never tracked, and the store's state = 'open' guard is pinned by TestControlsStore_ObservePullRequests), TestEvaluate_ObserveOnly, TestIntegration_StartRemediationsIntoCompletingWorkflow (100 signal-with-starts into a draining stand-in, none lost), and TestStartDueRemediations plus the 1.10 truth table for "no change starts nothing".
  • [x] 2.8 Store. store.Controls.SetNextDue(ctx, repositoryID, at time.Time) with a sqlc query, plus an integration test that runs as rg_evaluator (the grant, not the owner). Done: SetNextDue (zero clears) on store.Controls; TestControlsStore_SetNextDue.
  • [x] 2.9 Workflow (INV-0023 F3). Write next due per OQ17 on every path that calls scheduleNext (recorded, failed, skipped). It sits behind the same workflow.GetVersion change id as 2.6, so EvaluationWorkflow gains one version marker and one recaptured history, not two. The DefaultVersion branch keeps today's command order exactly. Done: scheduleNext runs the SetNextDue local activity (Evaluator.SetNextDue, by registered name) on version 1, so every path that schedules writes it. TestEvaluationWorkflow_RemediationHooks.
  • [x] 2.10 Replay.
  • TestReplay_CapturedHistories still passes on evaluation_first_run.json.
  • Capture a second history on the new version with go test -tags integration -run TestIntegration_OneEvaluation ./internal/activities -update-histories and commit it beside the old one. Do not overwrite the old history. Done: TestIntegration_OneEvaluation now captures evaluation_remediation_v1.json (version marker, the start activity, the local activity) and asserts next due and its clearing; both histories replay.
  • [x] 2.11 Parked repositories. A park ends the workflow run, so ParkRepository clears next_due_at and the card reads "— parked". Integration test. Done: the ParkRepository query sets next_due_at = NULL; TestIntegration_OneEvaluation asserts it after the park.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• An evaluation that changes a remediable control's generation in a remediate assignment starts exactly one RemediationWorkflow signal for it; a second evaluation while it runs produces a signal, not a second execution.
  • Observation as rg_evaluator cannot write any remediator column (grant test).
  • After one evaluation, /repositories/{id} returns a next_due_at inside the jitter window of EVAL_INTERVAL; a parked repository returns none; both the old and the new evaluation history replay.

docs.title: Phase 3: RemediationWorkflow, activities and the GitHub fake
Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 3.1 internal/workflows/remediation.go: RemediationWorkflow with a recheck signal channel and a recheckPending flag. A run loops: run one remediation (activities below), drain signals, re-read eval_generation, intent_revision and observed_head_sha through a ReadRemediationState activity, and loop again if any moved or a signal arrived; otherwise complete. ContinueAsNew after 100 loops.
  • [x] 3.2 Register the workflow and its activities only on the remediator worker (repo-guardian-remediate, worker deployment repo-guardian-remediate); a depguard or registration test proves the evaluator never registers them.
  • [x] 3.3 Activity options: every remediation activity heartbeats and carries a ScheduleToClose timeout; StartToClose below it; retry policy non-retryable on ErrOperationHeld, ErrStaleEpoch and holds. The activity exits cleanly when ClaimOperation returns ErrOperationHeld.
  • [x] 3.4 Budget: the remediation run acquires the per-installation budget workflow at id installation/remediate/<installation id> (the app-dimensioned id from IMPL-0028), with DefaultLeaseTTL sized to cover the remediation activities' ScheduleToClose.
  • [x] 3.5 Epoch fence helper fence(ctx, repo, control, epoch): re-reads effective_mode, remediable, the write set and epoch and returns ErrStaleEpoch when any changed. Called immediately before every external write in Phases 4 and 5; a lint-style test walks the write call sites and fails if one is not preceded by it.
  • [x] 3.6 Classification in the run, in order: github.AsThrottled (either App) → defer through the controls line's deferral path (a workflow timer, never a sleep in an activity); access loss → stop with hold = 'permission' or let resolution's effective_mode override take it; then outcomes. A secondary-limit 403 is a throttle before it is a permission failure.
  • [x] 3.7 Remediator bot identity: resolve the Remediation App's bot user id at remediator startup (GET /app for the slug, then GET /users/<slug>[bot] for the id and type = Bot), cache it, and fail startup when it cannot be resolved. Reuse IMPL-0028's resolver if it built one.
  • [x] 3.8 GitHub fake for remediation (internal/github/ghfake or the package IMPL-0028 created): stateful repositories with real three-way merge for update-branch, createCommitOnBranch expectedHeadOid and push semantics, ref create that fails on an existing branch, PR authorship by user id and head repository id, fork PRs, and a request log so tests can assert no branch delete was ever called.
  • [x] 3.9 Replay: capture a RemediationWorkflow history from the first behaviour test and add it to internal/workflows/testdata with a replay test, as today's capture does for EvaluationWorkflow.
  • [x] 3.10 Tests (time-skipping environment): a signal during a run produces one extra loop, not a second run; overlapping attempts of one activity act once; a throttle defers without recording.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• The workflow runs end to end against the fake with a no-op remediation and completes; the replay test passes in CI.
  • The evaluator binary's dependency graph does not reach the remediation activities or the Writer package (depguard).

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 4.1 Re-read: assignment, result and latest remediation; stop unless needs_remediation (the remediation_due predicate for this one row).
  • [x] 4.2 Find: GetRef("repo-guardian/<slug>") and the open PR on it. Tracked means a remediations row with this branch and a PR number.
  • [x] 4.3 Untracked branch: adopt only when an open PR on it is authored by the Remediation App's bot user id with type Bot and head repository id equal to this repository's. Otherwise hold stale_branch when the head equals the journaled bot head of a closed_by_user row, else foreign_branch. Commit author text is never consulted.
  • [x] 4.4 No branch: ReserveSlot; ErrPRCap holds pr_cap. Write the intent (base_sha = pinned default-branch head, branch, expected_head, intent_revision, assignment_epoch) before any external step.
  • [x] 4.5 Tracked PR: verify the head descends from the last journaled bot commit (ListCommits or compare); otherwise hold conflict, upsert the sticky comment (OQ9), never force-push. When the default branch was renamed, UpdatePullRequestBase first.
  • [x] 4.6 Behind main: UpdateBranch with expected_head_sha = the observed head. 422 merge conflict → hold conflict with the comment; 422 head moved → defer; any other 422 → error; 202 → defer, and the next run re-pins the head the merge produced. Journal pr_rebased.
  • [x] 4.7 Fresh Evaluate at the pinned default-branch head through the Remediation App's Reader (D22: never stored status).
  • [x] 4.8 Call the type's Remediate (built in IMPL-0029, per its OQ2) and control.ValidateChangeSet on the result, then the self-check (evaluate the changed content; refuse when a Fixed rule does not pass or a passing rule regresses). A change set with nothing in Fixed is recorded as a recommendation-style no-op on the PR row and not retried until the generation moves (DESIGN-0031 D14).
  • [x] 4.9 Obsolete bot edits: for each path the journal shows the bot wrote that the current change set no longer owns, revert it only where the current blob equals the journaled blob_sha; a human's edit to the same path is left alone. Reverts join the same commit.
  • [x] 4.10 Compliant at the fresh read with an open PR: close it as closed_compliant (sticky comment, ClosePullRequest), never delete the branch. Drift found by the fresh read keeps it open.
  • [x] 4.11 New branch: CreateRef at base_sha, journal branch_created. Commit: Writer.Commit(branch, expected_head, changes, message); journal committed with every path and its blob SHA; ErrExpectedHeadMismatch → defer and re-pin.
  • [x] 4.12 PR: CreatePullRequest, or on 422 "already exists" list by head and adopt the open one authored by the App; otherwise UpdatePullRequest with the re-rendered title and body. Labels via the PR template. Journal pr_created/pr_updated; the reserved row becomes open with pr_number and pr_url.
  • [x] 4.13 PR title, body and labels rendered from the evaluation through the control's pr {} block and internal/template (template.PRVars with .Control, .Fixed, .Manual, .Notes), defaults per OQ10; bodies over 65000 characters truncated with the existing marker.
  • [x] 4.14 Recovery: a PR create that failed after the commit is completed by the next attempt, which finds the branch at exactly the journaled committed_sha under the same operation_key.
  • [x] 4.15 Record (RecordRun), then last_remediation_at, then the workflow's loop check (3.1).
  • [x] 4.16 Behaviour tests, one per DESIGN-0032 Testing Strategy bullet under "Remediation workflow": onboarding opens the PR; a no-change evaluation does nothing; human edits plus a main merge; main changes the same file (mergeable proposal or conflict; retired-rule revert; human edit kept); human closes (cooldown, closed_generation, stale_branch, fresh branch after a human deletes it); compliant close only after a fresh read; merged is terminal with no branch delete in the fake's log; expected-head mismatch (concurrent push, rewind, delete-and-recreate) defers; update-branch 202/422 conflict/422 head-moved; spoofed bot author and a same-named fork PR refused; create-after-commit recovery and 422 adoption; every failing control at once near the cap with crashes injected between reservation, commit, create and record (open count never above the cap, reservations reclaimed, ordinal order).

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• Every behaviour test passes under -race.
  • No test in the suite records a branch delete or a force push in the fake's request log.
  • A run killed at any step and re-run completes with exactly one PR and one commit per change.

docs.title: Phase 5: API remediations: recommend, direct and workflow
Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 5.1 recommend (default): a kind = 'api' row in state recommended with proposal JSONB (per resource: key, before, after). No GitHub write. Uses the slot only for the one-open index, not the PR cap.
  • [x] 5.2 Supersede: a recommendation whose intent_revision no longer matches becomes superseded and a new row runs with the new intent (an apply toggle with no file change is a new intent, D23). resolved when the control is compliant at a fresh read.
  • [x] 5.3 direct (D14): per resource in ChangeSet.API, fence, read, write through Writer (UpdateRepository, UpsertRuleset for repository-sourced rulesets by id, SetCustomProperties, UpsertLabel, DeleteLabel), read back and compare; journal api_write with before and after. All done → applied; any failure → failed with the completed steps; the next run resumes from the journal and writes only what is not yet journaled done.
  • [x] 5.4 workflow (D15): only for types implementing WorkflowApply (custom_properties); the change becomes a PR on the Phase 4 path carrying .github/workflows/repo-guardian-<slug>.yml, with property values only through the IMPL-0020 A2 env-indirection shape (yamlq, propenv). A 403 on the workflow path holds permission with the Workflows permission named in the note.
  • [x] 5.5 Per-write gating: a write whose prerequisite read failed is Blocked and not attempted, even inside a non-compliant control; a property absent from the org schema is Blocked while the rest syncs.
  • [x] 5.6 Chart and docs: the Remediation App's permission table gains Workflows: write only when a policy has a workflow control; the chart README notes it.
  • [x] 5.7 Tests (DESIGN-0032 "Direct API apply"): fail the second of three writes and resume; mutate a target concurrently; toggle apply from recommend to direct without a file change (supersede, then apply); restore the Remediation App's access; a catalog-info parse failure never clears properties; unrelated human state survives.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• A partially failed direct apply shows exactly its completed steps through the store, and a re-run finishes it without repeating them.
  • recommend makes zero GitHub writes (fake request log).

docs.title: Phase 6: Sweep, lifecycle maintenance and Remediation App discovery
Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 6.1 remediation-sweep schedule (hourly, repo-guardian-remediate), ensured only by remediator pods: DueRemediations(REMEDIATION_SWEEP_BATCH) → signal-with-start at priority 4; one service_runs row per run.
  • [x] 6.2 Maintenance in the same schedule: MaintenanceCandidates(REMEDIATION_MAINTENANCE_BATCH) dispatching expire (ExpireReservations, metric), withdraw (close the PR with a comment as closed_withdrawn, or end the recommendation as withdrawn), supersede, and close_compliant (a fresh read in the same activity; close only when it agrees). A refused write holds permission and is shown as blocked cleanup.
  • [x] 6.3 remediation_cleanup_latency_seconds from the observed withdrawal or compliance time to the closing write.
  • [x] 6.4 controls-discovery-remediate schedule: lists the Remediation App's installations and repositories and refreshes the app = 'remediate' rows of app_installations and app_repository_access under the row-level policy; a change re-resolves the affected repositories (IMPL-0029's resolution trigger).
  • [x] 6.5 Role partitioning test: an evaluator pod never ensures remediation-sweep or controls-discovery-remediate; a remediator never ensures the evaluation schedules.
  • [x] 6.6 Config: REMEDIATION_RESERVATION_TTL (default 1h), REMEDIATION_SWEEP_BATCH, REMEDIATION_MAINTENANCE_BATCH, REMEDIATOR_CONCURRENCY, REMEDIATOR_DB_POOL_SIZE, with validation tests and chart values.
  • [x] 6.7 Tests (DESIGN-0032 "Lifecycle maintenance"): withdraw a control, exclude and park its repository, remove its org, switch it to evaluate, each with a PR or a recommendation outstanding; every artifact reaches its terminal state or blocked cleanup with no fresh failing result required.
  • [x] 6.8 Prune checks (INV-0023 F7.2). ControlsSnapshotWorkflow (internal/workflows/controls_service.go) ignores SnapshotInput.Retention and its comment says the controls line keeps no checks table, which is wrong. Add a PruneControlsChecks(before) activity after the snapshot, behind a GetVersion (captured snapshot histories must replay), deleting checks finished before now − CHECKS_RETENTION, and fix the comment. Lands with 6.9, so no repository reads "never evaluated" after a prune. Integration test as the evaluator role.
  • [x] 6.9 last_checked_at (OQ19). RecordEvaluation writes repositories.last_checked_at (the controls migration grants rg_evaluator UPDATE (last_checked_at)), and the API's last_evaluated_at reads that column in place of max(checks.finished_at), dropping the join. Fenced with the rest of the record (a stale-epoch discard writes nothing). Integration test: prune every check, and the repository still reports its last evaluation. Update CLAUDE.md, which says the controls line never writes last_checked_at.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• With no evaluation running, a withdrawn control's open PR is closed as closed_withdrawn within one sweep interval.
  • A crash between reservation and PR creation frees the slot within REMEDIATION_RESERVATION_TTL plus one sweep interval.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 7.1 Metrics in internal/metrics: remediation_runs_total{org,control,result}, remediation_prs_open{org,control,age_bucket} (leader-published from the store, queried with max by), remediation_blocked_total{org,reason}, remediation_reservations_expired_total{org}, remediation_cleanup_latency_seconds{org}, store_pool_wait_seconds{role}. No repository or PR label.
  • [x] 7.2 Alerts in the generated catalogue (internal/monitoring/alert) per OQ11, rare-event ones with alert.firstOrIncrease; mirror them in the chart PrometheusRule; make monitoring-generate, make lint-monitoring, make lint-alerts.
  • [x] 7.3 Dashboard panels: remediation backlog, open PRs by age, blocked by reason, run results; E4 log matchers for hold and adoption log lines, with TestLogLines_AreStillEmittedByTheBinary covering them.
  • [x] 7.4 API: /remediations (filters kind, state, org, control, age, hold; open PRs older than N days; recommendations outstanding; blocked cleanup); the remediation object (kind, state, intent_revision, observed_head_sha, acknowledged_head_sha, hold, proposal, steps) taking the Remediation schema name; the latest remediation on /repositories/{id}/controls; remediation events in /repositories/{id}/events; remediation backlog on /summary and /status. apitest with kin-openapi validation and TestAPIQueries_AreScoped extended.
  • 7.5 Moved to IMPL-0032 Phase 6 (2026-10-18): the Remediations view, the repository remediation panel and the status backlog are UI work and live with the rest of DESIGN-0037's pages. DESIGN-0037 supersedes D32's "Findings view is removed": both views exist.

The API the controls UI reads (DESIGN-0037 §API / Interface Changes), moved here from IMPL-0032 so it shares the schema, openapi.yaml and one PR with the remediation API. Each task is the full vertical slice: api/openapi.yaml → make generate-api → queries_controls/api_*.sql → make generate-sql → postgres.APIReader + api.Reader method → handler → a case in TestEndpoints_ValidateAgainstTheSpec (it fails on any operation without one) → make generate-ui-api → make lint-api lint-sql. Every new query lives in an api_*.sql file so TestAPIQueries_AreScoped lints its scope predicate.

  • [x] 7.6 /compliance/history?aggregate=none|fleet|org|control (default none, today's rows). New queries sum the ten bucket columns of compliance_snapshots per UTC day (snapshot_at::date, not the raw timestamp, so per-org snapshot times on one day collapse) and per org or control, and compute percent/coverage with floor_percent in SQL, never averaging. The response shape follows OQ14. Store tests:
  • the fleet series equals summing none with ControlPosture.Plus on the same fixture;
  • the org series agrees with ControlCompliance for the latest day.
  • [x] 7.7 GET /results.
  • Query api_results.sql over control_results ⋈ control_assignments ⋈ repositories ⋈ repository_policy_state, with the posture bucket computed by the same CASE as compliance.sql. It filters bucket (OQ15; ResultRow carries status too, but the query takes no status parameter), control, org, decision (from control_assignments), and rule: an EXISTS on rule_results with status fail or error.
  • Order and paging: sort since_asc (default) or since_desc on (last_changed_at, repository_id, control_id), with a keyset cursor bound to the filter hash (cursor.go).
  • Rows: each ResultRow carries repository id/org/name, control id/version, decision, status, bucket, failing_rules[], reason (the first failing rule's evidence reason, else its evidence_kind) and last_changed_at.
  • total: counted on the first page only (no cursor), in the same read-only transaction; later pages omit it (OQ16).
  • Tests: integration tests for scope (two-org authz), keyset paging with ties on last_changed_at, each filter, and total matching the filter. A parity test proves that with no filters, total for non-compliant equals Summary.compliance.non_compliant on the fixture.
  • [x] 7.8 Repository.compliance (Posture over the repository's assignments, same bucket CASE) on /repositories and /repositories/{id}, in one grouped query per page, not N+1. Integration test: one repository with mixed buckets.
  • [x] 7.9 Summary.parked_by_reason and Summary.controls_failing, computed in Go in GetSummary from the store.SummaryView it already reads (Repositories per park reason; Compliance rows with non_compliant > 0, counted by distinct control). No new SQL. apitest cases.
  • [x] 7.10 Summary.finding_age: six fixed buckets (<1d, 1–7d, 7–30d, 30–90d, 90–180d, 180d+) of now() − last_changed_at over results in the non_compliant bucket, in api_summary.sql with the scope predicate. The bucket sum equals Summary.compliance.non_compliant (test). The fixture spans every boundary.
  • [x] 7.11 Summary.open_prs_by_age (<1d, 1–7d, 7–30d, 30d+ of open pull-request remediations by created_at).
  • [x] 7.12 GET /remediations/activity?days=1..90 (default 14) → [{day, opened, closed}] (opened by created_at, closed by closed_at, per UTC day, scoped).
  • [x] 7.13 /results?pr_stale= and ResultRow.remediation (state, PR number/url, age). sort=pr_age joins the /results sorts; pr_stale is open pull-request remediations at least 30 days old.
  • [x] 7.14 Perf fixture (OQ18). Extend TestAPIPerf to seed rule_results and 90 days of compliance_snapshots at fleet size, add /results (each filter) and the history aggregates to the measured set, and log EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) for /results. Record the numbers in this doc. If a sequential scan shows, add a results_index controls migration (control_results (control_id, status, last_changed_at)) numbered after Phase 1's, bump ControlsSchemaVersion with it, and extend the controls dry-run test. Done: the seed adds one rule result per result (200k, failing where the result does) and 90 days of daily snapshots per org and control (18k rows). The default /results EXPLAIN showed a sequential scan over all 200k control_results, so 00008_results_index.sql adds control_results_control_status_changed (ControlsSchemaVersion 8; the dry-run test asserts the index), and both results queries filter cr.status directly when the bucket names a status, which is what lets the planner use it: bucket=non_compliant went from 353ms to 127ms EXPLAIN ANALYZE (bitmap index scan, 28,571 rows). Measured at 20k repositories, 200 requests each, auth off (whole fleet):
Endpoint p50 p99 /results?limit=50 318.7ms 342.1ms /results?bucket=non_compliant 129.7ms 145.0ms /results?control=control-3 32.2ms 35.9ms /results?rule=exists&bucket=non_compliant 514.1ms 614.6ms /results?org=org-3 29.8ms 44.5ms /results?decision=baseline 209.4ms 226.4ms /results?sort=since_desc 320.9ms 347.4ms /results?sort=pr_age 790.5ms 1129.6ms /results?pr_stale=true 547.3ms 565.8ms /compliance/history?days=90&aggregate=fleet 22.5ms 37.9ms /compliance/history?days=90&aggregate=org 42.2ms 55.1ms /compliance/history?days=90&aggregate=control 28.9ms 41.1ms /summary 478.4ms 492.1ms /orgs (unchanged, IMPL-0029 7.4) 199.2ms 364.4ms

Control, org and the history aggregates meet the 100ms target. The whole-fleet shapes do not: every one computes the posture bucket over the whole population, the first page also counts it (OQ16), and pr_age/pr_stale add the latest-remediation lateral per row. A scoped caller (one org) reads the 30–45ms shapes. Closing the whole-fleet gap (a materialised bucket column, or dropping the first-page total) is open, the same as /orgs. - [x] 7.15 Spec descriptions: Event.from_status/to_status document rule statuses on rule-level events; ParkReason lists suspended. Bump info.version (2.1.0, or with 7.4 if it already did) and document every addition in docs/usage/api.md. - [x] 7.16 Held results (OQ20). Expose the results held before a pull request exists (control_results.hold in pr_cap, foreign_branch, stale_branch, conflict) from /remediations?hold= as rows with kind = pull_request, no id and no pull request, under the same cursor (OQ20). The Remediation schema documents that row shape, and the two-org authz test covers it, so the Remediations view's Held list is complete.

a compliant close is always on, after a fresh read TestConvergence_OrphanCleanupDisabled_NoDeletion retired: v1 behaviour, no replacement — orphan_cleanup is gone; files are reverted, never deleted TestConvergence_DeleteFileError_IncrementsCounter_Continues retired: v1 behaviour, no replacement — the controls Writer deletes no file outside a commit, and pr_orphan_left_total is gone TestConvergence_Bundle_AddAndRemove_RendersBothSections retired: v1 behaviour, no replacement — one pull request per control, so there is no bundle TestConvergence_RenovateFirst_BothVariantsDeleted retired: v1 behaviour, no replacement — dependency_updates owns the renovate-or-dependabot choice as one control TestConvergence_RenovateFirst_RemovesDependabot retired: as above TestConvergence_RenovateFirst_GateClosesMidFlight_RestoresDependabot retired: as above; Drop every in-place adopt/backfill/verify-shadow claim. - [x] 8.4 v2-overview.md remediation parts: one PR per control on repo-guardian/<slug>, max_open_prs, reopen_after, search_terms/foreign-PR dropped, apply modes, holds, never deleting branches. - [x] 8.5 v2-onboarding.md remediation parts: the Remediation App's permissions and events (Workflows only for workflow controls), its webhook path, the remediator role, REMEDIATION_* and REMEDIATOR_* config, enabling mode = "remediate" for one org. - [x] 8.6 docs/operations/rgctl.md: link the cutover runbook's steps 3 and 6; note one record per App. Landed on main in PR #225 (rgctl.md and tools/rgctl live there): an "At the v2 cutover" section, the "v2 adopts edited PRs" line corrected (it adopts only its own Remediation App's), and the stale TestPRIdentity_IsFrozen comment dropped from tools/rgctl/internal/prs/identity.go. - [x] 8.7 CLAUDE.md: a remediation contract entry (record-is-narrow via grants, observed/acknowledged heads, epoch fence before every write, adopt by bot user id, never delete a branch, never force-push, nil-vs-terminal recommendation states) and the architecture lines for the new packages. - [x] 8.8 docz update impl design and review the regenerated indices. docs.title: Phase 9: Remediation rc and the homelab fresh install
docs.text: Human-run. The homelab has dev (v2 rc) and prod (v1) managing disjoint sets of repositories; both stop before the new install, so the split does not matter.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 9.1 Tag the remediation rc (dont-release label, manual v2.0.0-rc.N tag, chart 2.0.0-rc.N bumped by hand) per OQ4.
  • [ ] 9.2 Create or prepare the Apps per OQ5; mount each key as a file from its Secret, never as an env var.
  • [ ] 9.3 Stop writers: scale dev's v2 worker to zero and prod's v1 deployment to zero; confirm no old pod runs.
  • [ ] 9.4 On dev's Temporal: delete the discovery and snapshot schedules and terminate every running execution on task queue repo-guardian.
  • [ ] 9.5 Record open PRs once per old App: rgctl prs list --org <org> --format json --out <app>-<org>.json with prod's v1 App credentials and again with dev's App credentials, for every org each manages.
  • [ ] 9.6 Install the rc fresh: new database (owner plus rg_evaluator and rg_remediator provisioned by the chart), new Temporal namespace, both new webhook URLs set on the Apps; every assignment starts in evaluate mode.
  • [ ] 9.7 Verify evaluation: both worker deployments current, discovery complete, posture per org against the last v1/rc state, no unmeasurable surprises, KEDA scaling per queue.
  • [ ] 9.8 Remediation in one org (donaldgifford): set mode = "remediate"; watch the first per-control PRs, holds and the cap; close that org's old PRs per OQ6.
  • [ ] 9.9 Remaining orgs by policy change, per OQ7; close their old PRs per OQ6 with rgctl prs close --from <file> --yes (add --delete-branch only by choice; edited PRs are skipped).
  • [ ] 9.10 Keep both old databases (and the old charts' values) per OQ8; uninstall dev and prod releases once the window passes; then uninstall or reduce the old Apps.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• One v2 install manages every repository dev and prod managed; no old pod runs.
  • Every old open PR is either closed with a pointer comment or left deliberately (edited), with the rgctl output kept.
  • The first remediation org has had per-control PRs open, updated and closed through the full lifecycle with no unexplained hold.

docs.title: OQ1: Where do the remediation tables land in the goose chain?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: In 00003_controls_results, created by IMPL-0029 before its evaluate-only rc, as DESIGN-0032 numbers them, so the rc schema is already the GA schema and this plan adds behaviour only; Task 1.1 then verifies rather than creates.
  • (b) A new additive file 00005_remediation in this plan. Works on an rc database in place, but departs from the design's up-front numbering.
  • (c) Edit 00003 in this plan and discard any evaluate-only rc database. Clean chain, but breaks an rc install that already ran 00003.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ2: Who owns PR observation and the start-due-remediations activity?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: This plan (Phase 2). Both act on remediations rows, which do not exist before remediation; IMPL-0029's EvaluationWorkflow leaves the call site after Record.
  • (b) IMPL-0029, so EvaluationWorkflow is complete when it ships.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ3: Which control types remediate in v2.0.0?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: All built-in types. File types through PRs; API types recommend by default with direct and workflow (custom_properties) available by opt-in, as D14 and D15 decided.
  • (b) File types through PRs only; API types recommend only, with direct and workflow after GA. Smaller first release, Phase 5 shrinks to 5.1, 5.2 and 5.7.
  • (c) File types only; API types evaluate-only.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ4: Does remediation ship as an rc before v2.0.0?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Yes, one or more v2.0.0-rc.N tags (dont-release plus a manual tag); the homelab fresh install runs on the rc, and GA is cut from the same code after Phase 9.
  • (b) Cut v2.0.0 directly once Phases 1 to 8 merge and do the fresh install on GA.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ5: Which Apps does the fresh install use?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Two new Apps (Evaluation, read-only; Remediation, write). New bot identities make the old PRs plainly distinct, and both old Apps stay installed until their PRs are closed with rgctl, then are uninstalled.
  • (b) Reduce prod's v1 App to read-only and make it the Evaluation App (D1), and create one new Remediation App. One fewer App, but its installations and webhook URL change under live v1 PRs.
  • (c) Reuse dev's App as the Remediation App and create a new Evaluation App.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ6: When are the old deployments' PRs closed?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Per org, when that org turns on remediate. Old PRs keep proposing their fixes while the org is evaluate-only, and are closed with a pointer comment once per-control PRs replace them. rgctl's per-org record files already fit this.
  • (b) All at once right after the install is verified (DESIGN-0032 step 6 as written).
  • (c) All at once after every org is on remediate.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ7: What gates turning remediation on for the remaining orgs, and GA?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: donaldgifford in remediate for 7 days with every hold explained and no PR over the cap, then the remaining orgs; GA after 7 more days with no unexplained conflict, foreign_branch or permission hold.
  • (b) 3 days each.
  • (c) No time gate: flip the remaining orgs once the first org's PRs look right, and tag GA when they do.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ8: How long are the old databases kept?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Until v2.0.0 has run in the homelab for 14 days, then a pg_dump archive is kept and the databases are dropped with the dev and prod uninstall.
  • (b) Until the last old PR is closed, then dropped with no archive.
  • (c) Indefinitely.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ9: What does the sticky PR comment look like?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: One sticky comment per PR with marker <!-- repo-guardian:control:v1 --> on row 1, edited in place for holds (conflict), the compliant close and the withdrawn close, with a content hash so identical states make no API call (the IMPL-0013 pattern).
  • (b) Reuse v1's <!-- repo-guardian:reconcile-log:v1 --> marker.
  • (c) A new comment per event.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ10: Is there a built-in default PR body?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Yes. An embedded default title (chore: <control title>) and body (what it fixes from .Fixed, what needs a human from .Manual and .Notes, a link to the repository's controls page) in internal/template; the enterprise or control pr {} block overrides it field by field.
  • (b) No default: a control without a pr {} block fails policy load.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ11: Which remediation holds alert?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: foreign_branch, permission and remediation_app_no_access/suspended alert (warning, with firstOrIncrease); conflict alerts only when held over 7 days; pr_cap, stale_branch and cooldown never alert (routine, shown in the UI).
  • (b) Every blocked reason alerts.
  • (c) Only permission alerts.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ12: Where is v2.0.0 tagged?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Fast-forward main to v2 and tag v2.0.0 on main, with the dont-release label on the merge PR and the tag pushed by hand, so main is the v2 line from GA on.
  • (b) Tag on v2 and merge to main later.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ13: How many PRs?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-07: (a). The maintainer's direction: one PR per plan, so the agent does every task it can without waiting on a merge between phases. A task that needs the maintainer (homelab runs, GitHub App registration, approving a large git rm, release tags) is marked deferred - human required and done by the maintainer, during review or after the merge.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: one PR for the whole plan into v2, with dont-release; Phases 9 and 10 are deferred - human required.
  • (b) One PR per phase into v2. Smaller reviews, but every phase waits on a merge.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ14: The shape of aggregated history points
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-19: (a). DESIGN-0037's API section records the relaxed fields.

HistoryPoint requires org, control_id and decision. A fleet point has none of them, and a control point has no org.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: loosen HistoryPoint. org, control_id and decision become optional, and the description states which are present per aggregate. One schema and one hook; the only consumer is our UI and spec 2.x is pre-release. It does relax a required field, contrary to DESIGN-0037's "nothing changes shape", so record it there.
  • (b) A separate AggregatePoint schema returned when aggregate is not none (a oneOf on the response). Strictly additive, but the generated client needs a discriminator, and the strict server's oneOf response is awkward.
  • (c) A new endpoint /compliance/trend?by=fleet|org|control leaving /compliance/history untouched. Additive and clean, but two history endpoints to explain.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ15: What /results filters on: status or bucket
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-19: (a). DESIGN-0037's vocabulary now reads "a finding is a result in the non-compliant bucket".

The nav badge and DESIGN-0037's "N of M" read Summary.compliance.non_compliant, which is the posture bucket. Raw control_results.status = non_compliant also includes stale results and rows under access-denied parks and suspended installs.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: filter on bucket (the ten posture buckets, computed by the shared CASE). The Findings page asks for bucket=non_compliant, and ResultRow carries both status and bucket. The badge, total, finding_age and the page agree by construction. DESIGN-0037's vocabulary is refined to "a finding is a result in the non-compliant bucket".
  • (b) Filter on raw status. Simpler SQL, but the page shows stale and parked results the fleet count does not, and the counts disagree.
  • (c) Both parameters. Flexible, but two ways to ask the same question.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ16: When /results computes total
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-19: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: count on the first page only (no cursor), in the same read-only transaction. The client keeps it across "Load more". One count per filter change, and the number is stable while paging.
  • (b) Count on every page. Always fresh, but repeats the count for each page.
  • (c) No exact total: show "N loaded" and use the Summary count only when no filter is set. Cheapest, but filtered views lose "of M".
  • other:

docs.title: OQ17: How next due is persisted
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-19: (a).

RecordEvaluation runs before scheduleNext draws the jitter, and the failed and skipped paths never record.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a SetNextDue local activity after scheduleNext on every path, behind the remediation-v1 change id that 2.6 introduces (one marker for both). One write per iteration, uniform across recorded, failed and skipped, with no reordering of the existing commands.
  • (b) Draw the jitter before recording and pass NextDue in RecordEvaluationInput (version-gated reorder). No extra activity, but the failed and skipped paths still need their own write, and the gate is more involved.
  • (c) Drop next_due_at from the API and the card. No workflow change, but operators lose "when is this looked at next".
  • other:

docs.title: OQ18: The control_results index
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-19: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: decide from task 7.14's plan output. Add 00005 only if /results shows a sequential scan at fleet size. This follows DESIGN-0037's Data Model.
  • (b) Add the index up front. One less decision, but a schema migration we may not need.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ19: last_evaluated_at once checks are pruned
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-19: (a). Task 6.9.

last_evaluated_at is max(checks.finished_at) for the repository. Pruning checks past CHECKS_RETENTION (6.8) makes a repository idle longer than the retention read "never evaluated".

  • (a) ✅ recommended: persist repositories.last_checked_at from RecordEvaluation (the evaluator gets UPDATE (last_checked_at)), and the API reads it instead of the checks aggregate. One column write per evaluation; the value survives any retention, and the API query loses a join.
  • (b) Keep the newest successful check per repository when pruning. No new write, but the prune query is more involved and the API still aggregates.
  • (c) Accept "never" past the retention (90 days by default, longer than EVAL_INTERVAL by far). Nothing to build, but a parked repository reads "never" after three months.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ20: Where the Held list reads branch holds from
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-19: (a).

remediations.hold is permission only. pr_cap, foreign_branch, stale_branch and conflict sit on control_results.hold, often before any remediations row exists. The Remediations view's Held list (DESIGN-0037) needs both.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: /remediations?hold= also returns held results with no remediation row, as rows with kind = pull_request, no id and no pull request, so one query and one cursor back the view. The Remediation schema documents the row shape.
  • (b) /results?hold= for the result holds, and the view merges the two lists. Each endpoint stays pure, but the view pages two cursors.
  • (c) Show only remediations.hold in the view and branch holds on the repository page. Simplest, but "what is stuck" needs two places.
  • other:

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Rebuild the look and layout of the v2 business UI and the public status page to DESIGN-0036: one dark theme declared once as Tailwind tokens, bundled fonts under the unchanged CSP, a shell with an icon sidebar, top bar, breadcrumbs and a shared page header, the Fleet, Rules, Orgs, Findings and Repository pages re-laid out on the data the read-only API serves today, a findings detail drawer with evidence and a timeline, a designed status page, and a set of generic table, grid, drawer, chip and chart components that IMPL-0029 task 8.7 builds the Controls views on. The last code phase adds the five small, additive API fields the design names, each un-hiding one panel.

The picture of the result is ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html. Every task below that says "as the mockup draws it" means that file's route; where the mockup and this plan disagree, DESIGN-0036 wins and the mockup is fixed in the same change.

Implements: DESIGN-0036 (all sections; Open Questions taken at their ✅ recommendations unless the Open Questions below say otherwise), the UI consequences of DESIGN-0027 §The UI, and the additive API changes listed in DESIGN-0036 §API / Interface Changes.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• ui/web/src/index.css tokens, fontsource fonts, the Vite inline limit and a build guard over dist/.
  • The primitive and chart set in ui/web/src/components/ui/ and components/charts/, the badge tone table, formatTime with the Local/UTC toggle.
  • The shell (router.tsx → components/shell/): top bar, sidebar from a nav array, breadcrumbs, page header, org scope popover, range tabs, command palette, avatar menu, collapsed sidebar under 900px.
  • Fleet, Rules, rule detail, Orgs grid, org detail, Findings with the drawer, Repository, History and Policy restyles, and the status page.
  • The one BFF change (UI_DOCS_URL → docs_url in /ui/config) and the matching chart value ui.docsUrl.
  • Unit, component, build-guard, Playwright, axe and screenshot tests; updates to docs/usage/ui.md, ui/README.md and CLAUDE.md.
  • Five additive API changes, each with its sqlc query, handler, apitest case, regenerated server and client, and the UI panel it un-hides: aggregate= on /compliance/history, sort= on /findings, Summary.finding_age[], Status.compliance.history[] plus Status.operations, and OrgSummary.open_prs.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Any write path. The drawer's actions slot stays empty; no POST route is added to the BFF (IMPL-0029 8.7 owns re-evaluate).
  • A light theme, a portal shell (app switcher, bell), the "compliance drivers" map, the PR throughput card (DESIGN-0036 OQ15, deferred), a standalone /repos list (OQ11).
  • CSP, session, OIDC or proxy changes. The CSP string in ui/server/static.ts does not change.
  • Database tables or migrations. Every API addition is a query over existing columns.
  • Replacing lib/evidence.ts renderers (INV-0021 / IMPL-0029) or the Controls, Remediations and /policies views (IMPL-0029, IMPL-0030).
  • Grafana dashboards and alerts (DESIGN-0022, generated).

docs.title: How the phases are ordered
docs.text:
Phases 1 to 7 are code, each ending with make lint-ui, make test-ui and, from Phase 2 on, make test-ui-e2e green, with a commit per numbered task. Phase 1 is tokens, fonts and the component and chart set, so every page after it is composition. Phase 2 is the shell and the page anatomy; it is the phase that moves Playwright selectors, so the e2e suite is repaired here once. Phases 3 and 4 are the pages, in the order the design's rollout plan gives: Fleet and Rules first because they exercise every chart, then the three table-shaped pages and the drawer, which produce the generic DataTable, GroupGrid, DetailDrawer and FilterChips that IMPL-0029 reuses. Phase 5 is the status page, isolated because it is public and privacy-guarded. Phase 6 is accessibility, screenshots, docs and the removal of what the restyle made dead. Phase 7 is Go: the five API additions, each its own task, each un-hiding a panel that Phases 3 to 5 built hidden. Phase 8 is human-run: the rc image, the homelab deploy and the review of the pages against the mockup.

The plan lands as one PR into v2 with the dont-release label (OQ1) and must merge before IMPL-0029 task 8.7 starts (DESIGN-0036 OQ12). Phase 8 is deferred - human required.

docs.title: OQ1: One PR or two?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-16: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: one PR for the whole plan into v2 with dont-release, Phases 1 to 7 included, Phase 8 deferred - human required; the API additions are small and the UI panels that depend on them are built hidden, so the PR is consistent at every commit.
  • (b) Two PRs: Phases 1 to 6 (UI only, ui/** paths filter) then Phase 7 (Go + UI un-hiding). Smaller reviews; the first PR ships five hidden panels and the second waits on a merge.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ2: Do the two findings-shaped API additions ship here?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-16: (a).

sort=pr_age on /findings (7.2) and Summary.finding_age[] (7.3) extend endpoints IMPL-0029 replaces with controls views and the evaluations endpoint.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: ship both here; the SQL is a dozen lines over findings, the controls line needs the same age histogram and oldest-PR ordering over its results table, and 8.7 ports the two queries alongside the views it replaces. Note the port in IMPL-0029 8.7's task text when this merges.
  • (b) Defer both to IMPL-0029 and leave the age panel and sort chip hidden until then.
  • (c) Ship finding_age (a summary number that survives any model) and defer sort.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ3: How are component behaviours tested under bun test?
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-16: (a).

Today's only component test renders with renderToStaticMarkup, which cannot exercise focus, keyboard or state.

Implementation note (task 1.8): the DOM is registered by importing ui/web/testing/dom.ts first in a behaviour test and released in its afterAll, not by a bunfig.toml preload. The registrator also replaces fetch, Request and Response, which the server tests in the same run need from Bun; and radix decides at module load whether a document exists (its Portal never mounts otherwise), so the import has to precede radix, which a beforeAll cannot do.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: @happy-dom/global-registrator + @testing-library/react registered through a bunfig.toml preload for the handful of behaviour tests (Drawer, Pill, Tabs, DataTable, GroupGrid); render-to-string stays for everything static. Two dev dependencies, no second runner.
  • (b) Push every interaction test to Playwright; the e2e job is slower and needs Docker, so the feedback loop for a focus-trap bug is minutes, not seconds.
  • (c) Add vitest + jsdom beside bun test; a second runner and config for the same files.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ4: Icons
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-16: (a).

The design needs eight icons (grid, list, boxes, activity, check, book, shield, search, external link, clock). No icon library is installed.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: an inline SVG set in components/icons.tsx copied from the mockup (stroke 1.8, currentColor), ten functions, no dependency, nothing for the CSP or the bundle to absorb.
  • (b) lucide-react, shadcn's default; tree-shaken it is small, but it is a dependency with its own release cadence for ten glyphs.
  • (c) Text labels only, no icons; the sidebar loses its scan-ability.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ5: Where screenshot snapshots are generated and stored
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-16: (a).

macOS and Linux rasterise the bundled fonts differently, so a snapshot taken locally fails in CI and vice versa.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Linux-only snapshots committed under ui/e2e/__screenshots__/, the spec skipped off-Linux with a message, regenerated through the official Playwright container by a make test-ui-e2e-update-snapshots target that runs the e2e stack on the host and Chromium in the container against host.docker.internal:3100.
  • (b) Commit per-platform snapshots (Playwright's default naming) and let each developer regenerate their own; doubles the PNGs and the macOS set drifts with every OS update.
  • (c) No screenshot tests; axe and the Playwright layout assertions only (DESIGN-0036 OQ16 b).
  • other:

docs.title: OQ6: Fleet rule sparklines before the history aggregate exists
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-16: (a).

Without aggregate=, a 20-snapshot sparkline per rule is one /compliance/history?kind&rule request per rule returning one point per org per snapshot (six orgs × 20 = 120 points, one page each at the 200 limit).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: build the Trend column hidden in 3.3 and un-hide it in 7.1 on aggregate=fleet&kind&rule; the same PR delivers both, so no user ever sees the column missing.
  • (b) Ship it in 3.3 on the per-org points aggregated client-side; N rules × one request on every Fleet load, growing with orgs.
  • (c) Drop the sparkline column; the Trend-in-points column already shows direction.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ7: The ?series= pill selection and ?range= as URL state
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-16: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: both in the URL (?series=percent|failing| not_applicable|unknown, ?range=1d|7d|30d|90d), retained across links by retainSearchParams, so a shared Fleet link reproduces the chart; default percent and 90d are omitted from the URL.
  • (b) range in the URL, series in component state; a shared link loses the selected series.
  • (c) Both in localStorage; links stop being reproducible.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ8: Phase 2 e2e breakage window
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-16: (a).

Phase 2 moves selectors the existing suite depends on, and the suite must stay green at every commit for git bisect.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: 2.6 and 2.8 land in the same commit, so the shell swap and the selector migration are atomic; the tasks stay separate for tracking.
  • (b) Mark the affected specs test.fixme in 2.6 and un-fixme them in 2.8; two commits, a red-but-skipped window.
  • other:

docs.title: OQ9: Sidebar collapse breakpoint
docs.text:
Resolved 2026-10-16: (a).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: 900px, as DESIGN-0036 states; below it the sidebar is a left Dialog opened from a top-bar button, and the Orgs grid and tables already scroll horizontally in their cards.
  • (b) No collapse; the UI is desktop-only and 900px is below any supported viewport.
  • other:

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Bring back, on the controls model, the UI that IMPL-0029 removed with the findings model, add the Remediations view, and fix what rc.11 showed was rough:

  • a Findings page over GET /results, filterable by control, rule, org and decision, with a deep-linked drawer and Re-evaluate;
  • an expandable orgs tree whose children are repositories;
  • the richer fleet panels (KPI strip with deltas, finding age, worst controls, parked by reason, compliance by control with sparklines, open PRs by age, PR throughput);
  • the Remediations view, the repository remediation panel and the status page's remediation backlog;
  • CSV export on every table;
  • a curated changelog on the status page;
  • first, in its own small pull request, the INV-0023 repository-page fixes (rule tone, name crumb, remediable wording) and the stale status screenshot.

The picture of the result is ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html, accepted with DESIGN-0037. Every task that says "as the mockup draws it" means that file's route. Where a page has to differ, the task changes the mockup in the same commit; the plan never builds past it.

Implements: DESIGN-0037's UI (OQ1 = keep both words, OQ2–OQ10 = (a)), DESIGN-0032 D32's Remediations view as DESIGN-0037 restates it, and INV-0023 F1, F2, F4 and F7.3. F5 and F6 are already done (PR #221, eda8692). The API every page reads, and INV-0023 F3, F7.1 and F7.2, are IMPL-0030's (see the split).

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• The INV-0023 fixes (Phase 1, a separate pull request): the rule tone row and RuleStatusBadge, a view-supplied breadcrumb label, the Remediable rule wording and hint, and the status screenshot in both places.
  • UI foundations: restored lib/csv.ts, range tabs on ?days=, the header org scope, the ⌘K palette, useRepositories paging, the nav entries.
  • Pages: Findings and control-detail cards, the Orgs tree, the Fleet panels, the Remediations view, the repository remediation panel, the status backlog cell, the changelog card and its lint-ui gate.
  • e2e and docs: seed growth (including remediations), specs, axe, screenshots, docs/usage/ui.md, ui/README.md, CLAUDE.md.
  • CI: the ui paths filter gains the chart's Chart.yaml and the changelog, so the version gate runs on a release-bump PR.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Every Go change. The API additions, persisting next due, and INV-0023 F7.1 (STORE_DSN_<ROLE>) and F7.2 (checks prune) are IMPL-0030's. This plan regenerates the UI client from IMPL-0030's spec and consumes it.
  • Remediation itself (IMPL-0030).
  • The compliance drivers map and per-repository metrics (DESIGN-0037 non-goals).
  • Any write path beyond the existing re-evaluate POST.
  • CSP, session or BFF proxy changes. Every new call is a GET on the existing /api/* proxy.

docs.title: The split with IMPL-0030
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-18. The first draft of this plan carried its own API, next-due and remediation-data phases. Those are Go work that shares the controls schema, openapi.yaml and the EvaluationWorkflow version gate with remediation, so they moved to IMPL-0030, and IMPL-0030's UI task moved here:

Was Now IMPL-0032 Phase 2 (API additions, 2.1–2.5, 2.7, 2.8) IMPL-0030 Phase 7 (API for the controls UI) IMPL-0032 2.6 (client paging) stays: Phase 2 task 2.5 here IMPL-0032 Phase 3 (persist next due, INV-0023 F3) IMPL-0030 Phase 2, under the same version gate as StartDueRemediations IMPL-0032 Phase 9 data (9.1–9.3) IMPL-0030 Phase 7 IMPL-0032 Phase 9 UI (9.3 UI, 9.4, 9.5) Phases 3, 4 and 8 here INV-0023 F7.1, F7.2 (old OQ11) IMPL-0030 Phases 1 and 6 IMPL-0030 7.5 (UI: Remediations view, repository panel, status backlog) Phase 6 here Old OQ1–OQ4, OQ12 (history shape, bucket vs status, total, next due, index) IMPL-0030's open questions

So the order is: Phase 1 here ships now, IMPL-0030 ships next with every API this plan reads, and Phases 2 to 9 here build the UI on it.

An audit against the code (2026-10-18) checked DESIGN-0037's assumptions. The rows that shape this plan (the API rows went with the API to IMPL-0030):

Finding Effect on the plan The UI image builds with context ui/, so a root CHANGELOG.yaml is not in it; the build is Vite 8, which has no YAML loader OQ1, OQ2; Phase 7 The CI ui filter is ui/** + api/openapi.yaml, so a chart-only bump PR never runs lint-ui 7.4 GroupGrid shares one denominator (tracked) for percent and shading, nests children in an inner table and is unused OQ4; Phase 4 RangeTabs, OrgScope, CommandPalette, csv.ts, range.ts were deleted in 7ad928f; RangeTabs bound ?range= strings, and csv.ts carried findings-era helpers 2.1–2.4 restore and rework them BucketBadge/DecisionBadge keep their own tone maps outside toneFor 1.1 folds them in The e2e seed installs the remediate App on acme, so only the installed state is tested end to end OQ6; 8.7 adds the absent state docs/usage/img/ui/status.png is a hand copy of the e2e snapshot 1.5 copies it after re-rendering Status.apps names the Apps eval and remediate every gated panel decides from remediate

docs.title: How the phases are ordered
docs.text:
Phase 1 is the INV-0023 fixes: UI-only, no new API, visible on rc.11 today, so it ships now as its own small pull request. Phases 2 to 9 start once IMPL-0030 has merged, because every page reads an API it adds. Phase 2 rebuilds the shared pieces the pages compose from. Phases 3 to 5 are DESIGN-0037's pages in its order (Findings first, it needs the most), Phase 6 is the Remediations view and the other remediation panels, Phase 7 the changelog (it touches the build, lint-ui and CI), Phase 8 the seed, axe, screenshots and docs, and Phase 9 is human-run.

Each code phase ends with make lint-ui, make test-ui and make test-ui-e2e green, with a commit per numbered task. Phase 1 lands as one PR into v2; Phases 2 to 9 land as a second PR (the one-PR-per-IMPL rule, with the fixes split out by decision). Both carry the dont-release label (Rule 6).

docs.title: OQ2: How the changelog reaches the Vite bundle
docs.text:

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Make the API and UI run against Okta, Entra ID or Auth0 as readily as against Keycloak, by making the three provider assumptions in the code and chart configurable and by documenting the identity-provider contract with a recipe per provider. Ships as v2.0.0-rc.17, before the GA cutover (DESIGN-0038 OQ1).

Implements: DESIGN-0038 Part B (B1–B6), decisions D4–D7, OQ4–OQ9.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• OIDC_CLIENT_CLAIM on the api role (default azp), read where Claims.Client is set; the typed AZP field goes.
  • OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH_METHOD (client_secret_post default, client_secret_basic) and OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_PARAMS (JSON object, reserved keys refused) on the BFF.
  • Chart: api.auth.clientClaim, ui.oidc.tokenAuthMethod, ui.oidc.authorizationParams; nameClaim/groupsClaim in the schema; ui.oidc.scopes default aligned with the BFF's.
  • Test fixtures: Okta-, Entra- and namespaced-claim-shaped tokens in oidctest; the mock issuer accepting client_secret_basic; one e2e project on the basic method.
  • docs/operations/identity-provider.md: the contract table, the Keycloak section moved from docs/usage/api.md, Okta, Entra ID and Auth0 recipes, the Google note, verification through /me.
  • The rc.17 release bump, tag and publish.

  • Any change to the authorization model, /me, or the OpenAPI document.
  • ID-token acceptance at the API, opaque-token introspection, Google without a broker.
  • Homelab Keycloak reconfiguration: the defaults keep today's behaviour, so the rc.17 upgrade needs no IdP change.

  • internal/api/authn.go: AuthnConfig{Issuer, Audience, NameClaim, GroupsClaim, Now}; tokenClaims.AZP is the only source of Claims.Client; verify already reads name and groups by configured key from the full claim map, so the client claim follows the same path. isIDToken names Keycloak in its comment.
  • internal/config/api.go reads OIDC_NAME_CLAIM and OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM with defaults; cmd/repo-guardian/api.go builds AuthnConfig from them.
  • internal/api/oidctest/oidctest.go Token has Client (→ azp), Groups, Name (→ preferred_username), IDToken, Rogue, HMAC; the header typ is at+jwt. NameClaim: "preferred_username", GroupsClaim: "groups" is hard-coded in api_test.go, status_http_test.go and apiendpoints_integration_test.go.
  • ui/server/oidc.ts passes client.ClientSecretPost; ui/server/auth.ts builds the authorize URL from six fixed parameters; ui/server/config.ts has defaultScopes = "openid profile email offline_access" and no audience or method setting.
  • ui/server/testing/mock-issuer.ts checks the client secret from the POST body only; ui/e2e/stack.ts starts two BFFs (startUI).
  • Chart: values.yaml api.auth.{issuer,audience,nameClaim,groupsClaim} and ui.oidc.{clientId,scopes: [openid, profile, groups, offline_access]}; values.schema.json declares only enabled, issuer, audience under api.auth; _helpers.tpl renders the OIDC_* env; validateUI holds the UI render guards; tests/ui_test.yaml asserts the scopes default string.
  • Docs: docs/usage/api.md § Keycloak example; docs/usage/ui.md links it; ui/README.md has the env table.

docs.title: How the phases are ordered
docs.text: API first (Phase 1) because its fixtures are what Phases 2–4 are tested against; the BFF (Phase 2) next because the chart (Phase 3) renders its new env; docs (Phase 4) once every knob has its final name; the rc (Phase 5) last. Phases 1–4 are one pull request against v2 ([[feedback-one-pr-per-impl]] in memory); Phase 5 is the release-bump pull request.

docs.text: Each phase builds on the previous one. A phase is complete when all its tasks are checked off and its success criteria are met.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
OQ1. How oidctest grows provider shapes.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a Token.Claims map[string]any merged last plus three named constructors (Okta, Entra, Namespaced); one mechanism covers the next provider without a new field, and the constructors keep the tests readable.
  • (b) one boolean per shape (Okta bool, Entra bool); mirrors IDToken/Rogue, but every new claim variation is a new field.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ2. How the mock issuer exercises client_secret_basic.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: accept both methods always and record which one was used; the e2e no-remediation BFF runs on basic, the chromium one on post, and a unit test asserts the recorded method. No flag to thread through the stack.
  • (b) a tokenAuth: "post" | "basic" option on the issuer that refuses the other; stricter, but the stack then needs two issuers or a third BFF to cover both.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ3. Where reserved authorization parameters are refused.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: in all three places: BFF config validation (the runtime truth), validateUI (the message operators see at render) and the schema (not/required per key, so helm lint catches it too).
  • (b) BFF and validateUI only; the schema stays simpler and the render still fails.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ4. The OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_PARAMS wire format.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a JSON object, rendered by the chart with toJson; unambiguous for values containing = or , (Entra's domain_hint values, Auth0 audiences with /).
  • (b) key=value,key=value; shorter to type by hand, ambiguous for the values above.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ5. What else rides in rc.17.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: only this IMPL; the rc exists to put the identity knobs in operators' hands before the GA docs name them.
  • (b) also the internal/controls/file/file.go quadratic duplicate-key FIX:; a real cost but unrelated, and IMPL-0034 Phase 9 carries it.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Take v2 to main and ship v2.0.0 through the existing release pipeline: converge the branches with merge commits, make the tree GA-shaped before the final merge (docs, changelogs, branch-entry reverts, chart 2.0.0), land the first tier of supply-chain security (SBOMs, CodeQL, rulesets, pins, pod hardening, a verification page), run the soak IMPL-0030 set, then merge with the major label so one push produces the binaries, both registries, the UI image, the chart and provenance.

Implements: DESIGN-0038 Part A (A1–A9), Part D tier 1 (D4), decisions D1–D3, D10–D12, OQ1–OQ3, OQ10–OQ12, OQ16–OQ19. Supersedes IMPL-0030 OQ12 and carries IMPL-0030 Phase 10.
