docs.title: Pre-implementation audit
docs.text:
Verified 2026-10-24/25 (DESIGN-0038 § Background):

  • main = 1a825c0 (v1.14.1) has five commits v2 lacks: #203 (tools/rgctl), #227, #225 (docs/operations/rgctl.md), #228 (release.yml base-branch: true), #229. v2 = 517f0cd (rc.16) after #239. Merge-base 5bd96bb. The main ruleset (12545694) has rules deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request and no bypass actors; no required checks; no tag ruleset. No v2.0.0 tag or release exists.
  • release.yml: bump-version (jefflinse/pr-semver-bump@v1.7.4, labels major|minor|patch, noop dont-release) → release (goreleaser, GPG) → publish-ghcr/publish-ecr (reusable, tag from the bump; ECR gated on vars.ECR_PUBLISH_ENABLED). The action parses all tags as semver (loose), sorts, and with base-branch takes the newest reachable from the base branch; node-semver inc("2.0.0-rc.16", major|minor|patch) = 2.0.0.
  • prerelease.yml matches v*-*; changelog-update.yml runs git-cliff --output CHANGELOG.md (full regeneration) on v* pushes without a dash; cliff.toml has a header and render_always.
  • gh-pages.yml deploys mkdocs-ghpages.yml (nav up to DESIGN-0009, no Operations, no v2 pages; theme: material is its only non-nav difference from mkdocs.yml, which has exclude_docs and plugins: techdocs-core) with an unpinned pip install mkdocs-material; neither config enables pymdownx.superfences, so the 39 mermaid blocks render as code.
  • Landing docs still describe v1: README.md, docs/index.md, docs/usage/getting-started.md, docs/ADDING_RULES.md, docs/operations/{aws,scaling,ent-setup}.md, chart README intro. v2-migration.md contradicts itself at the RECONCILE_FRESHNESS and migrate.freshness rows.
  • Security: no sboms: in .goreleaser.yml; no attest in docker-bake.hcl; CodeQL default setup not-configured; 6 of 111 external action refs SHA-pinned; govulncheck/go-licenses installed @latest, mkdocs-material unpinned, mise.toml latest for trivy, syft, cosign, goreleaser, git-cliff, govulncheck, go-licenses; .github/dependabot.yml docker entry at directory: cicd (does not exist) and actions managed by both Dependabot and Renovate; renovate.json5 lacks the slsa-github-generator pin exception; values.yaml podSecurityContext: {} and a container context without allowPrivilegeEscalation/capabilities/seccomp while templates/ui.yaml has all of them plus automountServiceAccountToken: false; no role imports a Kubernetes client (k8s.io/client-go absent from go.mod); SECURITY.md § Reporting Vulnerabilities is three lines; the chart README is the only verification doc; no concurrency: anywhere; release.yml grants contents/packages/id-token: write workflow-wide.
  • ci.yml gates jobs on dorny/paths-filter outputs (go, docker, helm, workflows, alerts, monitoring, sql, temporal, api, ui); skipped jobs satisfy required checks (CLAUDE.md § CI paths-filter convention). pr-labels.yml requires exactly one semver label.

docs.title: How the phases are ordered
docs.text: Phase 1 first because every later edit must land on a tree that is a superset of main. Phases 2–5 are independent of one another and of the soak; they are separate pull requests against v2, each reviewable alone and none changing runtime behaviour. Phase 6 is the last pull request before M2 and makes the tree GA-shaped. Phase 7 runs in the homelab in parallel with 2–6 and is the clock. Phase 8 is M2 and the release; Phase 9 the clean-up. IMPL-0033 (rc.17) merges before Phase 6 so the GA docs name knobs that exist.

docs.title: Implementation Phases
docs.text: Each phase builds on the previous one. A phase is complete when all its tasks are checked off and its success criteria are met.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [x] 1.1 Branch. chore/sync-main-into-v2 from v2; git merge --no-ff origin/main. Expected conflicts: .github/workflows/release.yml (keep base-branch: true and v2's surrounding text), go.mod/ go.sum (keep v2's versions; both lines have 1.26.10). Anything else conflicting is noted on this task. Done on feat/impl-0034-ga-cutover (one PR for the IMPL), not a separate branch. Also conflicted: ci.yml (rgctl coverage step kept in test-go, before v2's replay/integration jobs), .gitignore (both), .golangci.yml (rgctl-boundary joined v2's depguard rules), Makefile (lint: lint-controls-docs lint-rgctl), mkdocs.yml and the two docz READMEs (v2's side, then 1.3).
  • [x] 1.2 Verify the superset. git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD exits 0; git ls-files tools/rgctl | wc -l > 0; docs/operations/rgctl.md exists; grep -c 'base-branch: true' .github/workflows/release.yml = 1; .codecov.yml carries the rgctl flag; go build ./... && go vet ./tools/... (rgctl's module layout per IMPL-0027) pass.
  • [x] 1.3 Nav. mkdocs.yml gains docs/operations/rgctl.md under Operations and DESIGN-0035 / IMPL-0027 under their sections (docz did not see them on v2); docz update design and docz update impl regenerate the READMEs; revert unrelated TOC churn.
  • [ ] 1.4 (deferred - human required: the maintainer opens and merges the PR) PR. dont-release, merge commit (pick "Create a merge commit" by hand; the default squash would flatten main's history into v2). CI green, including lint (rgctl is in the module set). This IMPL's single PR carries the sync, so that PR is the one to merge with "Create a merge commit".

docs.text:

• [x] 4.1 Prepend. changelog-update.yml: git-cliff --latest --strip all --prepend CHANGELOG.md (header and footer already live in the file; --latest renders the newest tag's section only). Verify locally against a scratch copy: run it for v2.0.0-rc.16 and confirm the rc.11 section and the 1.x sections below are unchanged byte for byte. Default the ref input to main only; reword the comment about rc tags. Done with --latest --prepend and no --strip: tested on a scratch copy (git-cliff 2.14.2, rc.18 as the newest tag), --strip all writes the section above # Changelog, because git-cliff only swaps the file's header out when it renders one. Without it the header stays on top, exactly one section is added and every older section is byte-identical. cliff.toml's header gained a trailing blank line so the new section is separated from it.
  • [x] 4.2 Triggers. ci.yml, license-check.yml, security.yml: branches: [main] (keep security.yml's pull_request trigger); ct.yaml target-branch: main. These land on v2 and are correct the moment M2 merges; until then v2 pushes run no CI, so this is the last pull request before Phase 6 and is merged together with it (OQ3). Single-PR note: this IMPL ships as one PR against v2, and a pull_request: branches: [main] trigger stops CI on that PR, so 4.2 is the branch's last commit, pushed after CI is green on everything else. Done as the branch's last commit; the remaining v2 strings in the workflows are the rc version in release.yml's comment and action/tool versions.

• [x] 5.1 SBOMs for binaries. .goreleaser.yml sboms: [{artifacts: archive}] (syft, SPDX JSON, *.sbom.json beside each archive; checksums.txt covers them). make release-snapshot (goreleaser --snapshot) locally shows the SBOM files; syft pinned in mise.toml (5.6). make release-local (goreleaser --snapshot) wrote four *.tar.gz.sbom.json files, all four in checksums.txt. release.yml and prerelease.yml install syft (anchore/sbom-action/download-syft) before goreleaser, which needs it on the runner.

In ghcr.yml and ecr.yml, after each cosign sign: syft <image@digest> -o spdx-json > sbom.json and cosign attest --yes --type spdxjson --predicate sbom.json <image@digest>, for the image, the UI image and the chart (the chart's SBOM is syft over the .tgz), then cosign verify-attestation --type spdxjson --certificate-identity-regexp ... <ref@digest> as the in-workflow verify (the SBOM-presence check from the design's testing strategy). Digests from steps.digest.outputs.digest, never a shell blob. dev/ui-dev (local type=docker loads) override attest with both types disabled=true, since an empty list does not override an inherited one and the docker exporter cannot carry attestations. syft over the chart .tgz gives an SPDX-2.3 document. The verify regexp is the workflow file (ghcr\.yml@/ecr\.yml@), matching both the release.yml call (@refs/heads/main) and an rc dispatch (@refs/tags/...).

Renovate's dashboard (#213) shows no duplicate of a Dependabot PR after one cycle (verified in Phase 9). *The UI entry ispackage-ecosystem: "bun", notnpm: the lockfile isbun.lock, and Dependabot's npm ecosystem needs apackage-lock.json.* - [x] 5.8 **Pod hardening.**values.yaml:podSecurityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 65534, runAsGroup: 65534, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}},securityContext: {readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}(moverunAsNonRoot/runAsUserup to the pod level, matchingui.yaml);automountServiceAccountToken: falseon every role's Deployment and on the hook Jobs (no role or Job calls the Kubernetes API:k8s.io/client-gois not ingo.mod, the Jobs runmigrateandpsql).templates/deployment.yaml,migrate-job.yamland the two controls-roles/read-only Jobs render them; helm-unittest asserts each field per role intests/security_context_test.yaml;ci-values.yaml(busybox) still renders. *The two psql Jobs keep the baked Postgres pod context (uid 999) and get a container context with no privilege escalation,drop: [ALL]and RuntimeDefault seccomp, but not a read-only root (the image's shell may spool the heredoc to/tmp).make helm-unittest257/257; default values render every Deployment and the migrate Job withautomountServiceAccountToken: false, RuntimeDefault and no privilege escalation.* - [x] 5.9 **Verifying releases.**docs/operations/verifying-releases.md: forrepo-guardian,repo-guardian-uiand the chart, thecosign verifyandcosign verify-attestation --type slsaprovenanceand--type spdxjsoncommands with the certificate identityhttps://github.com/donaldgifford/repo-guardian/.github/workflows/ghcr.yml@refs/tags/and the OIDC issuer; for binaries,checksums.txt+ its GPG signature today (the key published in the page and as a release asset, OQ20 says cosign replaces it in IMPL-0036) andslsa-verifier verify-imagefor the images; retrieving an SBOM withcosign download attestation. docs.text:
• A workflow_dispatch of ghcr.yml with dry_run=false for the current rc tag (re-publish is idempotent) attaches an SPDX attestation to all three artefacts and the verify step passes; cosign download attestation returns it.
  • gh api repos/.../code-scanning/default-setup reports configured with the three languages; the first CodeQL analysis is visible.

  • The push-triggered release.yml run after 5.11 shows jobs.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
OQ1. Mermaid on the interim MkDocs site.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: enable pymdownx.superfences with the mermaid fence in mkdocs-ghpages.yml; it is four lines, Material renders mermaid natively with it, and the GA site stops showing 39 diagrams as code while IMPL-0035 is built.
  • (b) leave it to Starlight; the GA site keeps today's rendering for a few more weeks.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (b).

OQ2. Where the strict docs build runs.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a new docs CI job on a docs paths filter, installing the pinned mkdocs-material with pip; it later becomes IMPL-0035's Starlight build job under the same name and filter.
  • (b) inside the existing lint job; fewer jobs, but lint would then run on docs-only pull requests and needs Python.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ3. The required status checks.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: one aggregate ci-ok job (needs every ci.yml job, if: always(), red on any failure or cancellation) plus Check Required Labels, govulncheck and Check Dependency Licenses from their own workflows; adding a CI job never needs a ruleset edit, and skipped (paths-filtered) jobs pass.
  • (b) list every job name in the ruleset; explicit, but every new or renamed job silently stops being required until someone edits the ruleset.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ4. Who runs the GitHub-settings changes (CodeQL, rulesets, Pages).

  • (a) ✅ recommended: the maintainer runs the gh api commands written in the task, after reviewing the JSON in the task note; they are outward-facing, hard to review after the fact, and need admin rights.
  • (b) the implementer runs them with the maintainer's explicit go-ahead per command; faster, same commands.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ5. The v* tag ruleset's rules.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: deletion and non_fast_forward only; existing release tags cannot be moved or deleted, and release.yml's GITHUB_TOKEN can still create the next one. The ruleset has no bypass actors, like main's.
  • (b) also restrict creation with a bypass actor for the GitHub Actions integration; stops a maintainer's accidental hand tag, but the bypass must name the right integration id and breaks the pipeline if it drifts.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ6. The GA preflight.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: scripts/ga-preflight.sh, run by the maintainer on the M2 head and pasted into the PR; one file, no CI wiring, and the checks are release-time facts (tags, labels) CI cannot see on a pull request.
  • (b) a make ga-preflight target wrapping the same script; one more Makefile entry for a once-per-major action.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ7. Where the 2.0.0 release notes live.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: docs/releases/2.0.0.md, linked from goreleaser's release header and from the README; the notes outlive the GitHub release page and render on the docs site.
  • (b) only the GitHub release body (goreleaser header); nothing to keep in the tree, not on the docs site.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Replace the MkDocs public site on GitHub Pages with an Astro Starlight site built from the same docs/ tree, deployed through GitHub's Pages Actions flow, with link validation, mermaid rendered in the browser, search, and a sidebar that follows the directory layout. The shape follows donaldgifford/claudelint's working Starlight setup (DESIGN-0003 there): site/ beside docs/, a symlinked content collection, an in-repo remark link rewriter, autogenerated sidebar groups per docz directory. TechDocs keeps reading mkdocs.yml; nothing in docs/ is rewritten for one renderer at the other's expense.

Implements: DESIGN-0038 Part C (C1–C5), D5–D8, OQ13–OQ15. Replaces IMPL-0034 Phase 2's interim site.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• site/: Astro + Starlight, bun-managed, pinned, with the docs/ content collection, a remark link rewrite, starlight-links-validator, client-side mermaid, Pagefind search.
  • Frontmatter title on the 35 pages that lack it, including the generated controls-reference.md through WriteReference.
  • The sidebar (autogenerated by directory, a hand-listed "Historical (1.x)" group), the landing page, the DESIGN-0036 tokens.
  • Replacing the docs CI job's MkDocs build with the Starlight build, astro check and a static check over dist/; gh-pages.yml → Pages Actions deploy. No browser in the docs build (OQ1 (b)).
  • Deleting mkdocs-ghpages.yml, the gh-pages branch and the pip install; CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING and README updates.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Removing mkdocs.yml or techdocs-core (TechDocs).
  • Rewriting document bodies beyond frontmatter, one admonition and the TOC blocks (OQ2).
  • Versioned docs (one site, the current line; 1.x pages are the Historical group).
  • Building the UI's ui/ and site/ as one workspace.

docs.title: Pre-implementation audit
docs.text:
Verified 2026-10-25:

  • 126 markdown files under docs/; 80 carry a docz <!--toc:start--> block; 473 relative .md links (DESIGN-0038 C2). 35 files have no frontmatter title: every docz section README.md, docs/index.md, docs/ADDING_RULES.md, all docs/operations/*.md and docs/usage/*.md. docs/usage/controls-reference.md is generated by repo-guardian controls docs (internal/controls/builtin/reference.go WriteReference, header # Control-type reference) and gated by make lint-controls-docs, so its frontmatter must come from the generator.
  • Three MkDocs !!! note "v1 only" admonitions, all in docs/operations/migrations.md (lines 67, 327, 414); the remaining pages use plain blockquotes.
  • 39 mermaid fences in 15 docs (DESIGN-0038 § Background).
  • Mermaid diagrams, docz TOC blocks and relative links all render on TechDocs today; TechDocs must keep working unchanged (D5).
  • mise.toml pins bun = "1.3.14" with a renovate comment; ui/ uses bun with bun.lock; Renovate's npm manager is enabled by the shared presets, so site/package.json is picked up with no config change.
  • .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml runs mkdocs gh-deploy --config-file mkdocs-ghpages.yml --force to the gh-pages branch; Pages is set to deploy from that branch (legacy source). actions/configure-pages, upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages need the pages: write and id-token: write permissions and the Pages source set to "GitHub Actions".
  • The docs paths filter and job exist from IMPL-0034 Phase 2 (MkDocs strict build); make lint-docs wraps it.
  • claudelint's setup (read 2026-10-25, site/ on main), the reference for this IMPL: site/src/content/docs is a 120000 symlink to ../../../docs because Starlight's docsLoader() hard-codes src/content/docs/ and its autogenerate filter strips that prefix (a bare glob({base: '../docs'}) serves pages but every autogenerated group renders empty); docsSchema is extended with docz's id/status/author/created as optional fields; site/src/plugins/remark-md-link-rewriter.mjs (unist-util-visit, ~60 lines) rewrites relative .md links to lowercase absolute routes and leaves out-of-tree links alone; docz READMEs carry frontmatter (title, sidebar: {order: 0, label: Overview}) that docz update preserves, and render at /<type>/readme/; docs.yml runs npm run check (astro check) + astro build and uploads dist/ if: always(); lint-md greps docs/ for !!!/??? admonitions and pymdownx so the shared source stays CommonMark+GFM; GFM alerts (> [!NOTE]) replaced admonitions. Two differences to keep: it uses npm with a pinned Node and caret ranges (we use bun and exact pins), and it deploys to Cloudflare Pages with PR previews (we stay on GitHub Pages, OQ5). Mermaid is wired in neither of its pipelines.
  • MkDocs site_dir collision. MkDocs's default output directory is site/, and .gitignore line 46 ignores site/; IMPL-0034 2.5 moves the build to build/mkdocs and narrows the ignore before this IMPL creates site/ (verify in 1.1).

docs.title: How the phases are ordered
docs.text: Phase 1 produces a building site from the unmodified tree so every later change is measured against a green build. Phase 2 makes the content render correctly (titles, links, diagrams, admonition, TOC blocks) and adds the validators that keep it so. Phase 3 shapes the sidebar, Phase 4 the look. Phase 5 wires CI before anything deploys, so Phase 6 switches the Pages source once with the build already proven on pull requests.

docs.title: Implementation Phases
docs.text: Each phase builds on the previous one. A phase is complete when all its tasks are checked off and its success criteria are met.

docs.title: Phase 1: Scaffold
docs.text: DESIGN-0038 C1, D5, OQ13/OQ14 (decided (a)).

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 1.1 site/ package. Confirm .gitignore no longer ignores site/ and mkdocs.yml has site_dir: build/mkdocs (IMPL-0034 2.5); then bun create astro@latest --template starlight into site/ (minimal; delete the sample content). Pin exact versions of astro, @astrojs/starlight, sharp, @astrojs/check, typescript, unist-util-visit in package.json (no ^), bun.lock committed, site/.gitignore for dist/, .astro/, node_modules/. Scripts dev, build, preview, check as in claudelint. The root .dockerignore gains site/; go.mod ignore gains ./site/node_modules.
  • [ ] 1.2 Config. site/astro.config.mjs: site: "https://donaldgifford.github.io", base: "/repo-guardian" (OQ5), trailingSlash: "always", Starlight title: "repo-guardian", favicon, social: {github: ...}, editLink.baseUrl pointing at blob/main/docs/, lastUpdated: true, customCss placeholder.
  • [ ] 1.3 Content from docs/. site/src/content.config.ts as in claudelint: docsLoader() with docsSchema({extend: z.object({id, status, author, created})}) (all optional; created a string or date), content via the relative symlink site/src/content/docs → ../../../docs (OQ3 covers the slug mapping). Confirm astro build follows the symlink, git ls-files -s shows it as 120000, and the symlink survives actions/checkout on Linux (claudelint's CI proves it).
  • [ ] 1.4 Exclusions. Exclude docs/**/README.md from the collection (they are docz indices; Phase 3 maps them to directory landing pages) with the loader's pattern/exclude so no readme/ route appears.
  • [ ] 1.5 Makefile. docs-install (cd site && bun install --frozen-lockfile), docs-build (bun run build), docs-dev (bun run dev), docs-check (bun run check, i.e. astro check), docs-mkdocs-check (the TechDocs mkdocs build --strict -d build/mkdocs, kept from IMPL-0034's lint-docs), and lint-docs = docs-check + docs-build + the Phase 2 validators + the MkDocs-only-syntax grep from claudelint's lint-md (^\s*!!!, ^\s*\?\?\?, pymdownx); make help lists them.
  • [ ] 1.6 First build. make docs-build succeeds with the unmodified tree (warnings allowed, collected on this task: missing titles, unresolved links). Record page count.

docs.title: Phase 2: Markdown compatibility
docs.text: DESIGN-0038 C2, D6, D7; IMPL-0035 OQ1, OQ2, OQ6.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 2.1 Titles. Add ---\ntitle: ...\n--- to the 34 hand-written pages lacking it (the title is the H1 text); keep the H1 in the body so TechDocs and GitHub rendering are unchanged. Starlight renders the title itself, so set markdown.remarkPlugins to strip the first H1 when it equals the frontmatter title (part of the in-repo plugin in 2.3) rather than deleting the H1s.
  • [ ] 2.2 Generated reference. WriteReference emits the frontmatter block (title: Control-type reference) before # Control-type reference; regenerate with repo-guardian controls docs; TestWriteReference_* goldens updated; make lint-controls-docs green.
  • [ ] 2.3 Link rewrite plugin. Copy claudelint's site/src/plugins/remark-md-link-rewriter.mjs (the user's own code) and extend it (OQ6): keep its resolve-against-source + lowercase + absolute-route behaviour; add the README.md → directory route and index.md → / rules (OQ3), prefix base (claudelint has none), and turn links to files outside docs/ (../CLAUDE.md, ../../charts/...), which claudelint leaves alone, into GitHub blob/main URLs. Unit tests with bun test for the six cases.
  • [ ] 2.4 Links validator. starlight-links-validator (pinned) in the Starlight plugins; errorOnRelativeLinks: false is not set (the rewrite must have removed them), errorOnInvalidHashes: true. The build fails on a dead link; fix the ones it finds (expected: a few in historical pages) and list them on the task.
  • [ ] 2.5 Mermaid, client-side (OQ1 (b)). A small remark plugin step (in the same in-repo plugin file) turns a ```mermaid fence into <pre class="mermaid">…</pre>, and a Starlight Head component override loads a pinned mermaid ESM build from site/node_modules (bundled by Astro, not a CDN) that runs mermaid.run() on page load and re-themes on the theme toggle (startOnLoad: false, theme: dark|default from data-theme). No browser in the build. All 39 diagrams render in a local preview; a diagram with a syntax error shows mermaid's inline error box, so 2.4's validator cannot catch it: add make lint-mermaid running mmdc-free validation with mermaid.parse in a bun script over every fence (mermaid's parser runs in bun with a DOM shim via happy-dom, already a UI dev dependency), and wire it into lint-docs. Verify once by breaking one diagram.
  • [ ] 2.6 Admonitions. The three !!! note "v1 only" blocks in migrations.md become blockquotes (> **1.x only.** ...), matching IMPL-0034 3.7's convention; TechDocs renders a blockquote fine.
  • [ ] 2.7 TOC blocks. Per OQ2, the remark plugin removes the <!--toc:start-->…<!--toc:end--> region on the Starlight side only (Starlight has its own right-hand TOC); the blocks stay in the files for TechDocs and GitHub.
  • [ ] 2.8 Markdownlint comments. <!-- markdownlint-* --> HTML comments pass through as comments in Starlight; confirm none render as text (MDX is not enabled; the collection is .md only).

  • Every page has a title in the sidebar and no page shows two H1s.
  • rg -c 'title:' --glob 'docs/**/*.md' -l | wc -l equals the page count from 1.6 plus the READMEs.

docs.title: Phase 3: Sidebar and landing
docs.text: DESIGN-0038 C3; IMPL-0035 OQ3, OQ4.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 3.1 Groups. Starlight sidebar: Getting started (usage/ autogenerate, ordered by sidebar.order frontmatter on the six pages), Operations (operations/ autogenerate minus the Historical pages), Reference (API spec page, control-type reference, policy reference), Design documents (design/, rfc/, adr/, impl/, investigation/ each autogenerated and collapsed), Historical (1.x) (hand-listed, OQ4). docz's numbered filenames sort naturally; no sidebar.order needed there.
  • [ ] 3.2 README → index. Each docz README.md (status tables) is rendered as the group's landing page: the loader maps <dir>/README.md to slug <dir> (OQ3) and the link plugin's README.md rule points at it. The autogenerated group shows it first via sidebar.order: 0.
  • [ ] 3.3 Landing page. docs/index.md becomes the Starlight splash template with the DESIGN-0038 A4 opening, three cards (install, operate, understand) and the verification pointer; the frontmatter template: splash and hero keys are ignored by TechDocs (confirm the TechDocs render still shows the body).
  • [ ] 3.4 404 and redirects. redirects for the MkDocs URLs that differ (MkDocs renders foo.md at /foo/, Starlight too, so the set should be small: ADDING_RULES casing and the docz README routes); Starlight's default 404 page.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• Every page is reachable from the sidebar exactly once; the Historical group holds the nine 1.x pages and nothing current.
  • The old MkDocs URLs for the Usage and Operations pages resolve (same path or a redirect), checked by a script over mkdocs.yml's nav.
  • The landing page renders on both Starlight and TechDocs.

docs.text: DESIGN-0038 C4; IMPL-0035 OQ7.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 4.1 Tokens. site/src/styles/theme.css sets Starlight's --sl-color-accent* and --sl-color-gray-* from the DESIGN-0036 palette (ui/design/repo-guardian-mockup.html :root block), both light and dark, with IBM Plex Sans / JetBrains Mono via @fontsource (OQ7); no component overrides.
  • [ ] 4.2 Logo and favicon. site/public/favicon.svg and the header logo from the UI's assets (ui/web/public/), MIT/Apache sources only.
  • [ ] 4.3 Static HTML. api/openapi.yaml served from site/public/api/openapi.yaml via a prebuild copy script, with a Reference page embedding Scalar's API reference component (MIT) pointed at it, so the spec is browsable.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• The site shares the UI's palette and fonts; the manual axe run reports no violations on the three sampled pages.
  • openapi.yaml renders as an API reference and downloads as the raw file.

docs.title: Phase 5: CI
docs.text: DESIGN-0038 C5 (build half).

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 5.1 docs job. ci.yml's docs job (IMPL-0034 Phase 2) replaces the MkDocs steps with jdx/mise-action (bun), a bun cache keyed on site/bun.lock, make docs-install, make lint-docs (astro check + build + validators + mermaid parse + the TechDocs strict build); the docs paths filter gains site/**, api/openapi.yaml, mise.toml. Upload dist/ as an artifact if: always() (claudelint's stand-in for PR previews, which GitHub Pages lacks). ci-ok picks it up through needs.
  • [ ] 5.2 Static check over dist/. site/scripts/check-dist.ts (bun test, no browser): the landing page exists, every sidebar group label appears in its HTML, one design page carries a <pre class="mermaid"> and the mermaid script tag, the Pagefind index directory exists, every old MkDocs URL from mkdocs.yml's nav resolves to a file or a redirect (Phase 3's check, made permanent). Runs in lint-docs after the build.
  • [ ] 5.3 Renovate. Confirm the dashboard lists site/package.json dependencies after the first run; add a groupName: "docs site" packageRule so astro/starlight/validators bump together.
  • [ ] 5.4 Local parity. make lint-docs runs exactly what CI runs.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• A docs-only pull request runs docs and nothing Go; a broken link in the PR turns ci-ok red.
  • The docs job installs no browser and finishes in under three minutes on a warm cache.

docs.title: Phase 6: Deploy and retire MkDocs on Pages
docs.text: DESIGN-0038 C5 (deploy half), D8.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 6.1 Pages source. deferred - human required: the maintainer sets Pages to "GitHub Actions" (Settings → Pages → Source), or gh api -X PUT repos/donaldgifford/repo-guardian/pages -f build_type=workflow.
  • [ ] 6.2 gh-pages.yml. Replace the mkdocs steps with actions/configure-pages, mise bun, make docs-install docs-build, actions/upload-pages-artifact (path: site/dist), actions/deploy-pages in a deploy job with environment: github-pages, permissions: {pages: write, id-token: write, contents: read}, concurrency: {group: pages, cancel-in-progress: true}; trigger on push to main filtered to docs/**, site/**, api/openapi.yaml, the workflow itself, plus workflow_dispatch.
  • [ ] 6.3 First deploy. Dispatch; confirm https://donaldgifford.github.io/repo-guardian/ serves the Starlight build, a design page shows its diagram, search works, and the README badge/link still resolves.
  • [ ] 6.4 Retire. Delete mkdocs-ghpages.yml and the pip install from every workflow; the docs CI job no longer installs Python. deferred - human required: delete the gh-pages branch after the Actions deploy has served for a week (git push origin --delete gh-pages).
  • [ ] 6.5 Docs about docs. CLAUDE.md: the gh-pages/mkdocs-ghpages sentences in § Release and § Documentation → "the public site is Astro Starlight in site/; mkdocs.yml is TechDocs only"; the docz update gotcha stays. CONTRIBUTING: "preview the docs with make docs-dev". README: the docs link.
  • [ ] 6.6 Close out. IMPL-0035 → Completed; DESIGN-0038 Part C references updated.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
OQ1. Mermaid rendering strategy.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: build-time SVG via rehype-mermaid (img-svg, chromium in the build); no client JavaScript, diagrams in search and print, and a bad diagram fails the build instead of showing an error box to readers. Costs a browser install in the docs job (~20s cached).
  • (b) client-side mermaid.js through a small Starlight component; lighter build, no validation, flashes on load, not indexed.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (b).

OQ2. The docz TOC blocks.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: strip them on the Starlight side in the remark plugin; the files keep their blocks for TechDocs and GitHub, and Starlight's own right-hand TOC replaces them.
  • (b) delete the blocks from the files and turn off docz TOC generation; one fewer transform, but TechDocs loses its in-page TOC and 80 files churn.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ3. docz README.md → directory landing.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: map the slug in the loader (README.md → <dir>), so docz keeps regenerating the READMEs untouched and the link plugin has one rule.
  • (b) slug: frontmatter in each README; docz would need to preserve it through docz update, which rewrites the tables but not the frontmatter today (verify before choosing).
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a). claudelint uses the frontmatter form (READMEs at /<type>/readme/ with sidebar: {order: 0, label: Overview}, preserved by docz update); if docsLoader() exposes no slug hook, fall back to that proven shape in 3.2 without re-opening the question.

OQ4. The Historical (1.x) group.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: hand-list the nine pages in the sidebar config and exclude them from the Operations autogeneration; the files stay where their inbound links and TechDocs expect them.
  • (b) move them to docs/historical/ and autogenerate; cleaner tree, but 473 links to re-check and TechDocs nav edits.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ5. Base URL.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: /repo-guardian on donaldgifford.github.io, today's URL; no DNS, existing links keep working.
  • (b) a custom domain; needs DNS the project does not own today, and every published link changes.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ6. The link rewrite.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: an in-repo remark plugin (~80 lines, unit tested) handling the .md → route mapping, README/index rules and out-of-tree links; the rules are ours and the third-party options each cover a subset.
  • (b) starlight-auto-links/rehype-astro-relative-markdown-links; less code to own, but README mapping and out-of-tree links still need a custom step.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ7. Theme approach.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: Starlight's CSS custom properties only, set from the DESIGN-0036 palette and fonts; no component overrides, so Starlight upgrades stay trivial.
  • (b) override header/sidebar components to match the UI shell; closer match, more to maintain on every Starlight release.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Finish the supply-chain work DESIGN-0038 Part D ranked below tier 1: pin every action to a commit, scan the images and the chart, lint and score the workflows, take secrets out of shell text and verify what we sign, then sign the binaries with cosign and SLSA generic provenance, add a NetworkPolicy, and revisit required signatures. Each phase is a pull request that leaves the pipeline publishing exactly as before.

Workflow linting, security auditing and action pinning are one tool, jdx/jactionlint (reviewed 2026-10-25): it carries actionlint's checks (correctness profile), a rule per zizmor audit under the same IDs (default profile = zizmor's regular persona), and unpinned-uses whose --online --fix pins tags to commits with a version comment, so pinact, actionlint and zizmor are not adopted separately.

Implements: DESIGN-0038 Part D tiers 2 and 3 (D4), D9, OQ20. Follows IMPL-0034 Phase 5 (tier 1).

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• SHA pinning of all external action references (jactionlint --online --fix) with Renovate keeping them current; the slsa-github-generator tag exception (tier 1) as an unpinned-uses policy.
  • Trivy image and config scans (SARIF to code scanning), bun audit and a UI licence check, jactionlint (actionlint + zizmor coverage, SARIF), dependency-review, OpenSSF Scorecard.
  • Verify-after-sign on every publish; registry credentials through env:/stdin only; secret-scanning settings review.
  • Cosign keyless signatures and SLSA generic provenance for the goreleaser archives; GPG retirement plan.
  • A chart NetworkPolicy template (default off), harden-runner in audit mode, Renovate lockFileMaintenance, the required-signatures decision.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Tier 1 (IMPL-0034 Phase 5): SBOMs, CodeQL, rulesets, @latest pins, pod security context, verifying-releases.md, SECURITY.md.
  • Changing the builders (goreleaser, bake) or the registries.
  • Runtime code. A finding from a scanner that needs a Go or TypeScript fix is filed as an issue and fixed on its own.

docs.title: Pre-implementation audit
docs.text:
Verified 2026-10-25 (DESIGN-0038 § Background, D4):

  • 6 of 111 external action references are SHA-pinned (the sigstore/cosign-installer uses with a # v4.1.2 comment); the rest are tags. Renovate's shared presets set pinDigests for github-actions but nothing has been pinned because the manager only pins references it has already seen pinned once (pinDigests applies on update, not retroactively).
  • trivy and syft are in mise.toml at latest (IMPL-0034 5.6 pins them) and unused by any workflow; cosign likewise local-only except through cosign-installer.
  • No actionlint, zizmor, dependency-review-action or Scorecard workflow; .github/actionlint.yml exists (self-hosted labels []) but nothing runs it.
  • jdx/jactionlint v2.3.0 (pushed 2026-10-25, 285 stars; a fork of actionlint by mise's author): reads actionlint's config; one rule per zizmor 1.30.1 audit with the same IDs and # zizmor: ignore[...] comments honoured; profiles correctness (actionlint + bug detectors), default (+ security and policy: unpinned-uses, missing-permissions, missing-timeout, concurrency-limits, artipacked, template-injection), pedantic; --baseline-write/ --baseline for gradual adoption; --fix (safe) and --fix=unsafe; --online adds impostor-commit, known-vulnerable-actions, ref-version-mismatch, archived-uses, repojacking, and makes unpinned-uses fixable (tag → commit + # vX.Y.Z comment, most specific tag, annotated tags followed, branches and unknown tags left alone); checks dependabot.yml too; installs through mise with mise.lock checksum + provenance verification; the jdx/jactionlint action uploads SARIF with advanced-security: true; shellcheck is used when on PATH (present on ubuntu-24.04). The unpinned-uses rule takes zizmor-style policies, which is where the slsa-github-generator ref-pin exception goes. Risk: a young fork; the three-tool fallback is noted under Dependencies.
  • ghcr.yml signs with cosign sign --yes and never runs cosign verify after; helm registry login takes --password-stdin in ecr.yml (piped from aws ecr get-login-password) and the GHCR login reads secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN through docker/login-action, so the remaining inlined secret is ecr.yml:73's shell variable assignment and the ${{ secrets.ECR_REGION }} interpolations in run: blocks.
  • Repository security settings: Dependabot security updates enabled; secret scanning enabled with push protection; non-provider patterns and validity checks disabled.
  • .goreleaser.yml signs checksums.txt with GPG only; no binary provenance. slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator ships a generator_generic_slsa3.yml reusable workflow that takes a base64-subjects input (sha256sum of the artefacts) and uploads multiple.intoto.jsonl to the release.
  • The chart has no NetworkPolicy template; the role Deployments reach GitHub, Temporal, Postgres and the OIDC issuer (api) and are reached by ingress (ingest webhook, api, ui) and Prometheus (/metrics).
  • release.yml runs bump-version on ubuntu-latest; no step-security/harden-runner anywhere.

docs.title: How the phases are ordered
docs.text: Phase 1 first because every later workflow edit is then written against pinned references and Renovate maintains them. Phases 2 and 3 add scanners and are independent; both report before they gate. Phase 4 touches the publish workflows and must land before Phase 5 adds another signing step there. Phase 5 is the tier-3 signing change. Phase 6 collects the remaining tier-3 items, each a small pull request.

docs.title: Implementation Phases
docs.text: Each phase builds on the previous one. A phase is complete when all its tasks are checked off and its success criteria are met.

docs.title: Phase 1: Action pinning
docs.text: DESIGN-0038 D4 tier 2 (pinning); IMPL-0036 OQ1.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 1.1 Pin once. jactionlint added to mise.toml (exact version, # renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=jdx/jactionlint) and mise lock run so mise.lock records its checksum. .github/jactionlint.yaml created with rules.unpinned-uses.policies mapping slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator to ref-pin (the CLAUDE.md reason in a comment) and .github/actionlint.yml folded into it. Then jactionlint --online --select unpinned-uses --diff reviewed and --fix applied (OQ1): every tag becomes owner/repo@<sha> # vX.Y.Z. Review the diff: the six existing pins unchanged; the SLSA generator references left at @v2.1.0; reusable-workflow uses: of our own files (./.github/workflows/ghcr.yml) untouched; anything jactionlint left with online-required/needs-judgment listed on this task and pinned by hand (gh api repos/<o>/<r>/git/ref/tags/<tag>).
  • [ ] 1.2 Renovate. Confirm the shared preset's github-actions pinDigests: true and helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests (renovate.json5 extends github>donaldgifford/renovate-config:ci; read the preset) will keep the # vX.Y.Z comment updated; add "extends": ["helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver"] if the comment form is not already configured. The IMPL-0034 5.7 exception for the SLSA generator is in place.
  • [ ] 1.3 Verify the pipeline. Run ghcr.yml by workflow_dispatch with dry_run=true for the current tag; every job runs on the pinned actions. The next Renovate run proposes digest updates with the version comment (check #213's dashboard).
  • [ ] 1.4 Guard. make lint-actions runs jactionlint --profile correctness plus --select unpinned-uses (offline; both exit 1 on a finding) until Phase 3 widens it to the default profile; Phase 3's workflow job runs the same target in CI so a new uses: foo/bar@v1 fails the pull request.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• grep -rhoE 'uses: [^./][^@]+@[^ ]+' .github | grep -vE '@[0-9a-f]{40}' returns only the slsa-github-generator references, and jactionlint --select unpinned-uses exits 0.
  • A dispatched publish dry run is green on the pinned tree.
  • Renovate's next digest PR carries # vX.Y.Z comments.

docs.title: Phase 2: Image, config and dependency scanning
docs.text: DESIGN-0038 D4 tier 2 (scanning); IMPL-0036 OQ2, OQ4, OQ5.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 2.1 Trivy image scan. security.yml: a trivy-image job that builds the release and ui-release bake targets locally (no push, load: true, single platform) and runs aquasecurity/trivy-action (pinned) with format: sarif, severity: HIGH,CRITICAL, ignore-unfixed: true, uploading to code scanning under category trivy-image-<target>. Per OQ2 the job reports for two weeks (exit-code: 0) and then flips to exit-code: 1 in a follow-up commit noted on this task.
  • [ ] 2.2 Trivy config scan. The same job runs trivy config over charts/repo-guardian (helm template output with default values and ci-values.yaml) and Dockerfile/ui/Dockerfile, SARIF category trivy-config; the IMPL-0034 5.8 hardening should leave it clean, and any remaining finding is either fixed or .trivyignored with a reason line.
  • [ ] 2.3 bun audit. ci.yml ui job gains bun audit --audit-level=high after install (reports to the log; OQ2's window applies, then fails on high); site/ gets the same in the docs job once IMPL-0035 lands.
  • [ ] 2.4 UI licences. license-check.yml gains a ui job running bunx license-checker-rseidelsohn --production --onlyAllow "<allowlist>" (OQ5) over ui/; the allowlist matches the Go job's (MIT;Apache-2.0;BSD-2-Clause;BSD-3-Clause;ISC;0BSD;MPL-2.0) plus CC0-1.0/Unlicense; the first run's exceptions are recorded in ui/.license-allowlist.json with a reason each.
  • [ ] 2.5 Dependency review. .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml on pull_request: actions/dependency-review-action (pinned) with fail-on-severity: high, deny-licenses mirroring the allowlists' complement (OQ4), comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure; required via ci-ok's sibling list (IMPL-0034 5.4) once it has run green on three pull requests.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• Code scanning shows CodeQL, govulncheck, trivy-image-release, trivy-image-ui-release and trivy-config tools with results from main.
  • A pull request adding a dependency with a GPL licence or a known high-severity advisory is blocked by dependency-review.
  • bun audit and the UI licence check run on every UI pull request; after OQ2's window both fail on a high finding.

docs.title: Phase 3: Workflow linting and Scorecard
docs.text: DESIGN-0038 D4 tier 2 (workflow hygiene); IMPL-0036 OQ3, OQ6. One linter, jactionlint, in place of actionlint + zizmor + pinact.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 3.1 Correctness first. jactionlint --profile correctness (actionlint's checks + shellcheck on run: blocks, shellcheck pinned in mise.toml for laptops) over .github/; fix every finding (these are mistakes, not debt). make lint-actions becomes jactionlint at the default profile with --baseline (3.2); ci.yml gets a workflows job on the existing workflows paths filter: jdx/mise-action (jactionlint from mise.lock), make lint-actions, and jactionlint --format sarif uploaded with github/codeql-action/upload-sarif (tool jactionlint) so findings land in code scanning beside CodeQL and trivy.
  • [ ] 3.2 Default profile. Run jactionlint (the default profile = zizmor's regular persona, OQ3) and triage: template-injection findings take the safe --fix (the expression moves to env:, the CLAUDE.md bake-metadata rule generalised) and the needs-judgment ones are edited by hand; missing-permissions/ excessive-permissions are covered by IMPL-0034 5.11's job-level blocks; artipacked takes the safe fix (persist-credentials: false) on every actions/checkout that does not push (every one but the changelog-update and bump-version checkouts); missing-timeout gets rules.missing-timeout.default-minutes: 30 in .github/jactionlint.yaml and the fix applied; concurrency-limits is satisfied by IMPL-0034 5.11 on the publish workflows and added to ci.yml (cancel-in-progress: true on pull requests). What is left goes into jactionlint --baseline-write so the build fails only on new findings, and the baseline file is burned down to empty within this phase (list the entries on this task).
  • [ ] 3.3 Online checks, scheduled. A weekly jactionlint --online run in the workflows job (schedule trigger, JACTIONLINT_ONLINE with GITHUB_TOKEN, contents: read) for impostor-commit, known-vulnerable-actions, ref-version-mismatch, archived-uses, repojacking; findings annotate the run and upload as SARIF. Not on pull requests (network, rate limits).
  • [ ] 3.4 Scorecard. .github/workflows/scorecard.yml: ossf/scorecard-action (pinned) on push to main and weekly, with publish_results: true (OQ6), SARIF to code scanning. Record the first score and the per-check breakdown on this task; the README gets the badge. Checks expected to lag: Branch-Protection (no required reviews; single maintainer), Signed-Releases (until Phase 5), Token-Permissions (fixed by 5.11 + 3.2), Pinned-Dependencies (Dockerfiles: pin apk/apt packages or mark them).
  • [ ] 3.5 Dockerfile pins. For Pinned-Dependencies: the Go Dockerfile and ui/Dockerfile FROM lines pinned to digests with a # renovate: comment (Renovate's docker manager updates them); any package installs pinned or removed.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• make lint-actions (jactionlint, default profile, empty baseline) passes locally and in the workflows CI job; introducing uses: actions/checkout@v4 or run: echo ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} fails it (verified once each).
  • Code scanning shows the jactionlint tool; the weekly online run reports no impostor-commit or known-vulnerable-actions.
  • Scorecard publishes a result for main; Token-Permissions and Pinned-Dependencies are at 10 after 3.2–3.5.
  • Every actions/checkout outside the two pushing workflows has persist-credentials: false.

docs.title: Phase 4: Publish-path hygiene
docs.text: DESIGN-0038 D4 tier 2 (verify-after-sign, secrets via env).

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 4.1 Verify after sign. In ghcr.yml and ecr.yml, directly after each cosign sign: cosign verify --certificate-identity "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/.github/workflows/<file>@${GITHUB_REF}" --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com <ref@digest> for the image, the UI image and the chart; after each SLSA job, slsa-verifier verify-image <ref@digest> --source-uri github.com/donaldgifford/repo-guardian --source-tag <tag> in a verify job that needs both the sign and SLSA jobs. The published artefact is unchanged; a verify failure fails the run loudly, which is what the v1.8.2/v1.11.0 post-mortems lacked.
  • [ ] 4.2 Secrets through env. Every run: block that interpolates ${{ secrets.* }} or a token output moves it to env: and reads the variable (ecr.yml token step, helm registry login password via --password-stdin <<< "$TOKEN", any gh call); jactionlint's template-injection and shellcheck confirm none remain. The ::add-mask:: on the ECR token stays.
  • [ ] 4.3 Secret scanning settings. deferred - human required: enable secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns and secret_scanning_validity_checks (gh api -X PATCH repos/... -f 'security_and_analysis[secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns][status]=enabled' ...); push protection is already on. Record the result.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
• [ ] 6.1 NetworkPolicy. templates/networkpolicy.yaml behind networkPolicy.enabled (default false, OQ8): one policy per role. Ingress: ingest from networkPolicy.ingress.webhookFrom (namespace/ pod selectors; empty = any), api and ui from ingress.apiFrom, every role's /metrics port from networkPolicy.ingress.metricsFrom (default the monitoring namespace selector); the baked Postgres and Valkey StatefulSets only from the roles. Egress: DNS; egress.github (TCP 443, CIDR list or 0.0.0.0/0 default with a comment); Temporal (temporal.address host:port → a namespaceSelector/podSelector under egress.temporal or a CIDR); Postgres (baked: pod selector; cnpg: the cluster's pods; external: egress.postgres CIDR); the OIDC issuer for api/ui (egress.oidc). helm-unittest renders each role's policy with the selectors; ci-values.yaml enables it so helm-test proves the pods still come up under kind (which enforces nothing, so also a kubectl exec curl smoke in the helm-test job is not attempted; the policy's correctness is reviewed, and the homelab (Cilium) is the enforcement test, deferred - human required).
  • [ ] 6.2 harden-runner. step-security/harden-runner (pinned) as the first step of every job in release.yml, ghcr.yml, ecr.yml, prerelease.yml with egress-policy: audit (OQ9); after two releases, read the reported endpoints and switch the publish jobs to block with the allowed-endpoints list in a follow-up noted here.
  • [ ] 6.3 Lock-file maintenance. renovate.json5 lockFileMaintenance: {enabled: true, schedule: ["before 6am on monday"]} so go.sum, ui/bun.lock and site/bun.lock are refreshed weekly even when no direct dependency moved.
  • [ ] 6.4 Required signatures. Decide per OQ10 after Phase 1–5: if Renovate is configured for platformCommit: enabled (GitHub App-signed commits) and Dependabot's commits are verified, add required_signatures to the main ruleset via gh api (deferred - human required); otherwise record the reason to wait in DESIGN-0038 D4 and close the item.
  • [ ] 6.5 Close out. Scorecard re-read and recorded; SECURITY.md's controls list final; IMPL-0036 → Completed; DESIGN-0038 → Implemented once IMPL-0033/0034/0035 are also complete.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
OQ1. How to get to SHA-pinned actions.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: pinact run once, Renovate maintains; one reviewable diff pins all 105 remaining references with version comments, and Renovate's digest updates keep them current with the comment form.
  • (b) let Renovate pin them over time; it only pins references it is updating, so most would stay unpinned for months.
  • (c) Dependabot github-actions version updates re-enabled with pinning; Dependabot pins on its first update too, and we just made it security-only to stop the duplicate PRs.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a). Tool: jactionlint --online --fix on unpinned-uses in place of pinact run; same shape, one diff, Renovate maintains.

OQ2. When the trivy image scan and bun audit start failing the run.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: report-only for two weeks, then fail on HIGH/CRITICAL with --ignore-unfixed; the window shows the baseline and fixes without blocking the first merges, and unfixed upstream CVEs in distroless cannot be acted on anyway.
  • (b) fail from the first run; cleaner signal, but the first green requires every current finding resolved or ignored in one PR.
  • (c) report-only indefinitely; it is then a dashboard nobody reads.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ3. The zizmor persona.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: regular (the default); auditor adds low-confidence findings (every uses: without a pin even when the pin is ours, unpinned runs-on) that pinact and Phase 1 already cover.
  • (b) auditor from the start, with findings ignored inline; more noise, marginal gain.
  • (c) pedantic; not for CI gating.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a). In jactionlint terms: the default profile, which is zizmor's regular persona; pedantic covers auditor/pedantic.

OQ4. dependency-review failure threshold and licences.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: fail-on-severity: high and deny-licenses for the copyleft set (GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0, LGPL-*, SSPL-1.0, EUPL-*); matches license-check.yml's allowlist by complement and blocks the two things a dependency bump can bring in that a scanner on main would only report after the merge.
  • (b) fail-on-severity: moderate; stricter, more Renovate PRs blocked by advisories with no fix.
  • (c) severity only, no licence rule; licences then rely on the post-merge license-check.yml.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ5. The UI licence tool.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: license-checker-rseidelsohn (the maintained fork of license-checker, MIT) run with bunx at a pinned version; reads node_modules, supports --onlyAllow, JSON output for the exceptions file.
  • (b) licensee or fossa SaaS; heavier, needs tokens.
  • (c) bun pm licenses if bun ships it by then; check at implementation time and prefer it if it exists with an allowlist.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ6. Scorecard publishing.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: publish_results: true and the README badge; public repository, public score, and the badge is the point.
  • (b) run privately (SARIF only); keeps a low early score off the README, but there is nothing to hide and the score lifts quickly.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ7. GPG retirement timing.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: keep GPG for one release after cosign ships, so one release carries both and the verification page can show both passing; then remove it (5.6).
  • (b) remove GPG in the same release cosign appears; cleaner, no overlap release for operators scripting gpg --verify.
  • (c) keep both indefinitely; two signing paths to maintain.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ8. NetworkPolicy shape.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: a chart template, default off, one policy per role, selectors from values with permissive egress defaults for GitHub (any 443) and explicit selectors for Temporal, Postgres, OIDC and metrics; operators turn it on where their CNI enforces.
  • (b) default on; breaks every install whose Temporal or Postgres is outside the selectors the defaults guess.
  • (c) ship an example in contrib/ only; nothing templated, nothing tested.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ9. harden-runner mode.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: audit on the publish workflows first, block on them after two releases with the observed endpoint list; the publish jobs are the ones with credentials, and audit shows what to allow before blocking something cosign or SLSA needs.
  • (b) block immediately with a guessed list; a missed Sigstore or registry endpoint breaks a release.
  • (c) audit on every workflow including CI; more reports, little extra protection where there are no secrets.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

OQ10. Required signatures on main.

  • (a) ✅ recommended: decide at Phase 6 with the evidence: enable only when Renovate (platformCommit) and Dependabot both produce verified commits and the maintainer's signing key is set up on every machine; otherwise record "not yet" in DESIGN-0038 D4 and revisit.
  • (b) enable now; unverified bot commits then block merges until each bot is reconfigured.
  • (c) never; signing is already policy by habit (git commit -S), but a ruleset is what makes it a control.
  • other:

Decision (2026-10-25): (a).

docs.title: INV 0001: Tailscale Funnel for Webhook Testing
docs.text:
Historical. The sidecar approach this investigation validated was later removed by INV-0016 / DESIGN-0023 / IMPL-0024 — ingress is operator-owned now; see docs/operations/ingress.md.

Status: Concluded Author: Donald Gifford Date: 2026-03-14

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Can we use Tailscale Funnel to expose the repo-guardian webhook endpoint running in Kubernetes so that GitHub can deliver webhooks to it? We will test on a local Talos k8s cluster first, with EKS as the eventual production target. A previous attempt failed for unknown reasons -- this investigation aims to identify and resolve those issues.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text:
Tailscale Funnel should work as a webhook ingress for the EKS-deployed app. The likely failure points from the previous attempt are:

  1. Funnel not enabled in the tailnet ACL policy.
  2. Port mismatch -- Funnel only supports ports 443, 8443, and 10000, while the app listens on 8080. The sidecar needs to proxy correctly.
  3. Tailscale serve config not routing traffic to the app container.
  4. Kubernetes networking between the sidecar and app containers.
  5. Auth key expiry or misconfiguration in the pod.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
repo-guardian runs in Kubernetes (local Talos cluster for dev/testing, EKS for production). GitHub needs a publicly reachable HTTPS endpoint to deliver webhooks. Currently we use ngrok for this, but the free tier generates a new URL on every restart, requiring a manual update of the GitHub App webhook URL each time.

Tailscale Funnel provides a stable *.ts.net URL that persists across pod restarts (assuming the same Tailscale node identity), which would eliminate this friction. We previously attempted Tailscale Funnel but it failed -- the reason was not documented.

Triggered by: DESIGN-0003: Tailscale Integration Research

docs.title: Phase 1: Verify Tailscale Funnel prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Check tailnet ACL policy allows Funnel ("nodeAttrs" with "funnel" cap).
  2. Confirm we have a reusable auth key or OAuth client credentials for the Tailscale node in k8s.
  3. Determine the Funnel hostname (e.g., repo-guardian.<tailnet>.ts.net).

docs.title: Phase 2: Sidecar container design for Kubernetes
docs.text:
1. Add a Tailscale sidecar container to the repo-guardian Deployment.
  2. Use the official tailscale/tailscale Docker image.
  3. Sidecar shares the pod network namespace (default in k8s -- all containers in a pod share localhost).
  4. Configure Tailscale serve to proxy Funnel HTTPS (port 443) to http://127.0.0.1:8080 (the app's webhook port).
  5. Sidecar needs:
  6. TS_AUTHKEY or OAuth credentials via a k8s Secret.
  7. TS_EXTRA_ARGS or serve config for Funnel setup.
  8. Writable state directory (emptyDir or PV for persistent identity).
  9. CAP_NET_ADMIN and /dev/net/tun (unless using userspace networking).

docs.title: Phase 3: Deploy and test on Talos cluster
docs.text:
1. Deploy the updated Deployment with the Tailscale sidecar to the local Talos cluster.
  2. Confirm the Funnel URL is reachable from the public internet.
  3. Update the GitHub App webhook URL to the Funnel *.ts.net URL.
  4. Trigger a webhook event (create a test repo or push to an existing one).
  5. Verify the webhook is received, HMAC-validated, and processed by the app.

docs.title: Phase 4: Persistence and reliability
docs.text:
1. Restart the pod -- confirm the Funnel URL remains stable.
  2. Verify auth key renewal or OAuth token refresh works across restarts.
  3. Confirm no webhook deliveries are lost during pod restarts.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Component Version / Value Tailscale 1.94.1 (local); TBD (sidecar image tag) Kubernetes Talos (local dev/test), EKS (production target) repo-guardian current main branch GitHub App dev app instance

docs.title: Funnel Constraints (from DESIGN-0003)
docs.text:
• Ports: Only 443, 8443, and 10000 are supported for Funnel.
  • HTTPS only: TLS termination is automatic (handled by Tailscale).
  • ACL policy: Funnel must be explicitly enabled in the tailnet ACL policy.
  • Auth keys: Regular keys expire after 90 days max. Use OAuth client credentials for long-lived deployments.

docs.title: Kubernetes Sidecar Considerations
docs.text:
• All containers in a pod share localhost, so the sidecar can reach the app on 127.0.0.1:8080 without any special networking.
  • Tailscale sidecar needs a writable directory for state. Options:
  • emptyDir -- simple but re-authenticates on every pod restart (new node identity each time).
  • PersistentVolume -- preserves node identity across restarts, keeps the same Funnel hostname.
  • If using emptyDir with Ephemeral: true, the node auto-removes from the tailnet on shutdown, but the Funnel URL remains stable as long as the same TS_HOSTNAME is used with a reusable auth key.
  • The Tailscale Kubernetes operator is another option but may be heavier than needed for a single-pod sidecar.

docs.title: ACL Policy
docs.text:
The tailnet ACL already had the required configuration:

  • tag:container defined in tagOwners with autogroup:admin as owner.
  • nodeAttrs grants funnel capability to tag:container.

No ACL changes were needed.

docs.title: Auth Key
docs.text: Generated a reusable, ephemeral auth key tagged with tag:container. The sidecar authenticates on pod start and auto-removes from the tailnet on shutdown. With TS_HOSTNAME=repo-guardian and a reusable key, the same Funnel hostname is reclaimed on restart.

docs.title: Sidecar Configuration
docs.text:
The working configuration uses:

  • Image: ghcr.io/tailscale/tailscale:latest
  • Userspace networking (TS_USERSPACE=true) -- avoids CAP_NET_ADMIN and /dev/net/tun. The sidecar runs as non-root (UID 1000).
  • Serve config via ConfigMap (TS_SERVE_CONFIG=/config/serve-config.json) -- proxies Funnel HTTPS 443 to http://127.0.0.1:8080.
  • State directory on emptyDir (TS_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/tailscale).

docs.title: Serve Config
docs.text:
{
  "TCP": { "443": { "HTTPS": true } },
  "Web": {
    "${TS_CERT_DOMAIN}:443": {
      "Handlers": { "/": { "Proxy": "http://127.0.0.1:8080" } }
    }
  },
  "AllowFunnel": { "${TS_CERT_DOMAIN}:443": true }
}

${TS_CERT_DOMAIN} is automatically expanded by Tailscale to the node's FQDN (e.g., repo-guardian.wyrm-ule.ts.net).

docs.title: Funnel URL
docs.text:
Public endpoint: https://repo-guardian.wyrm-ule.ts.net

  • TLS via Let's Encrypt (auto-provisioned by Tailscale).
  • HTTP/2 supported.
  • Health check (/healthz) returns 200.

docs.title: Webhook Delivery
docs.text:
Tested by adding a repo to the GitHub App installation:

  1. GitHub sent installation_repositories webhook to https://repo-guardian.wyrm-ule.ts.net/webhooks/github.
  2. Funnel proxied to the app on 127.0.0.1:8080.
  3. HMAC signature validated successfully.
  4. App processed the event, checked the repo for missing files, and logged the dry-run result.

Full end-to-end flow confirmed working: GitHub -> Tailscale Funnel -> k8s pod -> repo-guardian webhook handler -> checker engine.

docs.title: Previous Failure (Likely Cause)
docs.text:
While the exact previous failure was not documented, the most likely cause was one of:

  • Funnel not enabled in the ACL policy (it requires explicit nodeAttrs).
  • Not using TS_SERVE_CONFIG with a proper serve config JSON (Funnel won't activate without AllowFunnel in the serve config).
  • Missing userspace mode causing permission issues without CAP_NET_ADMIN.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: Answer: Yes. Tailscale Funnel works as a webhook tunnel for repo-guardian running in Kubernetes. The sidecar approach requires no code changes, provides a stable public URL with auto TLS, and runs without elevated privileges using userspace networking.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
1. Use the deploy/overlays/tailscale/ overlay for dev/test deployments that need GitHub webhook delivery.
  2. Keep ngrok in compose.yaml as a fallback for quick local testing outside of k8s.
  3. For production (EKS), use a proper ALB Ingress instead of Funnel. Funnel is a dev/test solution -- it routes through Tailscale's DERP relays which adds latency and is not designed for production webhook traffic.
  4. Auth key rotation: The current reusable key expires after 90 days. Consider switching to OAuth client credentials for longer-lived deployments, or automate key rotation.
  5. Webhook IP allowlisting: This investigation did not cover restricting access to the Funnel endpoint. Tailscale Funnel exposes the webhook URL to the public internet with no IP-level filtering. While HMAC validation rejects unauthorized payloads, an IP allowlist middleware would add defense-in-depth. See DESIGN-0004: GitHub Webhook IP Allowlist Middleware for the proposed solution.
